meta.orig_title: Gödel, Escher, Bach: an Eternal Golden Braid
meta.blurb_uz: Qanday qilib jonsiz moddadan «men» paydo bo'ladi? Duglas Hofstadter bu savolga matematik Kurt Gödel, rassom M. C. Escher va kompozitor J. S. Bax orqali yaqinlashadi: formal tizimlar va MU jumbog'i, rekursiya va fugalar, imkonsiz rasmlar, Gödelning to'liqsizlik teoremasi, DNK, miya, chumoli koloniyasi va sun'iy intellekt — hammasi bitta g'oya atrofida o'raladi: «g'alati halqa».
meta.why_uz: 1980-yilda Pulitser mukofotini olgan, butun avlod olimlari va dasturchilarini ilhomlantirgan kitob. Bu WordDrop o'quv nashrida kitobning har bir bobi va g'oyasi tartib bilan, tushunarli ingliz tilida to'liq ochib berilgan, har bobda Axilles va Toshbaqaning WordDrop yozgan kichik sahnachasi bor. Mantiq, matematika, informatika va ong haqidagi ilmiy ingliz tilini o'rganish uchun noyob material.
meta.author_uz: Duglas R. Hofstadter (1945-yilda tug'ilgan) — amerikalik kognitiv olim, Indiana universiteti professori, Nobel mukofoti sovrindori fizik Robert Hofstadterning o'g'li. «Gödel, Escher, Bach» (1979) — uning birinchi kitobi; keyin «Men — g'alati halqa» (2007), «Metamagik mavzular» va boshqa kitoblar yozgan.
meta.edition_uz: Bu — WordDrop o'quv nashri. «Gödel, Escher, Bach» mualliflik huquqi bilan himoyalangan (muallif hayot), shuning uchun bu yerda Hofstadterning asl matni va dialoglari emas, balki WordDrop yozgan to'liq sharh-bayon berilgan: kitobning har bir bobi va dialogi tartib bilan ochib beriladi. Har bobdagi «Scene» deb belgilangan Axilles va Toshbaqa sahnachalari — WordDrop tomonidan yozilgan, aniqlik uchun mo'ljallangan original qisqa dialoglar (Axilles va Toshbaqa qiyofalari Zenon va Lyuis Kerrolga borib taqaladi). Asl kitobni (Basic Books, 1979; 20 yillik nashri 1999) kitob do'konidan yoki kutubxonadan o'qishingiz mumkin. Muqova — Basic Books nashri dizayni.
meta.source_uz: WordDrop o'quv nashri; asl asar: Douglas R. Hofstadter, Gödel, Escher, Bach: an Eternal Golden Braid (Basic Books, 1979).

chapters.title: A book about how an 'I' can come from nothing
chapters.title_uz: Hech narsadan qanday qilib «men» paydo bo'lishi haqidagi kitob

paras.en: Gödel, Escher, Bach: an Eternal Golden Braid was published in 1979 by Douglas R. Hofstadter, a young American scientist who was then in his early thirties. It won the Pulitzer Prize for general nonfiction in 1980 and quickly became a cult book among mathematicians, programmers, philosophers and curious readers. Many people bought it because of its strange title and its beautiful cover, began reading, and found themselves in a long, playful journey through logic, music, art, biology and computers.
paras.uz: «Gödel, Escher, Bach: abadiy oltin o'rim» 1979-yilda o'sha paytda o'ttiz yoshlardagi yosh amerikalik olim Duglas R. Hofstadter tomonidan nashr etilgan. U 1980-yilda badiiy bo'lmagan adabiyot bo'yicha Pulitser mukofotini oldi va tezda matematiklar, dasturchilar, faylasuflar va qiziquvchan o'quvchilar orasida kult kitobga aylandi. Ko'p odamlar uni g'alati nomi va chiroyli muqovasi uchun sotib olib, o'qishni boshlashgan va o'zlarini mantiq, musiqa, san'at, biologiya va kompyuterlar bo'ylab uzoq, o'ynoqi sayohatda topishgan.

paras.en: What is the book really about? On the surface it seems to be about three men who never met: Kurt Gödel, an Austrian logician who in 1931 proved one of the most surprising theorems in mathematics; M. C. Escher, a Dutch artist who drew impossible buildings and hands drawing each other; and Johann Sebastian Bach, the German composer of canons and fugues. But Hofstadter later explained that these three are only a way in. The deeper question is how a self, an 'I', can arise from parts that have no self at all.
paras.uz: Kitob aslida nima haqida? Yuzaki qaraganda u hech qachon uchrashmagan uch kishi haqidagidek ko'rinadi: 1931-yilda matematikadagi eng hayratlanarli teoremalardan birini isbotlagan avstriyalik mantiqchi Kurt Gödel; imkonsiz binolar va bir-birini chizayotgan qo'llarni tasvirlagan gollandiyalik rassom M. C. Escher; va kanon va fugalar muallifi nemis kompozitori Iogann Sebastyan Bax. Lekin Hofstadter keyinroq bu uchtasi faqat kirish yo'li ekanini tushuntirgan. Chuqurroq savol — qanday qilib o'zida «men» bo'lmagan qismlardan «men» paydo bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: Think about it for a moment. Your brain is made of cells; the cells are made of molecules; the molecules are made of atoms. None of these atoms knows anything, wants anything or feels anything. And yet, somewhere in that huge pattern of activity, there is you — someone who reads this sentence, remembers yesterday and worries about tomorrow. How is that possible? Hofstadter's answer, developed over hundreds of pages, is that the self is a special kind of pattern: a pattern that refers back to itself. He calls it a 'strange loop'.
paras.uz: Bir lahza o'ylab ko'ring. Miyangiz hujayralardan iborat; hujayralar molekulalardan; molekulalar atomlardan. Bu atomlarning hech biri hech narsani bilmaydi, hech narsani istamaydi va hech narsani his qilmaydi. Shunga qaramay, o'sha ulkan faoliyat naqshining qayeridadir siz borsiz — bu jumlani o'qiyotgan, kechani eslaydigan va ertaga haqida qayg'uradigan kimsa. Bu qanday mumkin? Hofstadterning yuzlab sahifalar davomida ishlab chiqilgan javobi shuki, «men» — alohida turdagi naqsh: o'ziga qaytib ishora qiladigan naqsh. U buni «g'alati halqa» (strange loop) deb ataydi.

paras.en: A strange loop, in Hofstadter's sense, happens when you move upwards or downwards through the levels of some system and find yourself, unexpectedly, back where you started. Escher's staircase that climbs forever and returns to its beginning is a picture of it. Bach's canon that modulates up through all the keys and ends where it began is a musical version. And Gödel's sentence, a statement of arithmetic that indirectly says 'I am not provable', is the mathematical version. The book braids these three examples together — hence the 'golden braid' of the title.
paras.uz: Hofstadter ma'nosidagi g'alati halqa — biror tizimning darajalari bo'ylab yuqoriga yoki pastga harakatlanib, kutilmaganda o'zingizni boshlagan joyingizda topganingizda sodir bo'ladi. Escherning abadiy ko'tarilib, o'z boshlanishiga qaytadigan zinapoyasi — uning tasviri. Baxning barcha tonalliklar bo'ylab yuqoriga ko'tarilib, boshlangan joyida tugaydigan kanoni — musiqiy varianti. Gödel jumlasi esa — bilvosita «Meni isbotlab bo'lmaydi» deydigan arifmetika gapi — matematik varianti. Kitob bu uch misolni bir-biriga o'raydi — sarlavhadagi «oltin o'rim» shundan.

paras.en: Even the cover plays with this idea. It shows two wooden blocks hanging in a lit corner. Each block is carved so that, when light shines on it from three directions, its shadows form different letters: one block casts the shadows G, E and B; the other casts E, G and B. The same object looks like different things from different angles. This is a small lesson that runs through the whole book: meaning depends on the level and the point of view from which you look.
paras.uz: Hatto muqova ham bu g'oya bilan o'ynaydi. Unda yoritilgan burchakda osilib turgan ikkita yog'och blok tasvirlangan. Har bir blok shunday o'yilganki, unga uch tomondan yorug'lik tushganda, soyalari turli harflarni hosil qiladi: bir blok G, E va B soyalarini, ikkinchisi E, G va B soyalarini tashlaydi. Bir xil narsa turli burchaklardan turli narsalar bo'lib ko'rinadi. Bu butun kitob bo'ylab o'tadigan kichik saboq: ma'no qaysi daraja va qaysi nuqtai nazardan qarashingizga bog'liq.

paras.en: The structure of the book is unusual. It has twenty chapters, and before each chapter there is a dialogue — a short, often funny conversation, mostly between Achilles and the Tortoise. The dialogues are written like musical pieces: some are canons, some fugues, some inventions, and their form often imitates the idea of the chapter that follows. A dialogue presents an idea in a playful, intuitive way; the chapter then explains it seriously. The book itself is divided into two halves: Part I, 'GEB', and Part II, 'EGB'.
paras.uz: Kitobning tuzilishi g'ayrioddiy. Unda yigirma bob bor va har bir bobdan oldin dialog keladi — asosan Axilles va Toshbaqa o'rtasidagi qisqa, ko'pincha kulgili suhbat. Dialoglar musiqiy asarlar kabi yozilgan: ba'zilari kanon, ba'zilari fuga, ba'zilari invensiya va ularning shakli ko'pincha keyingi bobning g'oyasiga taqlid qiladi. Dialog g'oyani o'ynoqi, intuitiv tarzda taqdim etadi; bob esa uni jiddiy tushuntiradi. Kitobning o'zi ikki yarmiga bo'lingan: I qism «GEB» va II qism «EGB».

paras.en: Who are Achilles and the Tortoise? They come from one of the oldest puzzles in philosophy. The Greek thinker Zeno of Elea argued that swift Achilles could never overtake a slow tortoise that had a head start: by the time he reaches the place where the tortoise was, it has moved a little further, and so on forever. In 1895 Lewis Carroll, the author of Alice in Wonderland, wrote a short logical dialogue in which the same pair argue about the rules of reasoning. Hofstadter borrowed them and added new friends: a Crab, an Anteater, a Sloth and others.
paras.uz: Axilles va Toshbaqa kim? Ular falsafadagi eng qadimgi jumboqlardan biridan kelgan. Yunon mutafakkiri Eleyalik Zenon tez Axilles oldinda ketayotgan sekin toshbaqani hech qachon quvib o'ta olmasligini ta'kidlagan: u toshbaqa bo'lgan joyga yetganda, toshbaqa biroz oldinga siljigan bo'ladi va bu abadiy davom etadi. 1895-yilda «Alisa mo''jizalar mamlakatida» muallifi Lyuis Kerrol xuddi shu juftlik mulohaza qoidalari haqida bahslashadigan qisqa mantiqiy dialog yozgan. Hofstadter ularni olib, yangi do'stlar qo'shgan: Qisqichbaqa, Chumolixo'r, Yalqov (Lenivets) va boshqalar.

paras.en: A word about this edition. Gödel, Escher, Bach is protected by copyright, so WordDrop cannot reproduce Hofstadter's chapters or his dialogues. What you will read is a complete study edition: every part of the book is explained in order, in clear English, with an Uzbek translation, vocabulary, questions and notes. In each chapter you will also find a short 'Scene' — a little dialogue between Achilles and the Tortoise written by WordDrop, in the spirit of the book, to make the idea concrete. These scenes are ours, not Hofstadter's.
paras.uz: Bu nashr haqida bir so'z. «Gödel, Escher, Bach» mualliflik huquqi bilan himoyalangan, shuning uchun WordDrop Hofstadterning boblari va dialoglarini qayta chop eta olmaydi. Siz o'qiydigan narsa — to'liq o'quv nashri: kitobning har bir qismi tartib bilan, tushunarli ingliz tilida, o'zbekcha tarjimasi, lug'ati, savollari va izohlari bilan tushuntiriladi. Har bir bobda qisqa «Scene» — kitob ruhida WordDrop yozgan Axilles va Toshbaqa o'rtasidagi kichik dialog ham bor, g'oyani aniq qilish uchun. Bu sahnachalar bizniki, Hofstadterniki emas.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I have a confession. I tried to read a famous book about Gödel, Escher and Bach, and I got lost on page ten. Tortoise: Lost? Wonderful. Being lost is the first sign that a book is taking you somewhere new. Achilles: But I don't even know which of the three it is really about. Tortoise: Then let me tell you a secret. It is about none of them — and about the person who is reading it. Achilles: About me? Tortoise: About anything that can say 'me'. Come, let us start with a puzzle.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, bir narsani tan olishim kerak. Men Gödel, Escher va Bax haqidagi mashhur kitobni o'qishga urindim va o'ninchi sahifada adashib qoldim. Toshbaqa: Adashdingmi? Ajoyib. Adashish — kitob seni yangi joyga olib ketayotganining birinchi belgisi. Axilles: Lekin men u aslida uchtasidan qaysi biri haqida ekanini ham bilmayman. Toshbaqa: Unda senga bir sir aytay. U ularning hech biri haqida emas — va uni o'qiyotgan odam haqida. Axilles: Men haqimdami? Toshbaqa: «Men» deya oladigan har qanday narsa haqida. Qani, bir jumboqdan boshlaylik.

paras.en: How should you read this edition? Slowly, and with a pencil. Some chapters are light and full of stories; others, especially in the middle, are technical and ask you to follow formal rules step by step. Do not be afraid of the symbols: we will always explain what they mean in words. If something seems confusing, read the scene again, then the explanation. And remember Hofstadter's own playful rule, known as Hofstadter's Law: everything takes longer than you expect, even when you take this law into account.
paras.uz: Bu nashrni qanday o'qish kerak? Sekin va qo'lda qalam bilan. Ba'zi boblar yengil va hikoyalarga to'la; boshqalari, ayniqsa o'rtadagilari, texnik bo'lib, sizdan formal qoidalarga qadam-baqadam ergashishni talab qiladi. Belgilardan qo'rqmang: ular nimani anglatishini doimo so'zlar bilan tushuntiramiz. Agar biror narsa chalkash tuyulsa, sahnani yana o'qing, keyin tushuntirishni. Va Hofstadterning o'zining Hofstadter qonuni deb nomlangan o'ynoqi qoidasini eslang: hamma narsa kutganingizdan ko'proq vaqt oladi, hatto bu qonunni hisobga olganingizda ham.

chapters.recap_uz: Kirish bobi: kitob nima haqida, nega uch xil odam — mantiqchi Gödel, rassom Escher va kompozitor Bax — bir kitobda uchrashadi, uning g'alati tuzilishi (boblar va dialoglar navbatma-navbat keladi) va bu o'quv nashrini qanday o'qish kerak.
chapters.note_uz: Hofstadter kitobining asosiy savolini 20 yillik nashr so'zboshisida o'zi aniqlashtirgan: jonsiz unsurlardan qanday qilib jonli, o'zini anglaydigan mavjudot paydo bo'ladi? Har bir bobni o'qiyotganda shu savolni yodda tuting.

chapters.title: Introduction (I): Bach and the King's theme
chapters.title_uz: Kirish (I): Bax va qirol mavzusi

paras.en: Hofstadter's introduction is called 'A Musico-Logical Offering', and it opens with a true story. In May 1747, Johann Sebastian Bach, then sixty-two years old and famous as an organist and composer, travelled to Potsdam, where his son Carl Philipp Emanuel worked as a musician at the court of King Frederick II of Prussia, known as Frederick the Great. The king loved music, played the flute, and owned several new keyboard instruments called fortepianos. When he heard that 'old Bach' had arrived, he invited him to the palace at once.
paras.uz: Hofstadterning kirishi «Musiqiy-mantiqiy tortiq» deb ataladi va u haqiqiy voqea bilan ochiladi. 1747-yil may oyida o'sha paytda oltmish ikki yoshda bo'lgan, organchi va kompozitor sifatida mashhur Iogann Sebastyan Bax Potsdamga bordi; u yerda uning o'g'li Karl Filipp Emanuel Prussiya qiroli Fridrix II — Buyuk Fridrix saroyida musiqachi bo'lib ishlardi. Qirol musiqani sevardi, fleyta chalardi va fortepiano deb ataladigan bir nechta yangi klavishli cholg'ularga ega edi. «Keksa Bax» kelganini eshitib, u uni darhol saroyga taklif qildi.

paras.en: At the palace the king played a theme — a melody of his own, or one he presented as his own — and asked Bach to improvise a fugue on it. Bach sat down and improvised a three-voice fugue on the spot, to everyone's amazement. The king then asked for a fugue in six voices. That was too much even for Bach to improvise on an unfamiliar theme, and he promised to write one later. When he returned home to Leipzig, he composed a whole collection of pieces based on the king's theme and sent it to Frederick as a gift.
paras.uz: Saroyda qirol bir mavzu chaldi — o'zining kuyi yoki o'ziniki sifatida taqdim etgan kuy — va Baxdan uning asosida fuga improvizatsiya qilishni so'radi. Bax o'tirdi va hammani hayratda qoldirib, joyida uch ovozli fuga improvizatsiya qildi. Keyin qirol olti ovozli fuga so'radi. Notanish mavzu asosida improvizatsiya qilish hatto Bax uchun ham haddan tashqari og'ir edi va u buni keyinroq yozishga va'da berdi. Leyptsigga uyiga qaytgach, u qirol mavzusi asosida butun bir asarlar to'plamini yaratdi va uni Fridrixga sovg'a sifatida yubordi.

paras.en: This collection is called The Musical Offering. It contains two fugues called 'ricercars' — one in three voices and one in six voices, so Bach kept his promise — a trio sonata, and ten canons. Bach loved word games, and he added a Latin title whose first letters spell RICERCAR: the phrase means, roughly, 'At the king's command, the song and the remainder resolved with canonic art'. Hofstadter enjoys this little acrostic, because it is a first example of something that says one thing on the surface and another thing at a hidden level.
paras.uz: Bu to'plam «Musiqiy tortiq» deb ataladi. Unda «richerkar» deb ataladigan ikkita fuga — biri uch ovozli, biri olti ovozli, shunday qilib Bax va'dasini bajardi — trio-sonata va o'nta kanon bor. Bax so'z o'yinlarini yaxshi ko'rardi va bosh harflari RICERCAR so'zini hosil qiladigan lotincha sarlavha qo'shdi: bu ibora taxminan «Qirol buyrug'i bilan, kuy va qolgani kanonik san'at bilan hal qilindi» degan ma'noni beradi. Hofstadter bu kichik akrostixdan zavqlanadi, chunki bu yuzada bir narsani, yashirin darajada esa boshqa narsani aytadigan narsaning birinchi misoli.

paras.en: To follow the book, we need to understand what a canon is. In a canon, one voice plays a melody, and then a second voice enters a little later playing the same melody, then perhaps a third, so that the copies overlap and fit together into harmony. The simplest example is a round like 'Row, row, row your boat'. But Bach's canons are much more ingenious. The copy can enter at a different pitch; it can be played upside down (inversion), backwards (a 'crab canon'), or at a different speed (augmentation).
paras.uz: Kitobga ergashish uchun kanon nima ekanini tushunishimiz kerak. Kanonda bir ovoz kuy chaladi, keyin biroz kechroq ikkinchi ovoz kirib, xuddi shu kuyni chaladi, keyin balki uchinchisi, shunday qilib nusxalar bir-birining ustiga tushib, garmoniyaga birlashadi. Eng oddiy misol — «Row, row, row your boat» kabi navbatma-navbat kuylanadigan qo'shiq. Lekin Baxning kanonlari ancha zukkoroq. Nusxa boshqa balandlikda kirishi mumkin; uni teskari aylantirib (inversiya), oxiridan boshiga qarab («qisqichbaqa kanoni») yoki boshqa tezlikda (augmentatsiya) chalish mumkin.

paras.en: What makes this interesting for Hofstadter is that in a good canon, the melody and its transformed copies must fit together perfectly. A single line of music has to be written so that it harmonises with distorted versions of itself. This is a deep idea: a structure that 'contains' information about how it relates to copies of itself. Later in the book we will meet the same idea in logic, where a statement contains information about itself, and in biology, where DNA contains the instructions for copying DNA.
paras.uz: Hofstadter uchun buni qiziq qiladigan narsa shuki, yaxshi kanonda kuy va uning o'zgartirilgan nusxalari bir-biriga mukammal mos kelishi kerak. Bitta musiqa satri o'zining buzilgan versiyalari bilan uyg'un bo'ladigan qilib yozilishi kerak. Bu chuqur g'oya: o'zining nusxalari bilan qanday bog'lanishi haqidagi ma'lumotni «o'z ichiga olgan» tuzilma. Kitobning keyingi qismida xuddi shu g'oyani mantiqda — gap o'zi haqidagi ma'lumotni o'z ichiga oladi — va biologiyada — DNK DNKni nusxalash ko'rsatmalarini o'z ichiga oladi — uchratamiz.

paras.en: A fugue is like a canon, but freer. It begins with a single voice stating a theme, called the subject. Then a second voice enters with the same theme, usually in a different key, while the first voice continues with new material. Then a third enters, and so on. After all the voices have entered, the composer is free to develop the theme in many ways: fragments, inversions, overlapping entries called 'stretto'. A fugue therefore combines strict rules with creative freedom — exactly the combination Hofstadter will later find in formal systems and in thinking.
paras.uz: Fuga kanonga o'xshaydi, lekin erkinroq. U mavzu (subyekt) deb ataladigan mavzuni bitta ovozning bayon qilishi bilan boshlanadi. Keyin ikkinchi ovoz odatda boshqa tonallikda xuddi shu mavzu bilan kiradi, birinchi ovoz esa yangi material bilan davom etadi. Keyin uchinchisi kiradi va hokazo. Barcha ovozlar kirgandan keyin kompozitor mavzuni ko'p yo'llar bilan rivojlantirishda erkin: parchalar, inversiyalar, «stretto» deb ataladigan bir-birining ustiga tushadigan kirishlar. Shuning uchun fuga qat'iy qoidalarni ijodiy erkinlik bilan birlashtiradi — Hofstadter keyinroq formal tizimlarda va fikrlashda aynan shu birikmani topadi.

paras.en: One canon in The Musical Offering is especially important for the book. It is known as the 'Endlessly Rising Canon' (Canon per Tonos). It begins in the key of C minor, but it is built so cleverly that at its end it has modulated — moved smoothly — into D minor. Played again, it moves on to E minor, and so on. After six such repetitions it arrives back in C minor, but an octave higher. The music seems to climb forever and yet always returns home. Bach wrote in the margin a little wish that the king's glory might rise in the same way.
paras.uz: «Musiqiy tortiq»dagi bir kanon kitob uchun ayniqsa muhim. U «Abadiy ko'tariluvchi kanon» (Canon per Tonos) nomi bilan mashhur. U do minor tonalligida boshlanadi, lekin shunchalik mohirona qurilganki, oxirida u re minorga modulyatsiya qilgan — ravon o'tgan bo'ladi. Yana chalinsa, u mi minorga o'tadi va hokazo. Oltita shunday takrordan keyin u yana do minorga, lekin bir oktava yuqoriroqda qaytib keladi. Musiqa abadiy ko'tarilayotgandek ko'rinadi, shunga qaramay doim uyga qaytadi. Bax hoshiyaga qirolning shon-sharafi ham xuddi shunday ko'tarilishini tilab, kichik bir tilak yozib qo'ygan.

paras.en: This is Hofstadter's first example of a strange loop. In each step you move upwards — to a higher key — and yet after a number of steps you are back at the start. The ear feels both things at once: endless rising and a closed circle. In theory you could make the octave jumps disappear by fading out the high notes and fading in the low ones, and the canon would truly rise forever. Psychologists later created exactly such an effect, known as the Shepard tone, which seems to climb endlessly without ever getting higher.
paras.uz: Bu Hofstadterning g'alati halqaga birinchi misoli. Har bir qadamda siz yuqoriga — balandroq tonallikka — harakatlanasiz, shunga qaramay bir necha qadamdan keyin boshlang'ich joyga qaytasiz. Quloq ikkala narsani bir vaqtda his qiladi: cheksiz ko'tarilishni va yopiq doirani. Nazariy jihatdan yuqori notalarni so'ndirib, pastkilarini kuchaytirib oktava sakrashlarini yo'q qilish mumkin va kanon haqiqatan abadiy ko'tarilardi. Keyinroq psixologlar aynan shunday effekt — Shepard tovushi deb ataladigan, hech qachon balandlashmasdan cheksiz ko'tarilayotgandek tuyuladigan tovushni yaratishdi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: I hummed Bach's rising canon all morning, and now my head is spinning. I climbed and climbed, and found myself in the same key. Tortoise: Did you go anywhere? Achilles: Yes! Up! And also — no. Tortoise: Then you have met your first strange loop. Each step felt like progress, and the sum of all the steps was a circle. Achilles: Is that a trick of the ear? Tortoise: It is a trick of levels. Keep it in your pocket; we will find the same trick in pictures, in numbers, and finally in your own head.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Ertalabdan beri Baxning ko'tariluvchi kanonini xirgoyi qildim, endi boshim aylanyapti. Ko'tarildim, ko'tarildim va o'zimni o'sha tonallikda topdim. Toshbaqa: Biror joyga bordingmi? Axilles: Ha! Yuqoriga! Va shu bilan birga — yo'q. Toshbaqa: Unda sen birinchi g'alati halqangni uchratding. Har bir qadam taraqqiyotdek tuyuldi, barcha qadamlar yig'indisi esa doira bo'ldi. Axilles: Bu quloqning hiylasimi? Toshbaqa: Bu darajalarning hiylasi. Uni cho'ntagingda saqla; xuddi shu hiylani rasmlarda, sonlarda va nihoyat o'z boshingda topamiz.

paras.en: Hofstadter adds one more observation about Bach. Bach's music is full of hidden structure: patterns of keys, numbers, even his own name spelled in notes (in German notation B-A-C-H is B-flat, A, C, B-natural, and Bach used it in his last great work, The Art of the Fugue). Bach seems to have enjoyed music that refers to its own construction. This taste for self-reference — art that comments on itself, a work that contains its own signature — is the thread that will lead us from music to logic.
paras.uz: Hofstadter Bax haqida yana bir kuzatuv qo'shadi. Bax musiqasi yashirin tuzilmalarga to'la: tonalliklar, sonlar naqshlari, hatto notalar bilan yozilgan o'z ismi (nemis yozuvida B-A-C-H — si-bemol, lya, do, si notalari va Bax uni o'zining so'nggi buyuk asari «Fuga san'ati»da ishlatgan). Bax o'z tuzilishiga ishora qiladigan musiqadan zavqlangan ko'rinadi. O'z-o'ziga ishoraga bo'lgan bu did — o'zi haqida izoh beradigan san'at, o'z imzosini o'z ichiga olgan asar — bizni musiqadan mantiqqa olib boradigan ipdir.

quiz.q: What did Frederick the Great ask Bach to do in 1747?
o: Improvise a fugue on the king's theme
quiz.why_uz: Qirol o'z mavzusi asosida fuga improvizatsiya qilishni so'radi.

quiz.q: What is special about the 'Endlessly Rising Canon'?
o: It rises through keys and returns to the starting key an octave higher
quiz.why_uz: U oltita modulyatsiyadan keyin do minorga bir oktava yuqorida qaytadi.

quiz.q: What is a 'crab canon'?
o: A canon in which a voice plays the melody backwards
quiz.why_uz: Qisqichbaqa kanonida kuy oxiridan boshiga qarab chalinadi.

chapters.recap_uz: Kitob kirishi Baxdan boshlanadi: 1747-yilda Potsdamda Buyuk Fridrix Baxga mavzu berib, undan fuga improvizatsiya qilishni so'raydi. Bax bu mavzu asosida «Musiqiy tortiq»ni yaratadi. Bob kanon va fuga nima ekanini, «abadiy ko'tariluvchi kanon»ni va unda yashiringan birinchi «g'alati halqa»ni tushuntiradi.
chapters.note_uz: Musiqa nazariyasini bilmasangiz ham qo'rqmang: kanon — bir kuyni turli vaqtlarda kirib keladigan ovozlar ijro etishi, fuga esa shuning murakkabroq, erkinroq shakli. Hofstadterga bu shakllar qoidalarga bo'ysunadigan, lekin go'zallik yaratadigan tizimlar sifatida kerak.

chapters.title: Introduction (II): Escher, Gödel and the machines
chapters.title_uz: Kirish (II): Escher, Gödel va mashinalar

paras.en: After Bach, Hofstadter turns to Maurits Cornelis Escher, the Dutch graphic artist. Escher's prints show worlds that cannot exist but look perfectly logical. In Waterfall, water flows down a channel, turns a mill wheel, and then — following the channel along what seems to be a level path — arrives back at the top of the waterfall. In Ascending and Descending, a line of monks walks endlessly up a staircase on the roof of a building, and the staircase forms a closed loop. Each part of these pictures is reasonable; only the whole is impossible.
paras.uz: Baxdan keyin Hofstadter gollandiyalik grafik rassom Maurits Kornelis Escherga o'tadi. Escherning gravyuralari mavjud bo'la olmaydigan, lekin mutlaqo mantiqiy ko'rinadigan dunyolarni ko'rsatadi. «Sharshara»da suv ariq bo'ylab pastga oqib, tegirmon g'ildiragini aylantiradi, keyin — tekis yo'ldek ko'rinadigan ariq bo'ylab — yana sharsharaning tepasiga qaytib keladi. «Ko'tarilish va tushish»da rohiblar qatori bino tomidagi zinapoyada cheksiz yuqoriga yuradi va zinapoya yopiq halqa hosil qiladi. Bu rasmlarning har bir qismi oqilona; faqat butuni imkonsiz.

paras.en: These are visual strange loops: you go 'up' at every step and end where you started, exactly as in Bach's rising canon. Another of Escher's prints, Drawing Hands, shows something even stranger: two hands, each holding a pencil, each drawing the other into existence. Which came first? Neither — each depends on the other. Hofstadter will return to this picture at the very end of the book, because it is a perfect image of what he calls a 'tangled hierarchy', where the level that creates and the level that is created loop into each other.
paras.uz: Bular vizual g'alati halqalar: har qadamda «yuqoriga» chiqasiz va xuddi Baxning ko'tariluvchi kanonidagidek, boshlagan joyingizda tugaysiz. Escherning yana bir gravyurasi — «Chizayotgan qo'llar» bundan ham g'alatiroq narsani ko'rsatadi: har biri qalam ushlagan ikki qo'l, har biri ikkinchisini borliqqa chizmoqda. Qaysi biri birinchi paydo bo'lgan? Hech biri — har biri ikkinchisiga bog'liq. Hofstadter bu rasmga kitobning eng oxirida qaytadi, chunki u u «chigal ierarxiya» deb atagan narsaning mukammal tasviri: yaratuvchi daraja va yaratilgan daraja bir-biriga halqa bo'lib o'raladi.

paras.en: Escher also loved pictures in which figure and background change places. In his Metamorphosis prints, black birds flying to the right gradually become the white spaces between white fish swimming to the left; lizards become hexagons, hexagons become a honeycomb. You cannot decide which shapes are 'the picture' and which are 'the space around it'. This interest in figure and ground will become a whole chapter later, applied to numbers: the set of theorems of a system and the set of non-theorems can be thought of as figure and ground.
paras.uz: Escher shuningdek shakl va fon o'rin almashadigan rasmlarni yaxshi ko'rardi. Uning «Metamorfoza» gravyuralarida o'ngga uchayotgan qora qushlar asta-sekin chapga suzayotgan oq baliqlar orasidagi oq bo'shliqlarga aylanadi; kaltakesaklar oltiburchaklarga, oltiburchaklar asalari uyasiga aylanadi. Qaysi shakllar «rasm» va qaysilari «uning atrofidagi bo'shliq» ekanini hal qila olmaysiz. Shakl va fonga bo'lgan bu qiziqish keyinroq sonlarga tatbiq etilgan butun bir bobga aylanadi: tizim teoremalari to'plami va teorema bo'lmaganlar to'plamini shakl va fon deb tasavvur qilish mumkin.

paras.en: Then comes Gödel, and Hofstadter starts with an ancient paradox. Epimenides, a man from Crete, is supposed to have said: 'All Cretans are liars.' If he is telling the truth, he is lying; if he is lying, perhaps he is telling the truth. The cleaner modern version is the liar sentence: 'This sentence is false.' If it is true, then it is false; if it is false, then it is true. The problem comes from self-reference: the sentence talks about itself, and in doing so creates a loop that cannot be resolved.
paras.uz: Keyin Gödel keladi va Hofstadter qadimiy paradoksdan boshlaydi. Kritlik Epimenid: «Barcha kritliklar yolg'onchi», degan ekan. Agar u rost gapirayotgan bo'lsa, u yolg'on gapiryapti; agar yolg'on gapirayotgan bo'lsa, balki rost gapirayotgandir. Zamonaviy toza varianti — yolg'onchi jumlasi: «Bu jumla yolg'on.» Agar u rost bo'lsa, demak u yolg'on; agar yolg'on bo'lsa, demak u rost. Muammo o'z-o'ziga ishoradan kelib chiqadi: jumla o'zi haqida gapiradi va shu bilan hal qilib bo'lmaydigan halqa yaratadi.

paras.en: At the beginning of the twentieth century, such paradoxes began to frighten mathematicians. Bertrand Russell discovered a version inside set theory: consider the set of all sets that do not contain themselves. Does it contain itself? Either answer leads to a contradiction. To protect mathematics, Russell and Alfred North Whitehead wrote Principia Mathematica (1910–1913), a huge attempt to build all of mathematics from logic using strict rules that would forbid such self-reference. Their method, the 'theory of types', separated objects into levels so that nothing could talk about itself.
paras.uz: XX asr boshida bunday paradokslar matematiklarni qo'rqita boshladi. Bertran Rassel to'plamlar nazariyasi ichida uning bir variantini kashf etdi: o'zini o'z ichiga olmaydigan barcha to'plamlar to'plamini ko'rib chiqing. U o'zini o'z ichiga oladimi? Ikkala javob ham ziddiyatga olib keladi. Matematikani himoya qilish uchun Rassel va Alfred Nort Uaytxed «Principia Mathematica»ni (1910–1913) yozishdi — butun matematikani bunday o'z-o'ziga ishorani taqiqlaydigan qat'iy qoidalar yordamida mantiqdan qurishga ulkan urinish. Ularning usuli — «tiplar nazariyasi» — narsalarni darajalarga ajratdi, toki hech narsa o'zi haqida gapira olmasin.

paras.en: The great German mathematician David Hilbert hoped for even more. He wanted a formal system that was both consistent (it never proves a contradiction) and complete (every true statement of mathematics can be proved in it), together with a proof that this was so. This was 'Hilbert's programme'. In 1931, a twenty-five-year-old logician in Vienna, Kurt Gödel, published a paper that showed this dream could not be fulfilled. Its title referred to formally undecidable propositions of Principia Mathematica and related systems.
paras.uz: Buyuk nemis matematigi David Hilbert bundan ham ko'proq narsaga umid qilardi. U ham ziddiyatsiz (hech qachon ziddiyatni isbotlamaydigan), ham to'liq (matematikaning har bir haqiqiy gapini unda isbotlash mumkin) bo'lgan formal tizimni, shuningdek bunday ekanining isbotini istardi. Bu «Hilbert dasturi» edi. 1931-yilda Venada yigirma besh yoshli mantiqchi Kurt Gödel bu orzu amalga oshmasligini ko'rsatgan maqola chop etdi. Uning sarlavhasi «Principia Mathematica» va unga o'xshash tizimlarning formal hal qilib bo'lmaydigan jumlalari haqida edi.

paras.en: Gödel's idea was brilliant. He found a way to make statements of arithmetic talk about arithmetic itself. Every symbol, formula and proof in the system could be assigned a code number — today we call it Gödel numbering. Then statements about formulas ('this formula can be proved') become statements about numbers ('this number has a certain property'). Using this trick, Gödel constructed a statement that, read on the level of numbers, is about numbers, but read on a higher level says, in effect: 'This statement cannot be proved in this system.'
paras.uz: Gödel g'oyasi ajoyib edi. U arifmetika gaplarini arifmetikaning o'zi haqida gapirtirishning yo'lini topdi. Tizimdagi har bir belgi, formula va isbotga kod raqam berish mumkin edi — bugun biz buni Gödel raqamlash deb ataymiz. Shunda formulalar haqidagi gaplar («bu formulani isbotlash mumkin») sonlar haqidagi gaplarga («bu son ma'lum xususiyatga ega») aylanadi. Shu hiyla yordamida Gödel shunday gap tuzdiki, u sonlar darajasida o'qilganda sonlar haqida, yuqoriroq darajada o'qilganda esa amalda: «Bu gapni bu tizimda isbotlab bo'lmaydi», deydi.

paras.en: Now think. If the system could prove this statement, it would prove something false, and the system would be unreliable. If the system is reliable, the statement cannot be proved — but then what it says is true. So there is a true statement of arithmetic that the system cannot prove. And this is not a weakness of one particular system: any sufficiently powerful system will have its own such statement. This is Gödel's Incompleteness Theorem. It is a strange loop in pure mathematics: the system, by describing itself, reveals its own limits.
paras.uz: Endi o'ylang. Agar tizim bu gapni isbotlay olganida, u yolg'on narsani isbotlagan bo'lardi va tizim ishonchsiz bo'lardi. Agar tizim ishonchli bo'lsa, gapni isbotlab bo'lmaydi — lekin unda u aytayotgan narsa haqiqat. Demak, tizim isbotlay olmaydigan haqiqiy arifmetik gap bor. Va bu biror alohida tizimning zaifligi emas: har qanday yetarlicha kuchli tizimda o'zining shunday gapi bo'ladi. Bu — Gödelning to'liqsizlik teoremasi. Bu sof matematikadagi g'alati halqa: tizim o'zini tasvirlash orqali o'zining chegaralarini ochib beradi.

paras.en: The introduction ends with machines. In the nineteenth century Charles Babbage designed an 'Analytical Engine', a mechanical computer that was never fully built. His friend Ada Lovelace wrote notes on it and remarked that the engine could only do what we know how to order it to do. A century later Alan Turing (1936) described an abstract universal machine and (1950) asked whether machines can think. Hofstadter connects this to Gödel: if a mind is a kind of formal system, does Gödel's theorem limit it? Or can a system, like a mind, 'jump out' of itself?
paras.uz: Kirish mashinalar bilan tugaydi. XIX asrda Charlz Bebbij hech qachon to'liq qurilmagan mexanik kompyuter — «Analitik mashina»ni loyihalashtirgan. Uning do'sti Ada Lavleys u haqda izohlar yozib, mashina faqat biz unga qanday buyurishni bilgan narsanigina qila oladi, deb qayd etgan. Bir asrdan keyin Alan Tyuring (1936) abstrakt universal mashinani tasvirlab berdi va (1950) mashinalar fikrlay oladimi, degan savolni qo'ydi. Hofstadter buni Gödel bilan bog'laydi: agar aql o'ziga xos formal tizim bo'lsa, Gödel teoremasi uni cheklaydimi? Yoki tizim, aql kabi, o'zidan «sakrab chiqa» oladimi?

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: So Escher draws, Bach composes and Gödel proves — the same thing? Tortoise: Not the same thing; the same shape. Watch: 'This sentence has five words.' Achilles: Let me count... yes, five. It's true! Tortoise: And it is about itself. Now: 'This sentence cannot be proved by Achilles.' Achilles: Easy, I'll prove it — oh. If I prove it, it's false. If I can't, it's true and I've failed. Tortoise: You see? A sentence that knows exactly where your limits are. Mathematicians were not amused either.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Demak, Escher chizadi, Bax bastalaydi, Gödel isbotlaydi — bir xil narsanimi? Toshbaqa: Bir xil narsani emas; bir xil shaklni. Qara: «Bu jumla beshta so'zdan iborat.» Axilles: Sanab ko'ray... ha, beshta. Bu rost! Toshbaqa: Va u o'zi haqida. Endi: «Bu jumlani Axilles isbotlay olmaydi.» Axilles: Oson, isbotlayman — oh. Agar isbotlasam, u yolg'on bo'ladi. Isbotlay olmasam, u rost va men yutqazdim. Toshbaqa: Ko'rdingmi? Chegaralaring qayerda ekanini aniq biladigan jumla. Matematiklar ham bundan xursand bo'lishmagan.

quiz.q: What does Escher's Drawing Hands show?
o: A fish turning into a bird
quiz.why_uz: Har biri ikkinchisini chizayotgan ikki qo'l — chigal ierarxiya tasviri.

quiz.q: What did Gödel show in 1931?
o: That any sufficiently powerful consistent system has true statements it cannot prove
quiz.why_uz: To'liqsizlik teoremasi: tizim isbotlay olmaydigan haqiqiy gaplar bor.

quiz.q: What is Gödel numbering?
o: Assigning code numbers to symbols, formulas and proofs
quiz.why_uz: Belgilar va formulalarga kod raqam berish — gaplar sonlar haqidagi gaplarga aylanadi.

chapters.recap_uz: Kirishning ikkinchi yarmi: Escherning imkonsiz rasmlari (cheksiz zinapoya, o'zidan o'zi oqadigan sharshara, bir-birini chizayotgan qo'llar) g'alati halqaning vizual shakli sifatida; yolg'onchi paradoksi, Rassel va Hilbertning orzusi, Gödelning 1931-yilgi kashfiyoti; va nihoyat Bebbij, Ada Lavleys va Tyuring — fikrlaydigan mashinalar g'oyasi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bobda Gödel teoremasining mazmuni faqat umumiy ko'rinishda beriladi. Uning qanday isbotlanishi butun kitob davomida, XIV bobgacha asta-sekin ochiladi — sabr qiling.

chapters.title: Chapter I: The MU-puzzle
chapters.title_uz: I bob: MU jumbog'i

paras.en: Before Chapter I, Hofstadter places a short dialogue in which Achilles and the Tortoise play with simple rules. The chapter then introduces the first formal system of the book. A formal system is like a game played with symbols. You are given a few strings of symbols to start with, called axioms, and a few rules for producing new strings from old ones. Any string you can produce by following the rules is called a theorem. Nothing else matters: you are not allowed to use your understanding, only the rules.
paras.uz: I bobdan oldin Hofstadter Axilles va Toshbaqa oddiy qoidalar bilan o'ynaydigan qisqa dialog joylashtiradi. Keyin bob kitobning birinchi formal tizimini taqdim etadi. Formal tizim — belgilar bilan o'ynaladigan o'yinga o'xshaydi. Sizga boshlash uchun aksiomalar deb ataladigan bir nechta belgilar qatori va eski qatorlardan yangilarini hosil qilish uchun bir nechta qoida beriladi. Qoidalarga amal qilib hosil qila oladigan har qanday qator teorema deb ataladi. Boshqa hech narsa muhim emas: sizga tushunchangizdan emas, faqat qoidalardan foydalanishga ruxsat beriladi.

paras.en: The system is called the MIU-system because it uses only three letters: M, I and U. It has a single axiom: the string MI. And it has four rules. Rule I: if a string ends with I, you may add U at the end (so MI can become MIU). Rule II: if you have Mx, where x is any string, you may make Mxx — doubling everything after the M (so MIU becomes MIUIU). Rule III: if III appears anywhere, you may replace it with U. Rule IV: if UU appears anywhere, you may drop it.
paras.uz: Tizim MIU-tizimi deb ataladi, chunki u faqat uchta harfdan foydalanadi: M, I va U. Unda bitta aksioma bor: MI qatori. Va to'rtta qoida bor. I qoida: agar qator I bilan tugasa, oxiriga U qo'shishingiz mumkin (shunday qilib MI MIU ga aylanishi mumkin). II qoida: agar sizda Mx bo'lsa, bu yerda x — istalgan qator, Mxx hosil qilishingiz mumkin — M dan keyingi hamma narsani ikki baravar qilish (shunday qilib MIU MIUIU ga aylanadi). III qoida: agar biror joyda III paydo bo'lsa, uni U bilan almashtirishingiz mumkin. IV qoida: agar biror joyda UU paydo bo'lsa, uni olib tashlashingiz mumkin.

paras.en: Then comes the puzzle: can you produce the string MU? Try it. You start with MI. Rule II gives MII, then MIIII. Rule III turns MIIII into MUI or MIU. Rule I, Rule IV... You can play for a long time, generating strings like MIUIU, MUIIU, MIIIIIIII. Many readers spend an hour trying, and the strings grow and shrink, but MU never appears. Hofstadter wants you to experience this: the feeling of working inside a system, mechanically, and slowly beginning to suspect that something prevents you from reaching the goal.
paras.uz: Keyin jumboq keladi: MU qatorini hosil qila olasizmi? Sinab ko'ring. Siz MI dan boshlaysiz. II qoida MII ni, keyin MIIII ni beradi. III qoida MIIII ni MUI yoki MIU ga aylantiradi. I qoida, IV qoida... Siz MIUIU, MUIIU, MIIIIIIII kabi qatorlar hosil qilib, uzoq o'ynashingiz mumkin. Ko'p o'quvchilar bir soat urinib ko'rishadi, qatorlar o'sadi va qisqaradi, lekin MU hech qachon paydo bo'lmaydi. Hofstadter sizni buni boshdan kechirishingizni istaydi: tizim ichida, mexanik ishlash va maqsadga erishishga nimadir to'sqinlik qilayotganidan asta-sekin shubhalana boshlash tuyg'usi.

paras.en: Here Hofstadter introduces an important distinction: working within the system (the 'M-mode', mechanical mode) versus thinking about the system from outside (the 'I-mode', intelligent mode). A machine following the rules will never stop to ask whether MU is reachable; it will just keep producing strings. A human, after a while, gets bored, steps back, and looks for patterns. This ability to jump out of a task and observe it from above is, for Hofstadter, one of the marks of intelligence — and a theme that will return throughout the book.
paras.uz: Shu yerda Hofstadter muhim farqni kiritadi: tizim ichida ishlash («M-rejim», mexanik rejim) va tizim haqida tashqaridan o'ylash («I-rejim», aqlli rejim). Qoidalarga amal qiladigan mashina hech qachon MU ga yetib bo'ladimi, deb so'rash uchun to'xtamaydi; u shunchaki qatorlar hosil qilishda davom etadi. Inson esa bir muddatdan keyin zerikadi, orqaga chekinadi va naqshlarni izlaydi. Vazifadan sakrab chiqib, unga yuqoridan qarash qobiliyati Hofstadter uchun aqlning belgilaridan biri — va butun kitob bo'ylab qaytadigan mavzu.

paras.en: So let us think in I-mode. Look at the number of I's in each string. The axiom MI has one I. Rule I and Rule IV don't change the number of I's. Rule II doubles it. Rule III subtracts three. Start with 1; doubling gives 2, 4, 8, 16...; subtracting 3 gives other numbers. But can you ever reach a number of I's that is divisible by 3? If you start with a number not divisible by 3, doubling it gives a number not divisible by 3, and subtracting 3 doesn't change divisibility by 3. So the count of I's can never be 0.
paras.uz: Keling, I-rejimda o'ylaylik. Har bir qatordagi I lar soniga qarang. MI aksiomasida bitta I bor. I qoida va IV qoida I lar sonini o'zgartirmaydi. II qoida uni ikki baravar qiladi. III qoida uchtani ayiradi. 1 dan boshlang; ikki baravar qilish 2, 4, 8, 16... ni beradi; 3 ni ayirish boshqa sonlarni beradi. Lekin 3 ga bo'linadigan I lar soniga yeta olasizmi? Agar 3 ga bo'linmaydigan sondan boshlasangiz, uni ikki baravar qilish 3 ga bo'linmaydigan sonni beradi, 3 ni ayirish esa 3 ga bo'linishni o'zgartirmaydi. Demak, I lar soni hech qachon 0 bo'la olmaydi.

paras.en: And MU has zero I's — zero is divisible by 3. Therefore MU is not a theorem of the MIU-system: it can never be produced. Hofstadter actually leaves this solution for later chapters and lets the reader find it, but this is the answer. Notice what happened: we could not prove that MU is unreachable by playing inside the system, no matter how long we played. We had to step outside and reason about a property — the number of I's — that the rules themselves never mention.
paras.uz: MU da esa nolta I bor — nol 3 ga bo'linadi. Demak, MU MIU-tizimining teoremasi emas: uni hech qachon hosil qilib bo'lmaydi. Hofstadter aslida bu yechimni keyingi boblarga qoldiradi va o'quvchiga uni o'zi topishga imkon beradi, lekin javob shu. Nima bo'lganiga e'tibor bering: tizim ichida qanchalik uzoq o'ynamaylik, MU ga yetib bo'lmasligini o'ynash orqali isbotlay olmadik. Biz tashqariga chiqib, qoidalarning o'zi hech qachon tilga olmaydigan xususiyat — I lar soni haqida mulohaza yuritishimiz kerak edi.

paras.en: This introduces a key vocabulary. A theorem is a string that can be produced. A derivation is the step-by-step list showing how it was produced. An important question for any formal system is whether there is a decision procedure — a test that always finishes and tells you whether a given string is a theorem or not. For MIU, the divisibility argument gives us a partial test. In general, it is easy to list theorems one by one, but much harder to decide, for a given string, whether it will ever appear on the list.
paras.uz: Bu muhim lug'atni kiritadi. Teorema — hosil qilish mumkin bo'lgan qator. Keltirib chiqarish (derivatsiya) — u qanday hosil qilinganini ko'rsatadigan qadam-baqadam ro'yxat. Har qanday formal tizim uchun muhim savol — qaror chiqarish protsedurasi bormi: har doim tugaydigan va berilgan qator teorema yoki yo'qligini aytadigan test. MIU uchun bo'linish dalili bizga qisman test beradi. Umuman olganda, teoremalarni birma-bir sanab chiqish oson, lekin berilgan qator ro'yxatda qachondir paydo bo'ladimi — buni hal qilish ancha qiyin.

paras.en: Hofstadter also points out that rules can be used in different orders, and the space of possible strings branches like a tree, with MI at the root. You can generate theorems systematically, level by level: first MI, then everything one step away, then everything two steps away, and so on. This guarantees that every theorem eventually appears. But if a string is not a theorem, this process will never tell you so — it will simply run forever. The difference between 'eventually appears' and 'can be decided' will become very important later.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek qoidalarni turli tartibda qo'llash mumkinligini va mumkin bo'lgan qatorlar maydoni ildizida MI bo'lgan daraxtdek shoxlanishini ko'rsatadi. Teoremalarni tizimli ravishda, darajama-daraja hosil qilish mumkin: avval MI, keyin bir qadam uzoqdagi hamma narsa, keyin ikki qadam uzoqdagi hamma narsa va hokazo. Bu har bir teorema oxir-oqibat paydo bo'lishini kafolatlaydi. Lekin agar qator teorema bo'lmasa, bu jarayon buni sizga hech qachon aytmaydi — u shunchaki abadiy davom etadi. «Oxir-oqibat paydo bo'ladi» va «hal qilish mumkin» o'rtasidagi farq keyinroq juda muhim bo'ladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: MI, MII, MIIII, MUI, MUIU... I've been at it since breakfast, Tortoise. Tortoise: And how close are you to MU? Achilles: Very close! It has only two letters. Tortoise: Shortness is not closeness. Stop writing for a moment and count something. Achilles: Count what? Tortoise: The I's. What do the rules do to them? Achilles: Double them, or take away three... and one is never... oh! I'll never get zero! Tortoise: Then you have just done something no rule allowed: you thought about the rules.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: MI, MII, MIIII, MUI, MUIU... Nonushtadan beri shu bilan bandman, Toshbaqa. Toshbaqa: MU ga qanchalik yaqinsan? Axilles: Juda yaqin! Unda bor-yo'g'i ikkita harf bor. Toshbaqa: Qisqalik yaqinlik emas. Bir lahza yozishni to'xtatib, biror narsani sana. Axilles: Nimani sanay? Toshbaqa: I larni. Qoidalar ular bilan nima qiladi? Axilles: Ikki baravar qiladi yoki uchtasini olib tashlaydi... va bir hech qachon... oh! Men hech qachon nol olmayman! Toshbaqa: Unda sen hozirgina hech bir qoida ruxsat bermagan ishni qilding: qoidalar haqida o'ylading.

paras.en: Why start a book about minds with a silly letter game? Because the MIU-system shows, in miniature, the situation of a mathematician working in a formal system like Principia Mathematica, and also the situation of a computer program following instructions. Inside the system, everything is mechanical. Meaning, insight and the answer to big questions come only when someone looks at the system from a higher level. The rest of the book asks: can a system ever look at itself from that higher level — and what happens when it does?
paras.uz: Nega aql haqidagi kitobni bema'ni harf o'yini bilan boshlash kerak? Chunki MIU-tizimi kichik ko'rinishda «Principia Mathematica» kabi formal tizimda ishlayotgan matematikning holatini, shuningdek ko'rsatmalarga amal qilayotgan kompyuter dasturining holatini ko'rsatadi. Tizim ichida hamma narsa mexanik. Ma'no, ichki idrok va katta savollarga javob faqat kimdir tizimga yuqoriroq darajadan qaraganda keladi. Kitobning qolgan qismi so'raydi: tizim qachondir o'ziga o'sha yuqoriroq darajadan qaray oladimi — va qaraganda nima bo'ladi?

quiz.q: What is the single axiom of the MIU-system?
quiz.why_uz: Yagona aksioma — MI.

quiz.q: Why can MU never be produced?
o: The number of I's can never become divisible by 3
U cannot be at the end
quiz.why_uz: I lar soni 1 dan boshlanadi va hech qachon 3 ga bo'linmaydi, MU da esa nol I.

quiz.q: What is the difference between M-mode and I-mode?
o: Mechanical work inside the system versus intelligent thinking about it
quiz.why_uz: M-rejim — mexanik, I-rejim — tizim haqida tashqaridan o'ylash.

chapters.recap_uz: Birinchi bob formal tizim nima ekanini oddiy o'yin — MIU tizimi orqali ko'rsatadi: uchta harf (M, I, U), bitta aksioma (MI) va to'rtta qoida. Savol: MU ni hosil qilish mumkinmi? Bob «tizim ichida ishlash» va «tizimdan tashqariga chiqib o'ylash» farqini, qaror chiqarish protsedurasi va teorema tushunchalarini tushuntiradi.
chapters.note_uz: Qog'oz va qalam oling va MIU o'yinini o'zingiz o'ynab ko'ring. Bu bob butun kitobning poydevori: keyingi barcha formal tizimlar shu andozada quriladi.

chapters.title: Chapter II: Meaning and form — the pq-system
chapters.title_uz: II bob: Ma'no va shakl — pq-tizimi

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter II is not by Hofstadter at all. It is Lewis Carroll's little piece from 1895, 'What the Tortoise Said to Achilles', which is now in the public domain. In it, Achilles has just won his race, and the Tortoise proposes a different kind of contest. He takes two statements, A and B, from Euclid's geometry, and a conclusion Z that follows from them. He agrees that A and B are true, but says he does not yet accept that Z follows. Achilles must force him, logically, to accept Z.
paras.uz: II bobdan oldingi dialog umuman Hofstadterniki emas. Bu Lyuis Kerrolning 1895-yilgi kichik asari «Toshbaqa Axillesga nima dedi», u hozir jamoat mulki. Unda Axilles poygani endigina yutgan va Toshbaqa boshqa turdagi musobaqani taklif qiladi. U Evklid geometriyasidan ikkita gap — A va B ni, va ulardan kelib chiqadigan Z xulosani oladi. U A va B ning to'g'riligiga rozi bo'ladi, lekin Z ulardan kelib chiqishini hali qabul qilmasligini aytadi. Axilles uni mantiqan Z ni qabul qilishga majbur qilishi kerak.

paras.en: Achilles writes down a new statement, C: 'If A and B are true, Z must be true.' The Tortoise happily accepts C, but asks: why should A, B and C together force me to accept Z? Achilles writes D: 'If A, B and C are true, Z must be true.' The Tortoise accepts D and asks the same question again. Achilles fills his notebook with E, F, G... and the Tortoise never has to accept Z. The point is deep: the rules of reasoning cannot all be written down as further statements. At some point you must simply use a rule, not state it.
paras.uz: Axilles yangi gap C ni yozadi: «Agar A va B to'g'ri bo'lsa, Z to'g'ri bo'lishi shart.» Toshbaqa C ni bajonidil qabul qiladi, lekin so'raydi: nega A, B va C birgalikda meni Z ni qabul qilishga majbur qilishi kerak? Axilles D ni yozadi: «Agar A, B va C to'g'ri bo'lsa, Z to'g'ri bo'lishi shart.» Toshbaqa D ni qabul qiladi va yana o'sha savolni beradi. Axilles daftarini E, F, G... bilan to'ldiradi va Toshbaqa hech qachon Z ni qabul qilishi shart bo'lmaydi. Ma'nosi chuqur: mulohaza qoidalarining hammasini qo'shimcha gaplar sifatida yozib bo'lmaydi. Qaysidir nuqtada qoidani aytmasdan, shunchaki undan foydalanish kerak.

paras.en: Hofstadter will use this lesson again and again: in any formal system, the rules of inference work at a different level from the strings they manipulate. Now he introduces the pq-system. It has three symbols: p, q and the hyphen (-). Its axioms follow a pattern, called an axiom schema: any string of the form x p - q x -, where x is a group of hyphens. For example, -p-q-- is an axiom, and so is --p-q---. There is one rule: if x p y q z is a theorem, then x p y - q z - is also a theorem.
paras.uz: Hofstadter bu saboqdan qayta-qayta foydalanadi: har qanday formal tizimda xulosa chiqarish qoidalari ular ishlov beradigan qatorlardan boshqa darajada ishlaydi. Endi u pq-tizimini taqdim etadi. Unda uchta belgi bor: p, q va chiziqcha (-). Uning aksiomalari aksioma sxemasi deb ataladigan andozaga amal qiladi: x p - q x - shaklidagi har qanday qator, bu yerda x — chiziqchalar guruhi. Masalan, -p-q-- aksioma, --p-q--- ham aksioma. Bitta qoida bor: agar x p y q z teorema bo'lsa, unda x p y - q z - ham teorema.

paras.en: Play with it for a while. From the axiom --p-q--- you can derive --p--q----, then --p---q-----. Soon you notice something. In every theorem, the number of hyphens before p, plus the number between p and q, equals the number after q. If you read p as 'plus', q as 'equals', and a group of hyphens as the number of hyphens in it, then --p---q----- says '2 plus 3 equals 5'. The meaningless game of symbols suddenly seems to be about addition. Every theorem becomes a true statement about adding numbers.
paras.uz: U bilan biroz o'ynab ko'ring. --p-q--- aksiomasidan --p--q---- ni, keyin --p---q----- ni keltirib chiqarish mumkin. Tez orada nimanidir payqaysiz. Har bir teoremada p dan oldingi chiziqchalar soni plus p va q orasidagi chiziqchalar soni q dan keyingi chiziqchalar soniga teng. Agar p ni «plus», q ni «teng», chiziqchalar guruhini esa undagi chiziqchalar soni deb o'qisangiz, --p---q----- «2 plus 3 teng 5» deydi. Ma'nosiz belgilar o'yini birdan qo'shish haqida bo'lib tuyuladi. Har bir teorema sonlarni qo'shish haqidagi haqiqiy gapga aylanadi.

paras.en: This is Hofstadter's central idea about meaning. Meaning, he says, arises through isomorphism: an exact correspondence between the structure of the symbol game and the structure of some part of reality. The symbols do not 'contain' meaning by themselves. But because the theorems of the pq-system line up perfectly with true additions, it is natural — almost irresistible — to say that the system is 'about' addition. When we discover such an isomorphism, we feel a little shock of understanding, as when a code is suddenly cracked.
paras.uz: Bu Hofstadterning ma'no haqidagi markaziy g'oyasi. Ma'no, deydi u, izomorfizm orqali paydo bo'ladi: belgilar o'yinining tuzilmasi va haqiqatning biror qismi tuzilmasi o'rtasidagi aniq moslik. Belgilar o'z-o'zidan ma'noni «o'z ichiga olmaydi». Lekin pq-tizimining teoremalari haqiqiy qo'shishlar bilan mukammal mos kelgani uchun, tizim qo'shish «haqida» deyish tabiiy — deyarli qarshi turib bo'lmaydigan. Biz bunday izomorfizmni kashf etganimizda, xuddi kod birdan ochilgandek, kichik tushunish zarbasini his qilamiz.

paras.en: Hofstadter also shows that the interpretation is not unique. You could read the same symbols in other ways, and some readings would also make every theorem true, though less naturally. He distinguishes a meaningful interpretation — one under which all theorems come out true — from meaningless ones. He also notes a limitation: with the 'plus' interpretation, the pq-system can express only true additions, but it cannot express that something is false, or say 'for all numbers'. It is a very small window onto arithmetic.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek talqin yagona emasligini ko'rsatadi. Xuddi shu belgilarni boshqa yo'llar bilan o'qish mumkin va ba'zi o'qishlar ham har bir teoremani haqiqiy qiladi, garchi kamroq tabiiy bo'lsa ham. U ma'noli talqinni — barcha teoremalar haqiqiy chiqadigan talqinni — ma'nosiz talqinlardan ajratadi. U shuningdek bir cheklovni qayd etadi: «plus» talqinida pq-tizimi faqat haqiqiy qo'shishlarni ifodalay oladi, lekin biror narsa yolg'on ekanini ifodalay olmaydi yoki «barcha sonlar uchun» deya olmaydi. Bu arifmetikaga juda kichik derazadir.

paras.en: Unlike the MIU-system, the pq-system has a simple decision procedure. Given any string, you can check whether it has the right shape and whether the hyphen counts add up. Notice also that the rule only makes strings longer. This is a useful property: if a system's rules never shorten strings, you can decide whether a string is a theorem by generating all theorems up to that length and checking. Systems with shortening rules, like MIU (whose Rules III and IV shorten strings), are much harder to decide.
paras.uz: MIU-tizimidan farqli o'laroq, pq-tizimida oddiy qaror chiqarish protsedurasi bor. Har qanday qator berilganda, u to'g'ri shaklga ega ekanini va chiziqchalar soni mos kelishini tekshirishingiz mumkin. Shuningdek, qoida faqat qatorlarni uzaytirishiga e'tibor bering. Bu foydali xususiyat: agar tizim qoidalari hech qachon qatorlarni qisqartirmasa, o'sha uzunlikkacha bo'lgan barcha teoremalarni hosil qilib, tekshirish orqali qator teorema ekanini hal qilishingiz mumkin. MIU kabi qisqartiruvchi qoidalarga ega tizimlarni (uning III va IV qoidalari qatorlarni qisqartiradi) hal qilish ancha qiyin.

paras.en: The chapter then asks a philosophical question: are the truths of arithmetic 'out there', independent of any system? Hofstadter introduces a typographical convention: a 'theorem' (small t) is a string produced in a formal system, while a 'Theorem' (capital T) is a true statement of mathematics as mathematicians understand it. He reminds us of Euclid's ancient proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers: suppose there were a largest prime; multiply all primes together and add one; the new number is not divisible by any of them, so there must be another prime.
paras.uz: Keyin bob falsafiy savol beradi: arifmetika haqiqatlari har qanday tizimdan mustaqil ravishda «u yerda» mavjudmi? Hofstadter tipografik kelishuvni kiritadi: «theorem» (kichik t) — formal tizimda hosil qilingan qator, «Theorem» (bosh T) esa matematiklar tushunadigan ma'nodagi matematikaning haqiqiy gapi. U Evklidning tub sonlar cheksiz ko'p ekanining qadimiy isbotini eslatadi: eng katta tub son bor deb faraz qiling; barcha tub sonlarni ko'paytirib, bir qo'shing; yangi son ularning birortasiga ham bo'linmaydi, demak, yana bir tub son bo'lishi kerak.

paras.en: Euclid's proof talks about all numbers, about infinity, in a few lines. It seems to show that human reasoning can grasp infinite truths with finite steps. Hofstadter's question for the rest of Part I is: can such reasoning be captured completely by a formal system — a mechanical game like MIU or pq, only much bigger? If it can, then mathematics is just very long M-mode. If it cannot, then there is something in mathematical truth that escapes every set of rules. Gödel, of course, will give the surprising answer.
paras.uz: Evklid isboti bir necha satrda barcha sonlar haqida, cheksizlik haqida gapiradi. U inson mulohazasi cheksiz haqiqatlarni chekli qadamlar bilan anglay olishini ko'rsatayotgandek tuyuladi. Hofstadterning I qismning qolgan qismi uchun savoli: bunday mulohazani formal tizim — MIU yoki pq kabi, faqat ancha kattaroq mexanik o'yin — to'liq qamrab ola oladimi? Agar olsa, matematika shunchaki juda uzun M-rejim. Agar ololmasa, matematik haqiqatda har qanday qoidalar to'plamidan qochib qoladigan nimadir bor. Albatta, hayratlanarli javobni Gödel beradi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: I've decoded your silly pq-game, Tortoise! p is plus, q is equals. It's just arithmetic. Tortoise: Is it? Then tell me: who put the arithmetic in? Achilles: Well — you did, when you made the rules. Tortoise: I made rules about hyphens. I never mentioned a single number. Achilles: But the theorems match the sums perfectly! Tortoise: Exactly. The meaning wasn't put in; it was found — in the match. Two structures dancing in step. Remember that word for the match: isomorphism. Achilles: It sounds like a disease. Tortoise: It is the cure for meaninglessness.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Sening bema'ni pq-o'yiningni ochdim, Toshbaqa! p — plus, q — teng. Bu shunchaki arifmetika. Toshbaqa: Shundaymi? Unda ayt-chi: arifmetikani kim kiritdi? Axilles: Xo'sh — sen, qoidalarni tuzganingda. Toshbaqa: Men chiziqchalar haqida qoidalar tuzdim. Birorta ham sonni tilga olmadim. Axilles: Lekin teoremalar yig'indilarga mukammal mos keladi! Toshbaqa: Aynan. Ma'no kiritilmagan; u topilgan — moslikda. Ikki tuzilma bir maromda raqsga tushmoqda. Bu moslik uchun so'zni eslab qol: izomorfizm. Axilles: Kasallikka o'xshab eshitiladi. Toshbaqa: Bu ma'nosizlikning davosi.

o: Rules of reasoning cannot all be written down as further premises
quiz.why_uz: Qaysidir nuqtada qoidani aytmasdan, undan foydalanish kerak — aks holda cheksiz regress.

quiz.q: Under the natural interpretation, what does --p---q----- mean?
quiz.why_uz: p — plus, q — teng, chiziqchalar soni — son.

quiz.why_uz: Ma'no izomorfizm — tuzilmalar o'rtasidagi aniq moslik orqali paydo bo'ladi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldin Lyuis Kerrolning 1895-yilgi dialogi keladi: Toshbaqa mantiqiy xulosani qabul qilish uchun cheksiz qo'shimcha asoslar talab qiladi. Bob esa pq-tizimini taqdim etadi va ma'no qanday qilib izomorfizm orqali paydo bo'lishini ko'rsatadi: ma'nosiz belgilar o'yini birdan qo'shish haqidagi haqiqatlarni ifodalay boshlaydi.
chapters.note_uz: «Izomorfizm» — kitobning eng muhim so'zlaridan biri. Uni «tuzilmalar o'rtasidagi aniq moslik» deb tushuning: bir tizimdagi har bir qismga ikkinchisida bir qism to'g'ri keladi va munosabatlar saqlanadi.

chapters.title: Chapter III: Figure and ground
chapters.title_uz: III bob: Shakl va fon

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter III is a playful experiment in form. It is a 'sonata for unaccompanied Achilles': we hear only Achilles speaking on the telephone to the Tortoise. The Tortoise's half of the conversation is missing, and yet, from Achilles' replies, we can reconstruct it quite well. The missing voice is like the background of a picture — not drawn, but clearly present. Bach wrote sonatas for solo violin and solo cello in which a single line of melody manages to suggest whole harmonies that are never actually played.
paras.uz: III bobdan oldingi dialog — shakl bo'yicha o'ynoqi tajriba. Bu «hamrohsiz Axilles uchun sonata»: biz faqat Toshbaqa bilan telefonda gaplashayotgan Axillesni eshitamiz. Suhbatning Toshbaqa yarmi yo'q, shunga qaramay Axillesning javoblaridan uni ancha yaxshi tiklay olamiz. Yo'q ovoz rasmning foniga o'xshaydi — chizilmagan, lekin aniq mavjud. Bax yakka skripka va yakka violonchel uchun sonatalar yozgan, ularda bitta kuy satri haqiqatda hech qachon chalinmaydigan butun garmoniyalarni his qildira oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter then turns to drawings. In any picture there is a figure — the shape we notice — and a ground — the space around it. Usually the ground is just leftover space. But some pictures are drawn so that the ground also forms meaningful shapes. Escher's tilings of birds and fish are the extreme case: every bit of space is a creature, and you can see either the black birds or the white fish, but not both at once. Hofstadter calls a figure whose ground is also a recognisable figure a 'recursive' figure.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter rasmlarga o'tadi. Har qanday rasmda shakl — biz payqaydigan qiyofa va fon — uning atrofidagi bo'shliq bor. Odatda fon shunchaki ortib qolgan bo'shliq. Lekin ba'zi rasmlar shunday chizilganki, fon ham ma'noli shakllar hosil qiladi. Escherning qushlar va baliqlardan iborat naqshlari — eng chekka holat: bo'shliqning har bir bo'lagi mavjudot va siz yo qora qushlarni, yo oq baliqlarni ko'rasiz, lekin ikkalasini bir vaqtda emas. Hofstadter foni ham taniladigan shakl bo'lgan shaklni «rekursiv» shakl deb ataydi.

paras.en: He also notices the same effect with letters. If you write a word in large letters and colour the background instead of the letters, the background may form other letters, or nothing at all. Most backgrounds are not themselves meaningful shapes. Hofstadter calls ordinary figures, whose ground is just shapeless leftover, 'cursive'. The question he will ask is a mathematical version of this: if a set of numbers is the 'figure', is its complement, the 'ground', also a set that some system can produce?
paras.uz: U xuddi shu effektni harflarda ham payqaydi. Agar so'zni katta harflar bilan yozib, harflarni emas, fonni bo'yasangiz, fon boshqa harflarni hosil qilishi yoki umuman hech narsa hosil qilmasligi mumkin. Ko'pchilik fonlar o'zi ma'noli shakl emas. Hofstadter foni shunchaki shaklsiz qoldiq bo'lgan oddiy shakllarni «kursiv» deb ataydi. U beradigan savol buning matematik varianti: agar sonlar to'plami «shakl» bo'lsa, uning to'ldiruvchisi — «fon» ham qandaydir tizim hosil qila oladigan to'plammi?

paras.en: To explore this, he builds the tq-system, a twin of the pq-system. Its theorems look like x t y q z, and under the natural interpretation t means 'times' and q means 'equals'. So ---t--q------ means '3 times 2 equals 6'. Then he adds a rule to create a new kind of theorem: if x t y q z is a theorem, and x and y each have at least two hyphens, then Cz is a theorem. Under interpretation, Cz means 'z is composite' — a number that can be written as a product of two numbers greater than one.
paras.uz: Buni o'rganish uchun u pq-tizimining egizagi — tq-tizimini quradi. Uning teoremalari x t y q z ko'rinishida bo'ladi va tabiiy talqinda t «karra», q «teng» degan ma'noni beradi. Shunday qilib ---t--q------ «3 karra 2 teng 6» degani. Keyin u yangi turdagi teorema yaratish uchun qoida qo'shadi: agar x t y q z teorema bo'lsa va x va y har birida kamida ikkita chiziqcha bo'lsa, unda Cz teorema. Talqinda Cz «z murakkab son» degani — birdan katta ikki sonning ko'paytmasi sifatida yozish mumkin bo'lgan son.

paras.en: So now we have a formal system that produces all composite numbers: C----, C------, C--------, C---------, and so on. The composite numbers are the 'figure'. What about the 'ground' — the numbers that are not composite, which (apart from 1) are the primes? Can we simply say 'P z is a theorem whenever C z is not a theorem'? No — that is not a legal rule in a formal system. Rules must produce new theorems from old ones by visible, mechanical steps; they cannot say 'if something is never produced'.
paras.uz: Shunday qilib endi bizda barcha murakkab sonlarni hosil qiladigan formal tizim bor: C----, C------, C--------, C--------- va hokazo. Murakkab sonlar — «shakl». «Fon»-chi — murakkab bo'lmagan sonlar, ular (1 dan tashqari) tub sonlar? Shunchaki «Cz teorema bo'lmagan har safar Pz teorema» deya olamizmi? Yo'q — bu formal tizimda qonuniy qoida emas. Qoidalar ko'rinadigan, mexanik qadamlar bilan eskilaridan yangi teoremalar hosil qilishi kerak; ular «agar biror narsa hech qachon hosil qilinmasa» deya olmaydi.

paras.en: Hofstadter shows that for the primes there is a way out: you can build a different system that directly produces the primes, using the idea 'does not divide'. A number is prime if no smaller number greater than one divides it, and 'does not divide' can be checked mechanically. So in this case the ground can be captured as a figure too. But this success required a new idea; it did not come automatically from the composite system. Prime numbers turn out to be a 'recursive' figure: both they and their complement can be produced.
paras.uz: Hofstadter tub sonlar uchun chiqish yo'li borligini ko'rsatadi: «bo'linmaydi» g'oyasidan foydalanib, tub sonlarni bevosita hosil qiladigan boshqa tizim qurish mumkin. Agar birdan katta hech bir kichikroq son uni bo'lmasa, son tub hisoblanadi va «bo'linmaydi»ni mexanik tekshirish mumkin. Shunday qilib bu holda fonni ham shakl sifatida qamrab olish mumkin. Lekin bu muvaffaqiyat yangi g'oyani talab qildi; u murakkab sonlar tizimidan avtomatik kelmadi. Tub sonlar «rekursiv» shakl bo'lib chiqadi: ularni ham, ularning to'ldiruvchisini ham hosil qilish mumkin.

paras.en: Then comes the key fact, which Hofstadter states here and proves much later: there exist formal systems whose non-theorems cannot be produced by any formal system at all. In technical language, there are sets that are 'recursively enumerable' — their members can be listed one by one by a mechanical procedure — but whose complements are not. For such a set, you can wait and see a member appear, but you can never be sure that something will not appear. The figure can be drawn, but the ground can never be drawn.
paras.uz: Keyin asosiy fakt keladi, Hofstadter uni shu yerda bayon qiladi va ancha keyin isbotlaydi: shunday formal tizimlar borki, ularning teorema bo'lmaganlarini umuman hech qanday formal tizim hosil qila olmaydi. Texnik tilda aytganda, «rekursiv sanaladigan» — a'zolarini mexanik protsedura bilan birma-bir ro'yxatga olish mumkin bo'lgan, lekin to'ldiruvchilari bunday bo'lmagan to'plamlar bor. Bunday to'plam uchun siz kutib, a'zo paydo bo'lganini ko'rishingiz mumkin, lekin biror narsa paydo bo'lmasligiga hech qachon ishonch hosil qila olmaysiz. Shaklni chizish mumkin, lekin fonni hech qachon chizib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: Why does this matter? Because it means that truth and provability might not line up. Imagine the set of all true statements of arithmetic. The theorems of a formal system can be listed mechanically — that is the figure. If the true statements that are not theorems formed a ground that could not be captured by any system, then no single system could ever produce all truths. This is exactly the shape of Gödel's theorem. Chapter III prepares the intuition: some ground is 'shapeless', and no set of rules can ever draw it.
paras.uz: Bu nega muhim? Chunki bu haqiqat va isbotlanuvchanlik mos kelmasligi mumkinligini anglatadi. Arifmetikaning barcha haqiqiy gaplari to'plamini tasavvur qiling. Formal tizim teoremalarini mexanik ravishda ro'yxatga olish mumkin — bu shakl. Agar teorema bo'lmagan haqiqiy gaplar hech qanday tizim qamrab ola olmaydigan fon hosil qilsa, unda hech qanday yagona tizim barcha haqiqatlarni hosil qila olmasdi. Bu aynan Gödel teoremasining shakli. III bob sezgini tayyorlaydi: ba'zi fonlar «shaklsiz» va hech qanday qoidalar to'plami uni hech qachon chiza olmaydi.

paras.en: The chapter ends by returning to music. In a piece of music, the melody is the figure and the accompaniment the ground, but in Bach's counterpoint every voice is a melody — the background is made of foregrounds. Listening to a fugue, you can choose which voice to follow, just as you can choose to see birds or fish in Escher. Hofstadter suggests that the ability to switch between figure and ground, between what is said and what is implied, is a key part of how minds find meaning.
paras.uz: Bob musiqaga qaytish bilan tugaydi. Musiqa asarida kuy — shakl, akkompanement — fon, lekin Baxning kontrapunktida har bir ovoz kuy — fon oldingi planlardan yasalgan. Fugani tinglarkansiz, qaysi ovozga ergashishni tanlashingiz mumkin, xuddi Escherda qushlarni yoki baliqlarni ko'rishni tanlashingiz mumkin bo'lganidek. Hofstadterning fikricha, shakl va fon o'rtasida, aytilgan va nazarda tutilgan narsa o'rtasida almashish qobiliyati aqlning ma'no topish usulining muhim qismidir.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: I've made a machine that prints every composite number, Tortoise: 4, 6, 8, 9, 10... It never misses one! Tortoise: Splendid. Now print me the primes. Achilles: Easy — the primes are just the numbers it doesn't print. Tortoise: And how long must I wait to be sure it will never print 7? Achilles: Well... forever? Tortoise: Then your 'easy' needs a new machine. A list of what happens is not a list of what never happens. Achilles: So the gaps need their own drawing? Tortoise: And sometimes, Achilles, the gaps cannot be drawn at all.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Men har bir murakkab sonni chop etadigan mashina yasadim, Toshbaqa: 4, 6, 8, 9, 10... U birortasini ham o'tkazib yubormaydi! Toshbaqa: Ajoyib. Endi menga tub sonlarni chop et. Axilles: Oson — tub sonlar u chop etmaydigan sonlar-ku. Toshbaqa: Va u hech qachon 7 ni chop etmasligiga ishonch hosil qilish uchun qancha kutishim kerak? Axilles: Xo'sh... abadiy? Toshbaqa: Unda sening «oson»ing yangi mashinaga muhtoj. Sodir bo'ladigan narsalar ro'yxati hech qachon sodir bo'lmaydigan narsalar ro'yxati emas. Axilles: Demak, bo'shliqlarga o'z chizmasi kerakmi? Toshbaqa: Ba'zan esa, Axilles, bo'shliqlarni umuman chizib bo'lmaydi.
