quiz.q: What is unusual about the dialogue before Chapter III?
o: We hear only Achilles' side of a phone call
quiz.why_uz: Toshbaqaning javoblari yo'q, ular fon sifatida taxmin qilinadi.

quiz.q: Why can't we just say 'Pz is a theorem whenever Cz is not a theorem'?
o: Formal rules cannot refer to what is never produced
quiz.why_uz: Qoidalar faqat ko'rinadigan mexanik qadamlar bilan ishlaydi.

quiz.q: What is the key fact stated in this chapter?
o: Some formal systems have non-theorems that no formal system can produce
quiz.why_uz: Ba'zi rekursiv sanaladigan to'plamlarning to'ldiruvchisi sanaladigan emas.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi dialogda biz faqat telefonda gaplashayotgan Axillesning so'zlarini eshitamiz — Toshbaqaning javoblari «fon» sifatida taxmin qilinadi. Bob Escher rasmlaridagi shakl va fon g'oyasini sonlarga ko'chiradi: ko'paytirish (tq-tizimi), murakkab sonlar (C-tizimi) va tub sonlar. Asosiy kashfiyot: ba'zi formal tizimlarda teorema bo'lmaganlar to'plami boshqa hech qanday formal tizimning teoremalari to'plami bo'la olmaydi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bobning eng muhim farqi: «sanab chiqish mumkin» (barcha a'zolarni birma-bir hosil qilish) va «hal qilish mumkin» (istalgan son a'zo yoki yo'qligini aniq aytish). Bu farq keyinroq Gödel va Tyuring boblarida markaziy bo'ladi.

chapters.title: Chapter IV: Consistency, completeness and geometry
chapters.title_uz: IV bob: Ziddiyatsizlik, to'liqlik va geometriya

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter IV, 'Contracrostipunctus', tells a story that is one of the best-known analogies in the whole book. The Crab buys an expensive record player and boasts that it can reproduce any sound perfectly. The Tortoise then brings him a record with a song called, in effect, 'I Cannot Be Played on Record Player 1'. When the Crab plays it, the song contains exactly those frequencies that make the machine vibrate so violently that it shatters. A 'perfect' player, it turns out, can be destroyed by a sound designed for it.
paras.uz: IV bobdan oldingi «Contracrostipunctus» dialogi butun kitobdagi eng mashhur analogiyalardan birini hikoya qiladi. Qisqichbaqa qimmatbaho grammofon sotib olib, u har qanday tovushni mukammal qayta tiklay olishi bilan maqtanadi. Keyin Toshbaqa unga amalda «Meni 1-grammofonda chalib bo'lmaydi» deb nomlangan qo'shiqli plastinka olib keladi. Qisqichbaqa uni chalganda, qo'shiqda aynan mashinani shunchalik qattiq tebratadigan chastotalar borki, u chil-chil sinadi. Ma'lum bo'lishicha, «mukammal» grammofonni unga mo'ljallab yaratilgan tovush yo'q qilishi mumkin.

paras.en: The Crab buys a new, better record player. The Tortoise studies it and brings a new record: 'I Cannot Be Played on Record Player 2'. The same thing happens. The Crab then tries a player that is deliberately low-quality and cannot reproduce every sound — and it survives, but now it cannot play everything. There is a dilemma: a player good enough to play any record can be destroyed by some record made for it; a player that protects itself by refusing certain records is no longer 'perfect'. Either it breaks, or it is incomplete.
paras.uz: Qisqichbaqa yangi, yaxshiroq grammofon sotib oladi. Toshbaqa uni o'rganib, yangi plastinka olib keladi: «Meni 2-grammofonda chalib bo'lmaydi». Xuddi shu narsa sodir bo'ladi. Keyin Qisqichbaqa ataylab sifatsiz, har bir tovushni qayta tiklay olmaydigan grammofonni sinab ko'radi — u omon qoladi, lekin endi hamma narsani chala olmaydi. Dilemma bor: har qanday plastinkani chala oladigan darajada yaxshi grammofonni unga mo'ljallab yasalgan qandaydir plastinka yo'q qilishi mumkin; ba'zi plastinkalarni rad etib o'zini himoya qiladigan grammofon esa endi «mukammal» emas. Yo u sinadi, yo u to'liq emas.

paras.en: Hofstadter makes the analogy explicit in the chapter. The record player is a formal system for mathematics. 'Playing every record' means proving every true statement — completeness. 'Not shattering' means not proving contradictions — consistency. The Tortoise's special record is Gödel's sentence, built precisely for a given system so that it describes that system's own limits. And the dialogue itself is full of tricks: its title is a play on 'acrostic' and 'contrapunctus', and the first letters of the speeches hide a message, just as Bach hid his name in music.
paras.uz: Hofstadter bobda analogiyani ochiq aytadi. Grammofon — matematika uchun formal tizim. «Har qanday plastinkani chalish» har bir haqiqiy gapni isbotlashni — to'liqlikni anglatadi. «Sinmaslik» ziddiyatlarni isbotlamaslikni — ziddiyatsizlikni anglatadi. Toshbaqaning maxsus plastinkasi — Gödel jumlasi, u aynan berilgan tizim uchun, o'sha tizimning o'z chegaralarini tasvirlaydigan qilib qurilgan. Dialogning o'zi ham hiylalarga to'la: uning nomi «akrostix» va «contrapunctus» so'zlari bilan o'yin, nutqlarning bosh harflari esa, xuddi Bax o'z ismini musiqada yashirgani kabi, xabarni yashiradi.

paras.en: Now the chapter defines the two key ideas more carefully. A formal system is consistent, under a given interpretation, if every theorem comes out true when interpreted. It is complete if every true statement that can be expressed in the system is a theorem. Hofstadter stresses that consistency is not a property of the symbols alone; it depends on the interpretation. A system might look inconsistent under one reading and perfectly consistent under another. This leads to a surprising experiment with the pq-system.
paras.uz: Endi bob ikki asosiy g'oyani aniqroq ta'riflaydi. Formal tizim berilgan talqinda ziddiyatsiz, agar talqin qilinganda har bir teorema haqiqiy chiqsa. U to'liq, agar tizimda ifodalash mumkin bo'lgan har bir haqiqiy gap teorema bo'lsa. Hofstadter ziddiyatsizlik faqat belgilarning xususiyati emasligini ta'kidlaydi; u talqinga bog'liq. Tizim bir o'qishda ziddiyatli, boshqasida mutlaqo ziddiyatsiz ko'rinishi mumkin. Bu pq-tizimi bilan hayratlanarli tajribaga olib keladi.

paras.en: Suppose we add a new axiom to the pq-system: -p-q-. Under the old interpretation it says '1 plus 1 equals 1', which is false — so the system becomes inconsistent. But wait: we can change the interpretation. If we read q not as 'equals' but as 'is greater than or equal to', then -p-q- says '1 plus 1 is greater than or equal to 1', which is true. Check the other theorems: they also come out true under the new reading. So the enlarged system is consistent after all. The new axiom forced the symbol q to change its meaning.
paras.uz: Faraz qilaylik, pq-tizimiga yangi aksioma qo'shamiz: -p-q-. Eski talqinda u «1 plus 1 teng 1» deydi, bu yolg'on — demak tizim ziddiyatli bo'lib qoladi. Lekin to'xtang: talqinni o'zgartirishimiz mumkin. Agar q ni «teng» emas, «katta yoki teng» deb o'qisak, -p-q- «1 plus 1 1 dan katta yoki teng» deydi, bu haqiqat. Boshqa teoremalarni tekshiring: ular ham yangi o'qishda haqiqiy chiqadi. Shunday qilib kengaytirilgan tizim baribir ziddiyatsiz. Yangi aksioma q belgisini ma'nosini o'zgartirishga majbur qildi.

paras.en: This is a model of what happened in the history of geometry, which Hofstadter tells next. Euclid built geometry on five postulates. The first four are simple: you can draw a line between two points, extend it, draw a circle, all right angles are equal. The fifth, the parallel postulate, is more complicated: it says, in effect, that through a point outside a line there is exactly one line parallel to it. For two thousand years mathematicians felt it was less obvious and tried to prove it from the other four.
paras.uz: Bu Hofstadter keyin hikoya qiladigan geometriya tarixida nima bo'lganining modeli. Evklid geometriyani beshta postulat ustiga qurgan. Birinchi to'rttasi oddiy: ikki nuqta orasida chiziq chizish, uni davom ettirish, aylana chizish mumkin, barcha to'g'ri burchaklar teng. Beshinchisi — parallellik postulati — murakkabroq: u amalda to'g'ri chiziqdan tashqaridagi nuqta orqali unga parallel aniq bitta chiziq o'tadi, deydi. Ikki ming yil davomida matematiklar uni kamroq ravshan deb his qilishgan va qolgan to'rttasidan isbotlashga urinishgan.

paras.en: In the eighteenth century the Italian Jesuit Girolamo Saccheri tried a clever approach: assume the fifth postulate is false, and look for a contradiction. He derived many strange results — triangles whose angles add up to less than 180 degrees — and finally declared them 'repugnant to the nature of the straight line'. But he had not found a real contradiction. In the nineteenth century Gauss, János Bolyai and Nikolai Lobachevsky realised the truth: the strange results form a perfectly consistent geometry of their own. Later Riemann found yet another kind.
paras.uz: XVIII asrda italiyalik iyezuit Jirolamo Sakkeri aqlli yondashuvni sinab ko'rdi: beshinchi postulat yolg'on deb faraz qilib, ziddiyat izlash. U ko'plab g'alati natijalarni — burchaklari yig'indisi 180 darajadan kam bo'lgan uchburchaklarni — keltirib chiqardi va oxiri ularni «to'g'ri chiziq tabiatiga zid» deb e'lon qildi. Lekin u haqiqiy ziddiyat topmagan edi. XIX asrda Gauss, Yanosh Boyai va Nikolay Lobachevskiy haqiqatni anglashdi: g'alati natijalar o'ziga xos mutlaqo ziddiyatsiz geometriyani tashkil etadi. Keyinroq Riman yana bir turini topdi.

paras.en: What changed? The words 'point' and 'line'. In Euclid's mind they had one meaning, taken from experience. But in a formal system, such words are undefined terms: they get their meaning passively, from the axioms in which they appear. Change the axioms, and the 'lines' become, for example, great circles on a sphere, or curves on a saddle-shaped surface. Just as q in the pq-system came to mean 'greater than or equal to', 'line' in non-Euclidean geometry came to mean something new. The symbols had not changed; the system had.
paras.uz: Nima o'zgardi? «Nuqta» va «chiziq» so'zlari. Evklid ongida ular tajribadan olingan bitta ma'noga ega edi. Lekin formal tizimda bunday so'zlar ta'riflanmagan atamalar: ular o'z ma'nosini passiv ravishda, o'zlari ishtirok etadigan aksiomalardan oladi. Aksiomalarni o'zgartiring va «chiziqlar», masalan, shar sirtidagi katta aylanalarga yoki egarsimon sirtdagi egri chiziqlarga aylanadi. pq-tizimidagi q «katta yoki teng» ma'nosini olganidek, noevklid geometriyadagi «chiziq» yangi narsani anglatadigan bo'ldi. Belgilar o'zgarmagan edi; tizim o'zgargan edi.

paras.en: Hofstadter ends the chapter with a reflection on different levels of consistency. A system can be logically consistent (no contradictions), mathematically consistent (agrees with known mathematics), physically consistent (could exist in our universe), and so on. Escher's pictures are logically consistent in each detail but physically impossible as wholes. Stories, dreams and even Lewis Carroll's worlds have their own levels of consistency. The question for mathematics is the strictest one: can a formal system be both consistent and complete? The record players suggest the answer.
paras.uz: Hofstadter bobni ziddiyatsizlikning turli darajalari haqidagi mulohaza bilan tugatadi. Tizim mantiqan ziddiyatsiz (ziddiyatlarsiz), matematik jihatdan ziddiyatsiz (ma'lum matematikaga mos), fizik jihatdan ziddiyatsiz (bizning koinotimizda mavjud bo'lishi mumkin) va hokazo bo'lishi mumkin. Escherning rasmlari har bir tafsilotda mantiqan ziddiyatsiz, lekin butunligicha fizik jihatdan imkonsiz. Hikoyalar, tushlar va hatto Lyuis Kerrolning dunyolari ham ziddiyatsizlikning o'z darajalariga ega. Matematika uchun savol — eng qat'iysi: formal tizim ham ziddiyatsiz, ham to'liq bo'la oladimi? Grammofonlar javobga ishora qiladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I've bought the finest record player in the world. It plays absolutely everything. Tortoise: Everything? Then it will play this little record of mine. Achilles: What's on it? Tortoise: A song about your player. It describes, very exactly, the one vibration your player cannot survive. Achilles: Then I'll buy a better player! Tortoise: And I'll write a better song. For every player, its own song. Achilles: Then I'll buy a player that refuses dangerous songs. Tortoise: Then it no longer plays everything. Choose, Achilles: broken or incomplete.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, dunyodagi eng zo'r grammofonni sotib oldim. U mutlaqo hamma narsani chaladi. Toshbaqa: Hamma narsanimi? Unda u mening mana bu kichik plastinkamni ham chaladi. Axilles: Unda nima bor? Toshbaqa: Sening grammofoning haqida qo'shiq. U grammofoning chiday olmaydigan yagona tebranishni juda aniq tasvirlaydi. Axilles: Unda yaxshiroq grammofon sotib olaman! Toshbaqa: Men esa yaxshiroq qo'shiq yozaman. Har bir grammofonga — o'z qo'shig'i. Axilles: Unda xavfli qo'shiqlarni rad etadigan grammofon olaman. Toshbaqa: Unda u endi hamma narsani chalmaydi. Tanla, Axilles: singanmi yoki to'liq emasmi.

quiz.q: In the record player analogy, what does the Tortoise's special record represent?
o: Gödel's sentence built for a given system
quiz.why_uz: Plastinka berilgan tizim uchun qurilgan Gödel jumlasini ifodalaydi.

quiz.q: What happens to the pq-system when the axiom -p-q- is added?
o: q can be reinterpreted as 'greater than or equal to', keeping it consistent
quiz.why_uz: Yangi aksioma q ning ma'nosini o'zgartirdi.

quiz.q: What did Gauss, Bolyai and Lobachevsky realise?
o: Denying the parallel postulate gives a consistent geometry
quiz.why_uz: Beshinchi postulatni inkor etish o'ziga xos ziddiyatsiz geometriyani beradi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Contracrostipunctus» dialogida Toshbaqa Qisqichbaqaning grammofonlarini maxsus plastinkalar bilan sindiradi: har bir plastinka «meni bu grammofonda chalib bo'lmaydi» degan ma'noga ega. Bob ziddiyatsizlik va to'liqlik tushunchalarini, pq-tizimining yangi talqinini va Evklidning beshinchi postulati tarixini — noevklid geometriyalarning kashf etilishini tushuntiradi.
chapters.note_uz: Grammofon hikoyasi Gödel teoremasining eng mashhur analogiyalaridan biri: har qanday yetarlicha kuchli tizim uchun uni «sindiradigan» gap topiladi, xuddi har qanday grammofon uchun uni buzadigan plastinka topilgandek.

chapters.title: Chapter V: Recursive structures and processes
chapters.title_uz: V bob: Rekursiv tuzilmalar va jarayonlar

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter V is called 'Little Harmonic Labyrinth', and it is itself a labyrinth. Achilles and the Tortoise are caught by a villain and escape by drinking a 'pushing potion', which carries them into the world of an Escher print. Inside that world they find a story, and step into it; inside that story there is another story. To get back out of each level, they need a 'popping tonic'. The dialogue keeps track of how deep they are — and, at the end, they climb out of several levels but never quite get back to where they started.
paras.uz: V bobdan oldingi dialog «Kichik garmonik labirint» deb ataladi va o'zi ham labirint. Axilles va Toshbaqa bir yovuzning qo'liga tushadi va «itaruvchi ichimlik» ichib qochadi, u ularni Escher gravyurasi dunyosiga olib kiradi. O'sha dunyoning ichida ular hikoya topib, unga kiradi; o'sha hikoyaning ichida yana bir hikoya bor. Har bir darajadan qaytib chiqish uchun ularga «chiqaruvchi damlama» kerak. Dialog ular qanchalik chuqurlikda ekanini kuzatib boradi — va oxirida ular bir necha darajadan chiqib oladi, lekin boshlagan joyiga hech qachon to'liq qaytmaydi.

paras.en: Inside one of the stories there is a genie who can grant wishes — but not a wish for more wishes. Such 'meta-wishes' must be approved by a meta-genie, who must ask a meta-meta-genie, and so on up an infinite tower. At the top of the tower stands GOD, which Hofstadter explains as an acronym: 'GOD Over Djinn'. This is a recursive acronym — the letter G stands for GOD itself, so the name contains itself. The joke is serious: it shows how a definition can refer to itself without collapsing into nonsense.
paras.uz: Hikoyalardan birining ichida tilaklarni bajaradigan jin bor — lekin ko'proq tilaklar so'rash tilagini emas. Bunday «meta-tilaklar»ni meta-jin tasdiqlashi kerak, u meta-meta-jindan so'rashi kerak va hokazo cheksiz minora bo'ylab yuqoriga. Minoraning tepasida GOD turadi, Hofstadter uni qisqartma sifatida tushuntiradi: «GOD Over Djinn» — «Jinlar ustidagi GOD». Bu rekursiv qisqartma — G harfining o'zi GOD ni anglatadi, shunday qilib nom o'zini o'z ichiga oladi. Hazil jiddiy: u ta'rif bema'nilikka qulamasdan o'ziga qanday ishora qilishi mumkinligini ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: The chapter begins with a simple picture of recursion: nesting. Hofstadter uses three words from computer science. To 'push' means to suspend what you are doing and go into a new, deeper task, remembering where you were. To 'pop' means to finish the deeper task and return to where you left off. The memory of all the suspended tasks is called a 'stack', like a stack of plates where you can only add or remove the top one. When you answer a phone call in the middle of reading, you push; when you hang up and continue reading, you pop.
paras.uz: Bob rekursiyaning oddiy tasviridan boshlanadi: ichma-ich joylashish. Hofstadter informatikadan uchta so'zni ishlatadi. «Push» — qilayotgan ishingizni to'xtatib, qayerda ekaningizni eslab qolib, yangi, chuqurroq vazifaga kirish. «Pop» — chuqurroq vazifani tugatib, to'xtagan joyingizga qaytish. To'xtatilgan barcha vazifalar xotirasi «stek» deb ataladi, xuddi faqat yuqoridagisini qo'shish yoki olish mumkin bo'lgan likopchalar taxlami kabi. O'qish o'rtasida telefonga javob berganingizda, siz push qilasiz; go'shakni qo'yib, o'qishni davom ettirganingizda, pop qilasiz.

paras.en: Stories within stories, sentences within sentences, and melodies that modulate away from their home key and then return are all examples of pushing and popping. In music, a piece in C major may move into G major, then into D major, building a stack of keys in the listener's mind; the ear 'expects' to pop back to C at the end. Hofstadter notes that Bach, in the dialogue's music, plays with this expectation. In language, a sentence like 'The man the dog the cat chased bit ran away' is grammatical but hard to understand, because it pushes too deep.
paras.uz: Hikoya ichidagi hikoyalar, gap ichidagi gaplar va o'z asosiy tonalligidan uzoqlashib, keyin qaytadigan kuylar — bularning hammasi push va pop misollari. Musiqada do major asar sol majorga, keyin re majorga o'tishi mumkin, tinglovchi ongida tonalliklar stekini quradi; quloq oxirida do ga pop qilib qaytishni «kutadi». Hofstadter dialog musiqasida Bax bu kutish bilan o'ynashini qayd etadi. Tilda «Mushuk quvgan it tishlagan odam qochib ketdi» kabi gap grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri, lekin tushunish qiyin, chunki u haddan tashqari chuqur push qiladi.

paras.en: Next, Hofstadter describes grammar using 'recursive transition networks' (RTNs). Imagine a map with arrows: to build a NOUN PHRASE, you might pass through 'article', then 'adjective', then 'noun'. But one of the boxes on the map can be 'NOUN PHRASE' itself — so to build a noun phrase you may need to build a smaller noun phrase inside it. The network calls itself. This is how a finite set of rules can generate an infinite number of sentences: 'the house', 'the house of the man', 'the house of the man with the dog', and so on.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter grammatikani «rekursiv o'tish tarmoqlari» (RTN) yordamida tasvirlaydi. Strelkali xaritani tasavvur qiling: OT BIRIKMASI qurish uchun «artikl», keyin «sifat», keyin «ot» orqali o'tishingiz mumkin. Lekin xaritadagi qutilardan biri OT BIRIKMASI ning o'zi bo'lishi mumkin — shunday qilib ot birikmasini qurish uchun uning ichida kichikroq ot birikmasini qurishingiz kerak bo'lishi mumkin. Tarmoq o'zini chaqiradi. Chekli qoidalar to'plami cheksiz miqdordagi gaplarni shunday hosil qila oladi: «uy», «odamning uyi», «itli odamning uyi» va hokazo.

paras.en: The important point is the difference between recursion and infinite regress. A recursive definition defines something in terms of simpler versions of itself, and always bottoms out in a base case. The classic example is the Fibonacci sequence: FIBO(1) = FIBO(2) = 1, and FIBO(n) = FIBO(n−1) + FIBO(n−2). To compute FIBO(5), you push down to FIBO(4) and FIBO(3), and so on, until you reach the simple cases you already know. Carroll's Tortoise, by contrast, never reaches a base case — that is why his regress is endless.
paras.uz: Muhim nuqta — rekursiya va cheksiz regress o'rtasidagi farq. Rekursiv ta'rif narsani o'zining soddaroq versiyalari orqali ta'riflaydi va har doim asos holatga yetib tugaydi. Klassik misol — Fibonachchi ketma-ketligi: FIBO(1) = FIBO(2) = 1 va FIBO(n) = FIBO(n−1) + FIBO(n−2). FIBO(5) ni hisoblash uchun siz FIBO(4) va FIBO(3) ga push qilasiz va hokazo, toki allaqachon biladigan oddiy holatlarga yetguningizcha. Kerrolning Toshbaqasi esa, aksincha, hech qachon asos holatga yetmaydi — shuning uchun uning regressi cheksiz.

paras.en: Hofstadter then presents some strange recursive sequences of his own. One is G(n) = n − G(G(n−1)), with G(0) = 0: a function defined in terms of itself applied twice. It produces a sequence with a hidden link to the golden ratio and to a tree that grows by a simple rule. Another, the 'Q-sequence', is defined by Q(n) = Q(n − Q(n−1)) + Q(n − Q(n−2)), with Q(1) = Q(2) = 1. Its values jump around chaotically, and nobody fully understands its behaviour. Simple recursive rules can produce surprising complexity.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter o'zining bir nechta g'alati rekursiv ketma-ketliklarini taqdim etadi. Biri — G(n) = n − G(G(n−1)), G(0) = 0: o'ziga ikki marta qo'llangan holda ta'riflangan funksiya. U oltin nisbat bilan va oddiy qoida bo'yicha o'sadigan daraxt bilan yashirin bog'liq ketma-ketlik hosil qiladi. Boshqasi — «Q-ketma-ketlik» Q(n) = Q(n − Q(n−1)) + Q(n − Q(n−2)), Q(1) = Q(2) = 1 bilan ta'riflanadi. Uning qiymatlari tartibsiz sakraydi va hech kim uning xatti-harakatini to'liq tushunmaydi. Oddiy rekursiv qoidalar hayratlanarli murakkablik hosil qilishi mumkin.

paras.en: He also shows a recursive picture: a graph, which he calls 'Gplot', that is made of smaller copies of itself, each copy distorted slightly, which in turn are made of smaller copies, forever. Such self-similar shapes were later popularised as fractals. Then he looks at physics: in quantum theory, a particle interacts with 'virtual particles', which themselves interact with others, and physicists draw Feynman diagrams that nest inside one another. A 'bare' electron is never seen alone; what we see is the electron with all its nested interactions — a recursive object.
paras.uz: U shuningdek rekursiv rasmni ko'rsatadi: o'zining kichikroq, biroz buzilgan nusxalaridan tashkil topgan, ular o'z navbatida yana kichikroq nusxalardan tashkil topgan va hokazo abadiy davom etadigan grafik, uni «Gplot» deb ataydi. Bunday o'ziga o'xshash shakllar keyinchalik fraktallar nomi bilan mashhur bo'ldi. Keyin u fizikaga qaraydi: kvant nazariyasida zarra «virtual zarralar» bilan o'zaro ta'sirlashadi, ular o'z navbatida boshqalar bilan ta'sirlashadi va fiziklar bir-birining ichiga joylashadigan Feynman diagrammalarini chizadi. «Yalang'och» elektron hech qachon yolg'iz ko'rinmaydi; biz ko'radigan narsa — barcha ichma-ich o'zaro ta'sirlari bilan elektron — rekursiv ob'ekt.

paras.en: Finally, Hofstadter mentions chess programs. A program choosing a move imagines each possible move, then each possible reply, then each reply to the reply, building a tree. To evaluate a position, it evaluates the positions that can follow — a recursive process that must stop at some depth and use a rough estimate there. This 'look-ahead' is recursion in action, and it shows a general truth: intelligent behaviour often involves exploring nested possibilities, but also knowing when to stop pushing and simply judge.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, Hofstadter shaxmat dasturlarini eslatadi. Yurish tanlayotgan dastur har bir mumkin bo'lgan yurishni, keyin har bir mumkin bo'lgan javobni, keyin javobga javobni tasavvur qilib, daraxt quradi. Pozitsiyani baholash uchun u undan keyin kelishi mumkin bo'lgan pozitsiyalarni baholaydi — bu qaysidir chuqurlikda to'xtashi va u yerda taxminiy bahodan foydalanishi kerak bo'lgan rekursiv jarayon. Bu «oldinga qarash» — harakatdagi rekursiya va u umumiy haqiqatni ko'rsatadi: aqlli xatti-harakat ko'pincha ichma-ich imkoniyatlarni o'rganishni, lekin shuningdek push qilishni qachon to'xtatib, shunchaki baho berishni bilishni o'z ichiga oladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I read a story in which a man reads a story in which a woman reads a story... and now I can't remember which story I'm in. Tortoise: Then keep a stack. Each time you enter a story, put a plate on the pile; each time you finish one, take a plate off. Achilles: And when the pile is empty? Tortoise: You are back in your armchair. Achilles: What if a story never ends? Tortoise: Then you never come back. That is the difference between a good recursion and a bad dream: the good one always has a bottom.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men bir hikoya o'qidim, unda bir erkak hikoya o'qiydi, unda bir ayol hikoya o'qiydi... va endi qaysi hikoyada ekanimni eslay olmayman. Toshbaqa: Unda stek tut. Har safar hikoyaga kirganingda, taxlamga likopcha qo'y; har safar birini tugatganingda, likopchani ol. Axilles: Taxlam bo'shab qolganda-chi? Toshbaqa: Sen yana kreslongdasan. Axilles: Agar hikoya hech qachon tugamasa-chi? Toshbaqa: Unda sen hech qachon qaytmaysan. Yaxshi rekursiya va yomon tush o'rtasidagi farq shu: yaxshisining doim tubi bor.

quiz.q: What does 'GOD' stand for in the dialogue?
o: GOD Over Djinn — a recursive acronym
quiz.why_uz: Rekursiv qisqartma: G harfi GOD ning o'zini anglatadi.

quiz.q: What distinguishes good recursion from infinite regress?
o: Recursion always bottoms out in a base case
quiz.why_uz: Rekursiya har doim asos holatga yetib tugaydi.

quiz.q: What does 'pop' mean?
o: Finish a deeper task and return to where you left off
quiz.why_uz: Pop — chuqurroq vazifadan qaytib, to'xtagan joyga qaytish.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Kichik garmonik labirint» dialogida Axilles va Toshbaqa hikoya ichidagi hikoyalarga «kirib» va «chiqib» yuradi, sehrli jin o'zidan kattaroq jinni chaqiradi va hokazo. Bob rekursiya — o'z ichiga o'zining kichikroq nusxasini olgan narsa — g'oyasini tushuntiradi: stek (push va pop), grammatika tarmoqlari, Fibonachchi sonlari, Hofstadterning G va Q ketma-ketliklari, o'zini takrorlaydigan grafik, fizika va shaxmat dasturlari.
chapters.note_uz: Rekursiya bilan cheksiz regress o'rtasidagi farqni yodda tuting: rekursiya har doim pastki darajada tugaydigan «asos holat»ga ega; Kerrolning Toshbaqasidagi regress esa hech qachon tugamaydi.

chapters.title: Chapter VI: The location of meaning
chapters.title_uz: VI bob: Ma'no qayerda joylashgan

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter VI is a friendly argument. Achilles and the Tortoise are listening to records on a jukebox, and they disagree about where the music 'really' is. Achilles says the information is in the record: the grooves contain the song. The Tortoise argues that the record alone is useless; the jukebox, with its needle, amplifier and speaker, is needed to turn the grooves into sound. Perhaps the jukebox contains more information than the record? Their argument goes round in circles, and the chapter tries to sort it out.
paras.uz: VI bobdan oldingi dialog — do'stona bahs. Axilles va Toshbaqa avtomat-grammofonda plastinkalarni tinglab o'tirishibdi va musiqa «aslida» qayerda ekani haqida kelisha olmayapti. Axilles ma'lumot plastinkada deydi: ariqchalar qo'shiqni o'z ichiga oladi. Toshbaqa plastinkaning o'zi foydasiz deb ta'kidlaydi; ariqchalarni tovushga aylantirish uchun igna, kuchaytirgich va karnayli avtomat kerak. Balki avtomat plastinkadan ko'proq ma'lumotga egadir? Ularning bahsi doira bo'ylab aylanadi va bob uni tartibga solishga harakat qiladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter starts with biology. A DNA molecule contains the instructions for building an organism. But a strand of DNA floating in a test tube will not build anything. It needs the machinery of a living cell — enzymes, ribosomes and so on — to read it and carry out its instructions. So where is the information about, say, a frog? Is it in the frog's DNA, or in the DNA plus the frog's egg cell that knows how to read it? This is the same question as the record and the jukebox.
paras.uz: Hofstadter biologiyadan boshlaydi. DNK molekulasi organizmni qurish uchun ko'rsatmalarni o'z ichiga oladi. Lekin probirkada suzib yurgan DNK zanjiri hech narsa qurmaydi. Uni o'qish va ko'rsatmalarini bajarish uchun tirik hujayra mexanizmi — fermentlar, ribosomalar va hokazolar kerak. Unda, masalan, qurbaqa haqidagi ma'lumot qayerda? Qurbaqa DNKsidami yoki DNK plyus uni qanday o'qishni biladigan qurbaqa tuxum hujayrasidami? Bu plastinka va avtomat haqidagi savolning o'zi.

paras.en: To make progress, Hofstadter distinguishes three layers of any message. The first is the frame message: the signal that says 'I am a message — decode me'. A bottle with paper inside, washed up on a beach, carries a strong frame message: someone obviously meant this to be read. The second is the outer message: information about how to decode the inner message, such as the language or the code being used. The third is the inner message: the actual content that the sender wanted to communicate.
paras.uz: Oldinga siljish uchun Hofstadter har qanday xabarning uch qatlamini ajratadi. Birinchisi — ramka xabari: «Men xabarman — meni och» degan signal. Sohilga chiqib qolgan, ichida qog'oz bo'lgan shisha kuchli ramka xabarini olib yuradi: kimdir buni o'qilishi uchun mo'ljallagani aniq. Ikkinchisi — tashqi xabar: ichki xabarni qanday ochish haqidagi ma'lumot, masalan, ishlatilgan til yoki kod. Uchinchisi — ichki xabar: jo'natuvchi yetkazmoqchi bo'lgan haqiqiy mazmun.

paras.en: The outer message is the tricky part, because it can never be fully stated in words. If you send instructions explaining how to read a message, those instructions are themselves a message that needs to be read. This is Lewis Carroll's Tortoise again: an infinite regress of decoding rules. The regress stops only because some decoding mechanism is built in — a brain, a cell, a record player — that simply does the work without being told. Every message relies on some reader who already understands something.
paras.uz: Tashqi xabar — eng nozik qism, chunki uni hech qachon so'zlar bilan to'liq bayon qilib bo'lmaydi. Agar xabarni qanday o'qishni tushuntiradigan ko'rsatmalar yuborsangiz, bu ko'rsatmalarning o'zi o'qilishi kerak bo'lgan xabar. Bu yana Lyuis Kerrolning Toshbaqasi: ochish qoidalarining cheksiz regressi. Regress faqat qandaydir ochish mexanizmi — miya, hujayra, grammofon — ichiga o'rnatilgani uchun to'xtaydi, u aytilmasdan shunchaki ishni bajaradi. Har bir xabar allaqachon nimanidir tushunadigan qandaydir o'quvchiga tayanadi.

paras.en: Hofstadter then considers the decipherment of ancient scripts. The Rosetta Stone, carrying the same text in Egyptian hieroglyphs, Demotic and Greek, allowed Jean-François Champollion to decode hieroglyphs in the 1820s. Other scripts, such as Linear B from ancient Crete, were deciphered from patterns alone. These cases show that meaning can be extracted from a message even without a dictionary, if the message has enough internal structure — repetitions, regularities, links to things we already know. The meaning was, in a sense, waiting in the message.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter qadimiy yozuvlarning ochilishini ko'rib chiqadi. Bir xil matnni Misr ierogliflari, demotik yozuv va yunon tilida olib yurgan Rozetta toshi Jan-Fransua Shampolionga 1820-yillarda ierogliflarni ochish imkonini berdi. Qadimgi Kritdagi «B chiziqli yozuvi» kabi boshqa yozuvlar faqat naqshlardan ochildi. Bu holatlar shuni ko'rsatadiki, agar xabarda yetarli ichki tuzilma — takrorlar, qonuniyatlar, biz allaqachon biladigan narsalar bilan bog'lanishlar — bo'lsa, ma'noni lug'atsiz ham chiqarib olish mumkin. Ma'no, ma'lum ma'noda, xabarda kutib turgan edi.

paras.en: This leads to a bold question: if we sent a recording of Bach's music into space, could an alien civilisation understand it? Hofstadter's answer is a cautious yes. Bach's music is so richly structured — so full of patterns, symmetries and transformations — that any sufficiently intelligent being studying it would recognise that it was made by an intelligence, and might even understand something of its beauty. He contrasts this with a random sequence of sounds, which would contain no frame message at all.
paras.uz: Bu jasur savolga olib keladi: agar biz Bax musiqasi yozuvini kosmosga yuborsak, begona tsivilizatsiya uni tushuna olarmidi? Hofstadterning javobi — ehtiyotkor «ha». Bax musiqasi shunchalik boy tuzilgan — naqshlar, simmetriyalar va o'zgarishlarga shunchalik to'la — ki uni o'rganayotgan har qanday yetarlicha aqlli mavjudot uni aql yaratganini taniydi va hatto uning go'zalligidan nimanidir tushunishi mumkin. U buni hech qanday ramka xabariga ega bo'lmagan tasodifiy tovushlar ketma-ketligiga qarama-qarshi qo'yadi.

paras.en: From this, Hofstadter argues for a kind of 'intrinsic meaning'. Meaning is not only in the eye of the beholder. A message has intrinsic meaning to the extent that any intelligence would decode it the same way. Of course, the decoder must have some general abilities — pattern recognition, curiosity, a sense of what counts as simple. But if these abilities are shared by all intelligent beings, then a well-structured message carries its meaning with it, the way DNA carries the frog in a form that any cell of the right kind can read.
paras.uz: Bundan Hofstadter o'ziga xos «ichki ma'no» foydasiga bahs yuritadi. Ma'no faqat qarovchining ko'zida emas. Xabar har qanday aql uni bir xil ochadigan darajada ichki ma'noga ega. Albatta, ochuvchi qandaydir umumiy qobiliyatlarga — naqshlarni tanish, qiziquvchanlik, nima oddiy ekanini his qilish — ega bo'lishi kerak. Lekin agar bu qobiliyatlar barcha aqlli mavjudotlarda umumiy bo'lsa, yaxshi tuzilgan xabar o'z ma'nosini o'zi bilan olib yuradi, xuddi DNK qurbaqani to'g'ri turdagi har qanday hujayra o'qiy oladigan shaklda olib yurgani kabi.

paras.en: The chapter also returns to formal systems. The theorems of the pq-system seem to carry the meaning 'addition' because their structure is isomorphic to addition. Anyone who studies them carefully will find that isomorphism — it is not something we arbitrarily impose. This is why mathematicians feel that they discover rather than invent. And it prepares Gödel's trick: if strings of symbols can carry meanings through isomorphism, then a string of arithmetic might carry a second meaning — a meaning about strings themselves — for anyone who sees the right isomorphism.
paras.uz: Bob formal tizimlarga ham qaytadi. pq-tizimining teoremalari «qo'shish» ma'nosini olib yurganga o'xshaydi, chunki ularning tuzilmasi qo'shishga izomorf. Ularni diqqat bilan o'rgangan har kim bu izomorfizmni topadi — bu biz o'zboshimchalik bilan yuklaydigan narsa emas. Shuning uchun matematiklar ixtiro qilishdan ko'ra kashf qilayotgandek his qilishadi. Va bu Gödel hiylasini tayyorlaydi: agar belgilar qatorlari izomorfizm orqali ma'no olib yura olsa, unda arifmetika qatori to'g'ri izomorfizmni ko'rgan har kim uchun ikkinchi ma'noni — qatorlarning o'zi haqidagi ma'noni — olib yurishi mumkin.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: The song is in the record. Obviously. Tortoise: Then play me the record without a record player. Achilles: Don't be silly. Tortoise: Then the song is partly in the player. Achilles: But the player can play any song — it doesn't know this one! Tortoise: True. So the song is in the record, for anyone who knows how records work. And how do we know how records work? Achilles: We... grew up with them? Tortoise: Exactly. Every message leans on a reader. The question is only how much the reader must already know.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Qo'shiq plastinkada. Aniq. Toshbaqa: Unda menga plastinkani grammofonsiz chalib ber. Axilles: Bema'ni gapirma. Toshbaqa: Unda qo'shiq qisman grammofonda. Axilles: Lekin grammofon har qanday qo'shiqni chala oladi — u bu qo'shiqni bilmaydi! Toshbaqa: To'g'ri. Demak, qo'shiq plastinkada, plastinkalar qanday ishlashini biladigan har kim uchun. Plastinkalar qanday ishlashini qayerdan bilamiz? Axilles: Biz... ular bilan o'sganmiz? Toshbaqa: Aynan. Har bir xabar o'quvchiga suyanadi. Savol faqat o'quvchi oldindan qancha narsani bilishi kerakligida.

quiz.q: What are the three layers of a message, according to Hofstadter?
o: Frame message, outer message, inner message
quiz.why_uz: Ramka, tashqi va ichki xabar.

o: It needs the machinery of a cell to read it

Bob ma'no xabarning o'zidami yoki uni o'qiydigan mexanizmdami, degan savolni tekshiradi: DNK va hujayra, Rozetta toshi, kosmosga yuborilgan xabarlar. chapters.note_uz: Bu bob «ma'no faqat kuzatuvchining ko'zida» degan fikrga qarshi chiqadi: Hofstadter ba'zi xabarlar o'zida yetarlicha tuzilmaga ega bo'lgani uchun har qanday aqlli mavjudot ularni ocha oladi, deb ta'kidlaydi.

chapters.title: Chapter VII: The propositional calculus
chapters.title_uz: VII bob: Mulohazalar hisobi

paras.en: Before Chapter VII comes a dialogue whose title, 'Chromatic Fantasy, And Feud', is a pun on Bach's Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue. In it, Achilles and the Tortoise quarrel over the little words of logic — 'and', 'or', 'not' — and over what it means for statements to contradict each other. The chapter then builds a formal system for exactly those little words. It is called the propositional calculus, and it is the basic machinery that mathematicians use, often without noticing, whenever they reason with 'if', 'and', 'or' and 'not'.
paras.uz: VII bobdan oldin sarlavhasi — «Chromatic Fantasy, And Feud» — Baxning «Xromatik fantaziya va fuga»si bilan so'z o'yini bo'lgan dialog keladi. Unda Axilles va Toshbaqa mantiqning kichik so'zlari — «va», «yoki», «emas» haqida va gaplarning bir-biriga zid bo'lishi nimani anglatishi haqida janjallashadi. Keyin bob aynan shu kichik so'zlar uchun formal tizim quradi. U mulohazalar hisobi deb ataladi va bu matematiklar «agar», «va», «yoki» va «emas» bilan mulohaza yuritganda, ko'pincha sezmasdan foydalanadigan asosiy mexanizm.

paras.en: The system uses letters such as P, Q and R to stand for whole statements, called atoms. It has four connecting symbols. The wedge ∧ means 'and'. The vee ∨ means 'or'. The horseshoe ⊃ means 'if ... then'. The tilde ~ means 'not'. Pointed brackets group things together, so <P∧Q> means 'P and Q', and <P⊃Q> means 'if P then Q'. A well-formed string is one built correctly according to these patterns, just as a grammatical sentence is one built correctly according to the rules of a language.
paras.uz: Tizim butun gaplarni — atomlarni ifodalash uchun P, Q va R kabi harflardan foydalanadi. Unda to'rtta bog'lovchi belgi bor. ∧ — «va». ∨ — «yoki». ⊃ (taqa) — «agar... unda». ~ (tilda) — «emas». Uchli qavslar narsalarni guruhlaydi, shunday qilib <P∧Q> «P va Q», <P⊃Q> esa «agar P unda Q» degani. To'g'ri tuzilgan qator — xuddi grammatik gap til qoidalariga ko'ra to'g'ri tuzilgani kabi, shu andozalarga ko'ra to'g'ri qurilgan qator.

paras.en: Then come the rules of inference. The joining rule: if you have P and you have Q, you may write <P∧Q>. The separation rule: if you have <P∧Q>, you may write P (or Q) alone. The double-tilde rule: ~~P can be replaced by P and vice versa — 'not not P' is the same as P. These rules look almost too obvious to state. But that is the point: in a formal system, nothing may be used unless it is written down as a rule, and the system must work even for someone — or something — that understands nothing.
paras.uz: Keyin xulosa chiqarish qoidalari keladi. Birlashtirish qoidasi: agar sizda P va Q bo'lsa, <P∧Q> ni yozishingiz mumkin. Ajratish qoidasi: agar sizda <P∧Q> bo'lsa, P ni (yoki Q ni) alohida yozishingiz mumkin. Qo'sh tilda qoidasi: ~~P ni P bilan almashtirish mumkin va aksincha — «P emas emas» P bilan bir xil. Bu qoidalar aytishga hojat yo'q darajada ravshan ko'rinadi. Lekin gap shunda: formal tizimda qoida sifatida yozilmagan hech narsadan foydalanish mumkin emas va tizim hech narsani tushunmaydigan kimsa — yoki narsa — uchun ham ishlashi kerak.

paras.en: The most interesting rule is the fantasy rule. It allows you to 'push' into a hypothetical world: you write '[', then a premise P — 'suppose P is true' — and then you derive whatever you can inside the fantasy. When you reach some string Q, you 'pop' out by writing ']', and you are allowed to write <P⊃Q> in the real world: 'if P, then Q'. This is exactly what we do when we reason 'Suppose it rains; then the street is wet; so, if it rains, the street is wet.' The fantasy rule connects logic with recursion and with the stack of Chapter V.
paras.uz: Eng qiziq qoida — xayol (fantaziya) qoidasi. U sizga faraziy dunyoga «push» qilishga imkon beradi: siz «[» ni, keyin P muqaddimasini — «faraz qilaylik, P to'g'ri» — yozasiz va xayol ichida nimani keltirib chiqara olsangiz, shuni keltirib chiqarasiz. Biror Q qatorga yetganingizda, «]» yozib «pop» qilasiz va haqiqiy dunyoda <P⊃Q> ni — «agar P, unda Q» — yozishga ruxsat olasiz. Biz «Faraz qilaylik, yomg'ir yog'adi; unda ko'cha ho'l; demak, agar yomg'ir yog'sa, ko'cha ho'l» deb mulohaza yuritganimizda aynan shunday qilamiz. Xayol qoidasi mantiqni rekursiya va V bobdagi stek bilan bog'laydi.

paras.en: There are a few more rules. Carry-over: facts from the outer world may be brought into a fantasy. Detachment, known by its Latin name modus ponens: if you have P and <P⊃Q>, you may write Q. Contrapositive: <P⊃Q> can be turned into <~Q⊃~P> — 'if it rains, the street is wet' is equivalent to 'if the street is not wet, it is not raining'. De Morgan's rule: <~P∧~Q> is equivalent to ~<P∨Q>. And the 'switcheroo': <P∨Q> is equivalent to <~P⊃Q> — 'P or Q' means 'if not P, then Q'.
paras.uz: Yana bir nechta qoida bor. O'tkazish: tashqi dunyodagi faktlarni xayolga olib kirish mumkin. Ajratib olish, lotincha nomi bilan modus ponens: agar sizda P va <P⊃Q> bo'lsa, Q ni yozishingiz mumkin. Kontrapozitsiya: <P⊃Q> ni <~Q⊃~P> ga aylantirish mumkin — «agar yomg'ir yog'sa, ko'cha ho'l» «agar ko'cha ho'l bo'lmasa, yomg'ir yog'mayapti» ga teng. De Morgan qoidasi: <~P∧~Q> ~<P∨Q> ga teng. Va «almashtirish» (switcheroo): <P∨Q> <~P⊃Q> ga teng — «P yoki Q» «agar P emas bo'lsa, unda Q» degani.

paras.en: With these rules you can produce theorems that are true no matter what the atoms mean. The simplest is <P⊃P>: if P then P. You derive it by pushing into a fantasy with premise P, noticing that P is already there, and popping out. Others are less obvious, such as <<P⊃Q>⊃<~Q⊃~P>>. Under the natural interpretation, every theorem is a tautology — a statement true in all possible situations. And for this system there is a decision procedure: the method of truth tables can check any string mechanically.
paras.uz: Bu qoidalar bilan atomlar nimani anglatishidan qat'i nazar haqiqiy bo'lgan teoremalarni hosil qilish mumkin. Eng oddiysi — <P⊃P>: agar P unda P. Uni P muqaddimasi bilan xayolga push qilib, P allaqachon u yerda ekanini payqab, pop qilib chiqish orqali keltirib chiqarasiz. Boshqalari kamroq ravshan, masalan <<P⊃Q>⊃<~Q⊃~P>>. Tabiiy talqinda har bir teorema tavtologiya — barcha mumkin bo'lgan vaziyatlarda haqiqiy gap. Va bu tizim uchun qaror chiqarish protsedurasi bor: haqiqat jadvallari usuli istalgan qatorni mexanik ravishda tekshira oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter also explains why contradictions are so dangerous in a formal system. Suppose both P and ~P were theorems. Then, using the rules, you could derive any string at all, Q included — 'from a contradiction, anything follows'. A system that contains a contradiction does not just make one mistake; it collapses, because every statement becomes provable, and so the word 'provable' loses all meaning. This is why consistency is the first thing mathematicians demand of a system — and why the record player that shatters is such a good image.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek ziddiyatlar formal tizimda nega bunchalik xavfli ekanini tushuntiradi. Faraz qilaylik, P ham, ~P ham teorema bo'lsin. Unda qoidalardan foydalanib, umuman istalgan qatorni, jumladan Q ni keltirib chiqarish mumkin bo'lardi — «ziddiyatdan hamma narsa kelib chiqadi». Ziddiyatni o'z ichiga olgan tizim shunchaki bitta xato qilmaydi; u quladi, chunki har bir gap isbotlanadigan bo'lib qoladi va «isbotlanadigan» so'zi butun ma'nosini yo'qotadi. Shuning uchun ziddiyatsizlik matematiklar tizimdan birinchi talab qiladigan narsa — va shuning uchun sinadigan grammofon shunday yaxshi obraz.

paras.en: At the end of the chapter, Hofstadter reflects on how this formal logic relates to real thinking. People do not reason by applying rules like 'switcheroo' one by one. Real reasoning is fast, intuitive, full of shortcuts and sometimes of errors. Formal logic is more like a slow-motion film of a few kinds of reasoning, made precise so that even a machine could follow it. Its value is that it shows, very clearly, which steps are purely mechanical — and so it helps us see where, if anywhere, something more than mechanism enters.
paras.uz: Bob oxirida Hofstadter bu formal mantiq haqiqiy fikrlash bilan qanday bog'liqligi haqida mulohaza yuritadi. Odamlar «almashtirish» kabi qoidalarni birma-bir qo'llab mulohaza yuritmaydi. Haqiqiy mulohaza tez, intuitiv, qisqa yo'llarga va ba'zan xatolarga to'la. Formal mantiq ko'proq mulohazaning bir necha turining sekinlashtirilgan filmiga o'xshaydi, u hatto mashina ham ergasha oladigan darajada aniq qilingan. Uning qadri shundaki, u qaysi qadamlar sof mexanik ekanini juda aniq ko'rsatadi — va shuning uchun mexanizmdan ko'proq narsa qayerda, agar umuman bo'lsa, kirib kelishini ko'rishga yordam beradi.

paras.en: Hofstadter also notes a limit of the propositional calculus: it treats statements as unbreakable atoms. It can express 'P and Q', but not what is inside P — not 'every number has a successor' or 'there exists a prime greater than 100'. To talk about numbers, and about 'all' and 'some', we need a richer system that looks inside statements. That system, Typographical Number Theory, is the subject of the next chapter, and it is the system in which Gödel's surprising sentence will finally be built.
paras.uz: Hofstadter mulohazalar hisobining chegarasini ham qayd etadi: u gaplarni bo'linmas atomlar sifatida ko'radi. U «P va Q»ni ifodalay oladi, lekin P ning ichidagini — «har bir sonning keyingisi bor» yoki «100 dan katta tub son mavjud»ni emas. Sonlar haqida, «barcha» va «ba'zi» haqida gapirish uchun bizga gaplarning ichiga qaraydigan boyroq tizim kerak. Bu tizim — Tipografik sonlar nazariyasi — keyingi bobning mavzusi va aynan unda Gödelning hayratlanarli jumlasi nihoyat quriladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, you just agreed that it's raining and that it isn't raining. You can't do that! Tortoise: Why not? I'm very flexible. Achilles: Because then I could prove anything. Watch: it's raining, so 'it's raining or you owe me a cake' is true. But it isn't raining — so you owe me a cake! Tortoise: Oh dear. Achilles: And by the same trick, you owe me a palace. Tortoise: All right, all right, I withdraw one of my statements. Achilles: You see? One contradiction, and the whole world is for sale.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, sen hozirgina yomg'ir yog'ayotganiga ham, yog'mayotganiga ham rozi bo'lding. Bunday qilib bo'lmaydi! Toshbaqa: Nega bo'lmaydi? Men juda moslashuvchanman. Axilles: Chunki unda men istalgan narsani isbotlay olardim. Qara: yomg'ir yog'yapti, demak «yomg'ir yog'yapti yoki sen menga tort qarzdorsan» haqiqat. Lekin yomg'ir yog'mayapti — demak, sen menga tort qarzdorsan! Toshbaqa: Voy-bo'y. Axilles: Xuddi shu hiyla bilan sen menga saroy qarzdorsan. Toshbaqa: Mayli, mayli, gaplarimdan birini qaytarib olaman. Axilles: Ko'rdingmi? Bitta ziddiyat — va butun dunyo sotuvda.

quiz.q: What does the fantasy rule allow you to do?
o: Assume P, derive Q, and then write 'if P then Q' in the real world
quiz.why_uz: Faraz qilib, keltirib chiqarib, <P⊃Q> bilan chiqish.

quiz.q: Why is a single contradiction so dangerous?
o: From a contradiction any statement can be derived
quiz.why_uz: Ziddiyatdan hamma narsa kelib chiqadi — «isbotlanadigan» ma'nosini yo'qotadi.

quiz.q: What can the propositional calculus NOT express?
o: What is inside statements, like 'every number has a successor'
quiz.why_uz: U gaplarni bo'linmas atomlar sifatida ko'radi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bob «va», «yoki», «agar... unda» va «emas» kabi mantiqiy so'zlarni formal tizim sifatida quradi. Hofstadter qoidalarni — birlashtirish, ajratish, qo'sh inkor, «xayol» (fantaziya) qoidasi, ajratib olish (modus ponens), kontrapozitsiya, De Morgan qoidasi va boshqalarni tushuntiradi, ziddiyat bo'lsa nima uchun hamma narsani isbotlash mumkinligini ko'rsatadi va mantiq ham mexanik o'yin bo'la olishini ta'kidlaydi.
chapters.note_uz: «Xayol qoidasi» (fantasy rule) — V bobdagi push va pop g'oyasining mantiqdagi ko'rinishi: «faraz qilaylik» deb xayolga kirasiz, nimanidir keltirib chiqarasiz va «agar... unda» xulosa bilan chiqasiz.

chapters.title: Chapter VIII: Typographical Number Theory
chapters.title_uz: VIII bob: Tipografik sonlar nazariyasi

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter VIII is called 'Crab Canon', after one of the canons in Bach's Musical Offering in which the melody is played forwards and backwards at the same time. Hofstadter's dialogue does the same with words: its lines read the same from the beginning to the middle as from the end back to the middle. Achilles speaks the Tortoise's lines in reverse order. Escher drew a picture with the same name, with crabs marching in both directions, and Hofstadter notes that palindromic patterns also appear in the structure of DNA.
paras.uz: VIII bobdan oldingi dialog Baxning «Musiqiy tortiq»idagi kuy bir vaqtda oldinga va orqaga chalinadigan kanonlardan biri sharafiga «Qisqichbaqa kanoni» deb ataladi. Hofstadter dialogi so'zlar bilan xuddi shunday qiladi: uning satrlari boshidan o'rtasigacha xuddi oxiridan o'rtasigacha o'qilgandek bir xil. Axilles Toshbaqaning satrlarini teskari tartibda aytadi. Escher ham xuddi shu nomli, qisqichbaqalar ikki yo'nalishda yurgan rasm chizgan va Hofstadter palindromik naqshlar DNK tuzilishida ham uchrashini qayd etadi.

paras.en: The chapter now builds the most important formal system of Part I: Typographical Number Theory, or TNT. Its purpose is to express any statement of ordinary arithmetic — about whole numbers, addition and multiplication — as a string of symbols. Numbers are written using 0 and the symbol S, which means 'the successor of', that is, 'the next number'. So S0 is 1, SS0 is 2, SSS0 is 3, and so on. These are called numerals. It is clumsy, but it uses only two symbols to name every natural number.
paras.uz: Endi bob I qismning eng muhim formal tizimini quradi: Tipografik sonlar nazariyasi yoki TNT. Uning maqsadi oddiy arifmetikaning har qanday gapini — butun sonlar, qo'shish va ko'paytirish haqida — belgilar qatori sifatida ifodalash. Sonlar 0 va «keyingisi», ya'ni «navbatdagi son» degan ma'noni beradigan S belgisi yordamida yoziladi. Shunday qilib S0 — 1, SS0 — 2, SSS0 — 3 va hokazo. Ular raqam-nomlar (numerallar) deb ataladi. Bu noqulay, lekin har bir natural sonni nomlash uchun faqat ikkita belgidan foydalanadi.

paras.en: TNT also has variables, written a, b, c, and when more are needed a′, a′′ and so on. It has + for addition, · for multiplication, = for equality, and parentheses. So (S0+S0)=SS0 is the TNT way of saying '1 plus 1 equals 2'. It includes all the connectives of the propositional calculus — ∧, ∨, ⊃, ~ — so complex statements can be built. And, crucially, it has two quantifiers: ∀a: meaning 'for all a', and ∃a: meaning 'there exists an a such that'. With these, TNT can say things about all numbers or about some numbers.
paras.uz: TNT da shuningdek a, b, c deb yoziladigan, ko'proq kerak bo'lganda a′, a′′ va hokazo o'zgaruvchilar bor. Unda qo'shish uchun +, ko'paytirish uchun ·, tenglik uchun = va qavslar bor. Shunday qilib (S0+S0)=SS0 — «1 plus 1 teng 2» deyishning TNT usuli. U mulohazalar hisobining barcha bog'lovchilarini — ∧, ∨, ⊃, ~ — o'z ichiga oladi, shuning uchun murakkab gaplarni qurish mumkin. Va, eng muhimi, unda ikkita kvantor bor: «barcha a uchun» degan ∀a: va «shunday a mavjudki» degan ∃a:. Ular bilan TNT barcha sonlar yoki ba'zi sonlar haqida gapira oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter gives exercises in translation. 'a is even' becomes ∃b:(SS0·b)=a — there exists a b such that 2 times b equals a. 'There is no largest number' becomes ∀a:∃b:... with a suitable relation. 'b is a power of two' is surprisingly hard to express, and he leaves it as a puzzle. The point is that TNT is rich enough to express statements like Fermat's Last Theorem or the conjecture that every even number greater than two is the sum of two primes. Any question of arithmetic becomes the question: is this string a theorem of TNT?
paras.uz: Hofstadter tarjima mashqlarini beradi. «a juft» ∃b:(SS0·b)=a ga aylanadi — shunday b mavjudki, 2 karra b teng a. «Eng katta son yo'q» mos munosabat bilan ∀a:∃b:... ga aylanadi. «b ikkining darajasi» ni ifodalash hayratlanarli darajada qiyin va u buni jumboq sifatida qoldiradi. Gap shundaki, TNT Fermaning buyuk teoremasi yoki ikkidan katta har bir juft son ikkita tub sonning yig'indisi degan gipoteza kabi gaplarni ifodalash uchun yetarlicha boy. Arifmetikaning har qanday savoli savolga aylanadi: bu qator TNT teoremasimi?

paras.en: What are the axioms? Hofstadter gives five, based on the work of the Italian mathematician Giuseppe Peano. Axiom 1: ∀a:~Sa=0 — zero is not the successor of any number. Axiom 2: ∀a:(a+0)=a. Axiom 3: ∀a:∀b:(a+Sb)=S(a+b) — this defines addition step by step. Axiom 4: ∀a:(a·0)=0. Axiom 5: ∀a:∀b:(a·Sb)=((a·b)+a) — this defines multiplication through addition. These five strings, together with rules, are supposed to capture everything about the natural numbers.
paras.uz: Aksiomalar qanday? Hofstadter italiyalik matematik Juzeppe Peano ishiga asoslangan beshtasini beradi. 1-aksioma: ∀a:~Sa=0 — nol hech qanday sonning keyingisi emas. 2-aksioma: ∀a:(a+0)=a. 3-aksioma: ∀a:∀b:(a+Sb)=S(a+b) — bu qo'shishni qadam-baqadam ta'riflaydi. 4-aksioma: ∀a:(a·0)=0. 5-aksioma: ∀a:∀b:(a·Sb)=((a·b)+a) — bu ko'paytirishni qo'shish orqali ta'riflaydi. Bu beshta qator qoidalar bilan birga natural sonlar haqidagi hamma narsani qamrab olishi kerak.

paras.en: The rules include all those of the propositional calculus, plus new ones for quantifiers and equality. Specification: from ∀a:(something about a), you may write the same thing about any particular number — what is true of all is true of each. Generalisation: if something has been proved about a with no special assumptions, you may write ∀a: in front of it. Interchange: ∀a:~ can be turned into ~∃a: and back — 'for all a, not' equals 'there is no a'. There are rules for symmetry and transitivity of equality, and for adding or dropping an S on both sides.
paras.uz: Qoidalar mulohazalar hisobining barcha qoidalarini, shuningdek kvantorlar va tenglik uchun yangilarini o'z ichiga oladi. Xoslashtirish: ∀a:(a haqida biror narsa) dan siz xuddi shu narsani istalgan aniq son haqida yozishingiz mumkin — barchasi uchun haqiqiy narsa har biri uchun haqiqiy. Umumlashtirish: agar a haqida hech qanday maxsus farazsiz nimadir isbotlangan bo'lsa, uning oldiga ∀a: yozishingiz mumkin. Almashtirish: ∀a:~ ni ~∃a: ga va orqaga aylantirish mumkin — «barcha a uchun, emas» «hech qanday a yo'q» ga teng. Tenglikning simmetriyasi va tranzitivligi, ikkala tomonga S qo'shish yoki olib tashlash uchun qoidalar bor.

paras.en: Hofstadter then demonstrates a curious weakness. Without one more rule, TNT can prove (0+0)=0, and (0+S0)=S0, and (0+SS0)=SS0, and so on — one theorem for every specific number. But it cannot prove the general statement ∀a:(0+a)=a, even though every individual instance is a theorem. He calls this ω-incompleteness (omega-incompleteness): the system proves each case but cannot jump to 'all cases'. A human sees the pattern immediately; the system, working mechanically, cannot make the leap.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter g'alati zaiflikni namoyish etadi. Yana bitta qoidasiz TNT (0+0)=0 ni, (0+S0)=S0 ni, (0+SS0)=SS0 ni va hokazoni — har bir aniq son uchun bitta teoremani isbotlay oladi. Lekin u umumiy ∀a:(0+a)=a gapini isbotlay olmaydi, garchi har bir alohida holat teorema bo'lsa ham. U buni ω-to'liqsizlik (omega-to'liqsizlik) deb ataydi: tizim har bir holatni isbotlaydi, lekin «barcha holatlar»ga sakray olmaydi. Inson naqshni darhol ko'radi; mexanik ishlayotgan tizim esa sakrashni amalga oshira olmaydi.

paras.en: The solution is the rule of induction, the formal version of a familiar argument. If you can prove that a statement holds for 0, and you can prove that whenever it holds for some a it also holds for Sa (the next number), then you may conclude that it holds for all a. It is like a line of dominoes: if the first falls, and each one knocks over the next, they all fall. With induction added, TNT can prove ∀a:(0+a)=a and much more. It becomes, as far as anyone could tell in the 1920s, a complete formalisation of arithmetic.
paras.uz: Yechim — induksiya qoidasi, tanish dalilning formal shakli. Agar gap 0 uchun bajarilishini isbotlay olsangiz va u qandaydir a uchun bajarilganda Sa (keyingi son) uchun ham bajarilishini isbotlay olsangiz, unda u barcha a uchun bajariladi degan xulosa chiqarishingiz mumkin. Bu domino qatoriga o'xshaydi: agar birinchisi yiqilsa va har biri keyingisini yiqitsa, hammasi yiqiladi. Induksiya qo'shilgach, TNT ∀a:(0+a)=a ni va yana ko'p narsani isbotlay oladi. U 1920-yillarda hech kim ayta olganicha, arifmetikaning to'liq formallashuviga aylanadi.

paras.en: But the lesson of ω-incompleteness stays with us. A system can be complete for every particular case and still miss a general truth, until a new kind of rule is added. And Gödel will show that no matter how many rules are added — induction included — there will always be a general truth that slips through. Hofstadter ends the chapter by insisting that TNT, though it looks like a dry game of symbols, is a mirror of number theory. Every true statement of arithmetic has a string in TNT; the question is whether that string can be produced.
paras.uz: Lekin ω-to'liqsizlik saboqi biz bilan qoladi. Tizim har bir alohida holat uchun to'liq bo'lishi va baribir yangi turdagi qoida qo'shilmaguncha umumiy haqiqatni o'tkazib yuborishi mumkin. Va Gödel qancha qoida qo'shilmasin — jumladan induksiya — doim sirg'alib o'tib ketadigan umumiy haqiqat bo'lishini ko'rsatadi. Hofstadter bobni TNT, garchi belgilarning quruq o'yiniga o'xshasa ham, sonlar nazariyasining ko'zgusi ekanini ta'kidlash bilan tugatadi. Arifmetikaning har bir haqiqiy gapi TNT da qatorga ega; savol — bu qatorni hosil qilish mumkinmi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I can prove 0 + 1 = 1, and 0 + 2 = 2, and 0 + 3 = 3... I've done the first thousand! Tortoise: And 0 + a = a for every a? Achilles: Obviously. Tortoise: Then prove it. Achilles: I just did — a thousand times. Tortoise: A thousand is not 'every'. Achilles: Then I'll do a million. Tortoise: Still not every. You need a different kind of step: show it for 0, show that each case pushes over the next. Achilles: Like dominoes! Tortoise: Like dominoes. One clever rule instead of infinitely many tired evenings.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men 0 + 1 = 1 ni, 0 + 2 = 2 ni, 0 + 3 = 3 ni isbotlay olaman... Birinchi mingtasini qildim! Toshbaqa: Va har bir a uchun 0 + a = a ni? Axilles: Aniq. Toshbaqa: Unda isbotla. Axilles: Hozirgina isbotladim — ming marta. Toshbaqa: Ming — «har bir» emas. Axilles: Unda millionta qilaman. Toshbaqa: Baribir har bir emas. Senga boshqa turdagi qadam kerak: 0 uchun ko'rsat, har bir holat keyingisini yiqitishini ko'rsat. Axilles: Domino kabi! Toshbaqa: Domino kabi. Cheksiz ko'p charchagan oqshomlar o'rniga bitta aqlli qoida.

quiz.q: How is the number 3 written in TNT?
quiz.why_uz: S — «keyingisi», shunday qilib SSS0 — 3.

quiz.q: What is ω-incompleteness?
o: The system proves every particular case but not the general statement
quiz.why_uz: Har bir holat isbotlanadi, lekin «barcha holatlar» emas.

quiz.q: What does the rule of induction allow?
o: Concluding a statement holds for all a if it holds for 0 and passes from each a to Sa

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Qisqichbaqa kanoni» dialogi oldindan ham, orqadan ham bir xil o'qiladi. Bob esa butun arifmetikani ifodalay oladigan formal tizim — TNT (Tipografik sonlar nazariyasi)ni quradi: 0, S (keyingi son), qo'shish va ko'paytirish, o'zgaruvchilar, «barcha» va «mavjud» kvantorlari, Peano aksiomalari va induksiya qoidasi. Gödel jumlasi aynan shu tizimda quriladi.
chapters.note_uz: TNT belgilaridan qo'rqmang: SSS0 shunchaki «3», ∀a: «barcha a uchun», ∃a: «shunday a mavjudki». Asosiysi — har qanday arifmetik gapni bu belgilar bilan yozish mumkinligi.

chapters.title: Chapter IX: Mumon and Gödel
chapters.title_uz: IX bob: Mumon va Gödel

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter IX, 'A Mu Offering', brings Achilles, the Tortoise and the Crab together to talk about Zen Buddhism. They discuss koans — short, puzzling stories or questions used by Zen teachers to shake their students out of ordinary ways of thinking. The most famous is about the Chinese master Joshu. A monk asks him whether a dog has Buddha-nature. Joshu answers with a single word: 'Mu'. In Japanese 'mu' can mean 'no' or 'nothing', but here it seems to reject the question itself — to say that it was badly asked.
paras.uz: IX bobdan oldingi «Mu tortig'i» dialogi Axilles, Toshbaqa va Qisqichbaqani Zen-buddizm haqida gaplashish uchun yig'adi. Ular koanlarni — Zen ustozlari shogirdlarini oddiy fikrlash usullaridan silkitib chiqarish uchun ishlatadigan qisqa, chalkash hikoyalar yoki savollarni muhokama qilishadi. Eng mashhuri — xitoylik ustoz Joshu haqida. Bir rohib undan itning Budda tabiati bormi, deb so'raydi. Joshu bitta so'z bilan javob beradi: «Mu». Yapon tilida «mu» «yo'q» yoki «hech narsa» degan ma'noni berishi mumkin, lekin bu yerda u savolning o'zini rad etayotganga — u noto'g'ri qo'yilgan deyayotganga o'xshaydi.

paras.en: Hofstadter notes the delightful coincidence: 'MU' is also the string that cannot be produced in the MIU-system. The answer 'Mu' in Zen 'unasks' a question; the string MU in the MIU-system is an unreachable goal. Both point to the limits of a system. The chapter explains that Mumon, a Chinese monk of the thirteenth century, collected forty-eight koans with his own comments in a book known as The Gateless Gate. Zen, Hofstadter says, is suspicious of words and logic; it tries to reach understanding by stepping outside every system of thought.
paras.uz: Hofstadter yoqimli tasodifni qayd etadi: «MU» — MIU-tizimida hosil qilib bo'lmaydigan qator ham. Zendagi «Mu» javobi savolni «so'ralmagan» qiladi; MIU-tizimidagi MU qatori — yetib bo'lmas maqsad. Ikkalasi ham tizim chegaralariga ishora qiladi. Bob XIII asrda yashagan xitoylik rohib Mumon qirq sakkizta koanni o'z izohlari bilan «Darvozasiz darvoza» nomi bilan mashhur kitobga to'plaganini tushuntiradi. Zen, deydi Hofstadter, so'zlar va mantiqqa shubha bilan qaraydi; u har qanday fikrlash tizimidan tashqariga chiqish orqali tushunishga erishishga intiladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter is fascinated but cautious. Zen teaches that every attempt to describe enlightenment in words fails, because words divide the world into categories — this and that, self and other — and enlightenment, Zen says, lies beyond such divisions. This is a kind of 'jumping out of the system' taken to an extreme. Yet Hofstadter observes that Zen can never fully escape, because even 'there is no system' becomes a kind of system, and even silence can be a statement. Every attempt to step outside creates a new level that can be stepped out of again.
paras.uz: Hofstadter maftun bo'ladi, lekin ehtiyotkor. Zen ma'rifatni so'zlar bilan tasvirlashga har qanday urinish muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'ladi, deb o'rgatadi, chunki so'zlar dunyoni toifalarga — bu va u, men va boshqa — ajratadi, ma'rifat esa, Zen aytishicha, bunday bo'linishlardan tashqarida. Bu chekkaga olib borilgan o'ziga xos «tizimdan sakrab chiqish». Shunga qaramay Hofstadter Zen hech qachon to'liq qocha olmasligini kuzatadi, chunki hatto «tizim yo'q» ham o'ziga xos tizimga aylanadi va hatto sukunat ham gap bo'lishi mumkin. Tashqariga chiqishga har bir urinish yana undan chiqib ketish mumkin bo'lgan yangi daraja yaratadi.

paras.en: Then the chapter changes gear completely. Hofstadter shows how Gödel turned statements about strings into statements about numbers, using the MIU-system as a practice case. Give each symbol a digit: M = 3, I = 1, U = 0. Then every string becomes a number: MI is 31, MIU is 310, MU is 30, MIIU is 3110. This is Gödel numbering in miniature. Nothing has changed except the notation, but now we can treat strings as numbers and the MIU rules as arithmetical operations on numbers.
paras.uz: Keyin bob tezlikni butunlay o'zgartiradi. Hofstadter Gödel qatorlar haqidagi gaplarni qanday qilib sonlar haqidagi gaplarga aylantirganini MIU-tizimini mashq namunasi sifatida ishlatib ko'rsatadi. Har bir belgiga raqam bering: M = 3, I = 1, U = 0. Shunda har bir qator songa aylanadi: MI — 31, MIU — 310, MU — 30, MIIU — 3110. Bu kichik ko'rinishdagi Gödel raqamlash. Yozuvdan boshqa hech narsa o'zgarmadi, lekin endi qatorlarni sonlar sifatida, MIU qoidalarini esa sonlar ustidagi arifmetik amallar sifatida ko'rib chiqishimiz mumkin.

paras.en: For example, Rule I says: if a string ends in I, add U. In numbers: if a number ends in the digit 1, multiply it by 10. Rule II, doubling everything after the M, becomes a more complicated but still purely arithmetical operation on the digits. Rule III, replacing III with U, means replacing the digits 111 with 0 somewhere in the number. Each typographical rule becomes an arithmetical rule. The set of numbers you can reach from 31 using these rules Hofstadter calls the 'MIU-numbers'.
paras.uz: Masalan, I qoida aytadi: agar qator I bilan tugasa, U qo'sh. Sonlarda: agar son 1 raqami bilan tugasa, uni 10 ga ko'paytir. M dan keyingi hamma narsani ikki baravar qiladigan II qoida raqamlar ustidagi murakkabroq, lekin baribir sof arifmetik amalga aylanadi. III ni U bilan almashtiradigan III qoida sonning biror joyida 111 raqamlarini 0 bilan almashtirish demak. Har bir tipografik qoida arifmetik qoidaga aylanadi. Bu qoidalar yordamida 31 dan yetib boriladigan sonlar to'plamini Hofstadter «MIU-sonlar» deb ataydi.

paras.en: Now the question 'Is MU a theorem of the MIU-system?' has become 'Is 30 a MIU-number?' — a question of pure number theory. And our earlier proof that MU is unreachable, based on counting I's, is now a proof about numbers and digits. Hofstadter calls such a shift an isomorphism between typography and arithmetic. Anything you can say about the strings, you can say about the numbers, and vice versa. The game of letters and the game of numbers move in perfect step.
paras.uz: Endi «MU MIU-tizimining teoremasimi?» degan savol «30 MIU-sonmi?» degan savolga — sof sonlar nazariyasi savoliga aylandi. Va MU ga yetib bo'lmasligi haqidagi I larni sanashga asoslangan oldingi isbotimiz endi sonlar va raqamlar haqidagi isbotdir. Hofstadter bunday siljishni tipografiya va arifmetika o'rtasidagi izomorfizm deb ataydi. Qatorlar haqida ayta oladigan har qanday narsani sonlar haqida ham ayta olasiz va aksincha. Harflar o'yini va sonlar o'yini mukammal bir maromda harakatlanadi.

paras.en: Here comes the decisive step. TNT can express statements about numbers. MIU-numbers are a set of numbers defined by arithmetical rules. So TNT can express the statement '30 is a MIU-number' as a string. But the same can be done for TNT itself! Give every TNT symbol a code number, and every TNT string becomes a number. The rules of TNT become arithmetical rules. The set of 'TNT-numbers' — the Gödel numbers of TNT theorems — is then a set of numbers that TNT itself can talk about.
paras.uz: Mana hal qiluvchi qadam. TNT sonlar haqidagi gaplarni ifodalay oladi. MIU-sonlar — arifmetik qoidalar bilan ta'riflangan sonlar to'plami. Demak, TNT «30 MIU-son» degan gapni qator sifatida ifodalay oladi. Lekin xuddi shu narsani TNT ning o'zi uchun ham qilish mumkin! Har bir TNT belgisiga kod raqam bering va har bir TNT qatori songa aylanadi. TNT qoidalari arifmetik qoidalarga aylanadi. «TNT-sonlar» to'plami — TNT teoremalarining Gödel raqamlari — shunda TNT ning o'zi gapira oladigan sonlar to'plami bo'ladi.

paras.en: In other words, a string of TNT, read on the level of arithmetic, talks about numbers; but read through Gödel's code, the same string can talk about strings of TNT — including, possibly, itself. TNT, which was designed only to talk about numbers, turns out to be able to talk about its own theorems. This is the moment when the formal system becomes a mirror held up to itself. Hofstadter compares it to a TV camera pointed at the screen it is feeding: suddenly the system contains an image of itself.
paras.uz: Boshqacha aytganda, TNT qatori arifmetika darajasida o'qilganda sonlar haqida gapiradi; lekin Gödel kodi orqali o'qilganda, xuddi shu qator TNT qatorlari haqida — jumladan, ehtimol, o'zi haqida — gapira oladi. Faqat sonlar haqida gapirish uchun mo'ljallangan TNT o'z teoremalari haqida gapira olishi ma'lum bo'ladi. Bu formal tizim o'ziga tutilgan ko'zguga aylanadigan lahza. Hofstadter buni o'zi ma'lumot berayotgan ekranga qaratilgan televizion kameraga qiyoslaydi: birdan tizim o'zining tasvirini o'z ichiga oladi.

paras.en: Part I ends here, on the edge of Gödel's theorem. The second meaning — about strings — is not visible to someone who reads TNT only as arithmetic. It is hidden, like the acrostic in Bach's title, or like the second figure in an Escher tiling. To see it you must notice the isomorphism. Hofstadter calls this kind of double meaning one of the most important ideas in the book: one and the same object can mean two different things at two different levels, and the higher meaning can loop back to describe the lower one.
paras.uz: I qism shu yerda, Gödel teoremasining bo'sag'asida tugaydi. Ikkinchi ma'no — qatorlar haqidagi — TNT ni faqat arifmetika sifatida o'qiydigan odamga ko'rinmaydi. U Bax sarlavhasidagi akrostix yoki Escher naqshidagi ikkinchi shakl kabi yashirin. Uni ko'rish uchun izomorfizmni payqash kerak. Hofstadter bunday qo'sh ma'noni kitobdagi eng muhim g'oyalardan biri deb ataydi: bir va o'sha narsa ikki xil darajada ikki xil narsani anglatishi mumkin va yuqoriroq ma'no pastki ma'noni tasvirlash uchun halqa bo'lib qaytishi mumkin.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Master Tortoise, does the MIU-system have Buddha-nature? Tortoise: Mu. Achilles: You mean no? Tortoise: I mean your question has too few sides. Let me ask instead: is 30 a MIU-number? Achilles: That's a sum question, not a Zen question. Tortoise: Is it? 30 is MU written in digits. Achilles: Oh... so asking whether MU can be made is the same as asking about the number 30. Tortoise: And asking about TNT's theorems is the same as asking about certain numbers — which TNT can talk about. Achilles: Then TNT can talk about itself! Tortoise: Mu.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Ustoz Toshbaqa, MIU-tizimining Budda tabiati bormi? Toshbaqa: Mu. Axilles: Yo'q demoqchimisan? Toshbaqa: Savolingning tomonlari juda kam demoqchiman. Uning o'rniga so'ray: 30 MIU-sonmi? Axilles: Bu hisob savoli, Zen savoli emas. Toshbaqa: Shundaymi? 30 — raqamlar bilan yozilgan MU. Axilles: Oh... demak, MU ni yasash mumkinmi deb so'rash 30 soni haqida so'rash bilan bir xil. Toshbaqa: TNT teoremalari haqida so'rash esa ma'lum sonlar haqida so'rash bilan bir xil — TNT ular haqida gapira oladi. Axilles: Unda TNT o'zi haqida gapira oladi! Toshbaqa: Mu.
