quiz.q: What did Joshu answer when asked whether a dog has Buddha-nature?
quiz.why_uz: «Mu» — savolni rad etuvchi javob.

quiz.q: In the MIU numbering (M=3, I=1, U=0), what number is MU?
quiz.why_uz: M=3, U=0, demak MU = 30.

quiz.q: What is the decisive discovery of this chapter?
o: Through Gödel numbering, TNT can talk about its own theorems
quiz.why_uz: TNT qatorlari Gödel kodi orqali TNT qatorlari haqida gapira oladi.

chapters.recap_uz: I qismning yakuniy bobi ikki mutlaqo boshqa dunyoni yonma-yon qo'yadi: Zen-buddizm koanlari (Mumonning «Darvozasiz darvoza» to'plami va mashhur «Mu» javobi) va Gödel raqamlash. Zen tizimlardan, so'zlar va mantiqdan «sakrab chiqishga» intiladi; Gödel esa tizimni o'z ichida o'zi haqida gapirtiradi. Bob MIU-tizimini sonlarga aylantirib, qatorlar haqidagi savollar qanday qilib sonlar haqidagi savollarga aylanishini ko'rsatadi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob texnik jihatdan juda muhim: «MU teorema emas» degan gap «30 MIU-soni emas» degan sonlar nazariyasi gapiga aylanadi. Gödel butun g'oyasi shu almashtirishga tayanadi.

chapters.title: Chapter X: Levels of description, and computer systems
chapters.title_uz: X bob: Tavsif darajalari va kompyuter tizimlari

paras.en: Part II of the book is called 'EGB' — the same letters, in a different order, as if seen from another side of the cover's carved blocks. It opens with a dialogue in two halves, 'Prelude... Ant Fugue', placed around Chapter X. Achilles, the Tortoise, the Crab and a new character, the Anteater, meet at the Crab's house to listen to preludes and fugues from Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier. While they listen, they discuss how one should hear a fugue: as separate voices, or as a whole? This question of levels is the theme of the whole second part.
paras.uz: Kitobning II qismi «EGB» deb ataladi — xuddi muqovadagi o'yilgan bloklarga boshqa tomondan qaralgandek, xuddi o'sha harflar boshqa tartibda. U X bob atrofiga joylashtirilgan ikki yarimli «Prelyudiya... Chumoli fugasi» dialogi bilan ochiladi. Axilles, Toshbaqa, Qisqichbaqa va yangi qahramon — Chumolixo'r Baxning «Yaxshi temperatsiyalangan klavir»idan prelyudiya va fugalarni tinglash uchun Qisqichbaqaning uyida uchrashadi. Tinglarkan, ular fugani qanday eshitish kerakligini muhokama qilishadi: alohida ovozlar sifatidami yoki butunlik sifatidami? Darajalar haqidagi bu savol butun ikkinchi qismning mavzusi.

paras.en: Chapter X begins with simple examples. A television picture is made of tiny dots of light. At the level of dots there is no face, no story, no smile — just brightness values. Yet at a higher level we see a person laughing. In the same way, a gas is made of billions of molecules moving randomly, but at a higher level we describe it with temperature and pressure, which no single molecule has. These are levels of description: different ways of describing the same system, each with its own concepts and its own laws.
paras.uz: X bob oddiy misollardan boshlanadi. Televizor tasviri yorug'likning mitti nuqtalaridan iborat. Nuqtalar darajasida yuz ham, hikoya ham, tabassum ham yo'q — faqat yorqinlik qiymatlari. Shunga qaramay yuqoriroq darajada biz kulayotgan odamni ko'ramiz. Xuddi shunday, gaz tasodifiy harakatlanayotgan milliardlab molekulalardan iborat, lekin yuqoriroq darajada biz uni hech bir alohida molekulada bo'lmagan harorat va bosim bilan tasvirlaymiz. Bular tavsif darajalari: bir xil tizimni tasvirlashning turli usullari, har biri o'z tushunchalari va o'z qonunlariga ega.

paras.en: Hofstadter then turns to chess. Psychological experiments, especially by the Dutch psychologist Adriaan de Groot, showed that chess masters can glance at a real game position for a few seconds and then reproduce it almost perfectly, while beginners remember only a few pieces. But if the pieces are placed randomly, masters do no better than beginners. The explanation is 'chunking': masters do not see thirty separate pieces; they see a few meaningful groups — a castled king, a pawn chain, an attack. They perceive the board at a higher level.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter shaxmatga o'tadi. Psixologik tajribalar, ayniqsa gollandiyalik psixolog Adriaan de Grot tajribalari, shaxmat ustalari haqiqiy o'yin pozitsiyasiga bir necha soniya qarab, keyin uni deyarli mukammal qayta tiklay olishini ko'rsatdi, yangi boshlovchilar esa faqat bir nechta donani eslaydi. Lekin agar donalar tasodifiy joylashtirilsa, ustalar yangi boshlovchilardan yaxshiroq natija ko'rsatmaydi. Tushuntirish — «bo'laklash» (chunking): ustalar o'ttizta alohida donani ko'rmaydi; ular bir nechta ma'noli guruhni — rokirovka qilingan qirol, piyodalar zanjiri, hujumni ko'radi. Ular taxtani yuqoriroq darajada idrok etadi.

paras.en: Computers offer the clearest example of levels. At the bottom, a computer is electrical circuits; above that, machine language — sequences of 0s and 1s that tell the processor to move or add numbers. Above that is assembly language, in which those instructions have short names. Above that are high-level programming languages, in which a single line may stand for thousands of machine instructions. Programs called compilers and interpreters translate from higher levels down to lower ones. A programmer can think in high-level terms without ever seeing the electrons.
paras.uz: Kompyuterlar darajalarning eng aniq misolini taklif qiladi. Eng pastda kompyuter — elektr zanjirlari; undan yuqorida — mashina tili, protsessorga sonlarni ko'chirish yoki qo'shishni aytadigan 0 va 1 lar ketma-ketligi. Undan yuqorida — assembler tili, unda bu ko'rsatmalar qisqa nomlarga ega. Undan yuqorida — yuqori darajadagi dasturlash tillari, ularda bitta satr minglab mashina ko'rsatmalari o'rnini bosishi mumkin. Kompilyatorlar va interpretatorlar deb ataladigan dasturlar yuqori darajalardan pastkilariga tarjima qiladi. Dasturchi elektronlarni hech qachon ko'rmasdan, yuqori darajadagi tushunchalarda o'ylay oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter describes bootstrapping: how the first compiler for a new language can be written in a simpler language, and then the compiler can be used to rewrite itself in its own language — a kind of loop, like a person lifting himself by his own bootstraps. He also describes operating systems, which manage many programs and users at once. These levels are not just conveniences; they are what make complex behaviour possible. No human could write a word processor in 0s and 1s, but at the right level of description it becomes manageable.
paras.uz: Hofstadter bootstrapping — o'z-o'zini ko'tarishni tasvirlaydi: yangi til uchun birinchi kompilyator soddaroq tilda yozilishi mumkin, keyin kompilyatordan o'zini o'z tilida qayta yozish uchun foydalanish mumkin — o'zini o'z etigining qayishidan tortib ko'targan odam kabi o'ziga xos halqa. U shuningdek ko'plab dasturlar va foydalanuvchilarni bir vaqtda boshqaradigan operatsion tizimlarni tasvirlaydi. Bu darajalar shunchaki qulaylik emas; ular murakkab xatti-harakatni mumkin qiladigan narsa. Hech bir inson matn muharririni 0 va 1 larda yoza olmasdi, lekin to'g'ri tavsif darajasida bu boshqarib bo'ladigan bo'lib qoladi.

paras.en: Now comes a subtle idea: epiphenomena. Suppose an operating system works well with up to 35 users, but becomes very slow with 36. Where is the number 35 stored? Nowhere. There is no line in the program saying 'maximum 35 users'. The limit emerges from the way many small parts interact. Hofstadter calls such a property an epiphenomenon — a feature visible at a high level that is not written anywhere at a low level. A traffic jam, a crowd's mood, and perhaps many features of the mind are like this.
paras.uz: Endi nozik g'oya keladi: epifenomenlar. Faraz qilaylik, operatsion tizim 35 tagacha foydalanuvchi bilan yaxshi ishlaydi, lekin 36 tada juda sekinlashadi. 35 soni qayerda saqlangan? Hech qayerda. Dasturda «maksimal 35 foydalanuvchi» degan satr yo'q. Chegara ko'plab kichik qismlarning o'zaro ta'siri usulidan paydo bo'ladi. Hofstadter bunday xususiyatni epifenomen deb ataydi — yuqori darajada ko'rinadigan, lekin past darajada hech qayerda yozilmagan xususiyat. Tirbandlik, olomon kayfiyati va, ehtimol, aqlning ko'p xususiyatlari shunday.

paras.en: Hofstadter also discusses why levels can often be treated separately. In physics, we can describe an atom without knowing about quarks, and a cell without knowing about atoms in detail, because the levels are only weakly connected — what happens inside a lower unit mostly stays inside it. He calls this 'sealing off'. It is why science works at all: chemists do not need to solve quantum mechanics to mix solutions. But some systems, especially brains, may have levels that interact more strongly, and that makes them harder to understand from either side alone.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek darajalarni nega ko'pincha alohida ko'rib chiqish mumkinligini muhokama qiladi. Fizikada biz atomni kvarklar haqida bilmasdan, hujayrani esa atomlar haqida batafsil bilmasdan tasvirlay olamiz, chunki darajalar faqat zaif bog'langan — pastki birlik ichida sodir bo'ladigan narsa asosan uning ichida qoladi. U buni «muhrlanish» deb ataydi. Fan umuman ishlashining sababi shu: kimyogarlar eritmalarni aralashtirish uchun kvant mexanikasini yechishlari shart emas. Lekin ba'zi tizimlar, ayniqsa miyalar, kuchliroq ta'sirlashadigan darajalarga ega bo'lishi mumkin va bu ularni har qaysi tomondan alohida tushunishni qiyinlashtiradi.

paras.en: The chapter connects these ideas to the big debate between reductionism and holism. Reductionism says: to understand a whole, understand its parts. Holism says: the whole is more than the sum of its parts. Hofstadter, through the dialogue, gives a typically Zen answer — 'Mu' — to the question 'which is right?' Both are needed. The parts determine everything, but the explanation of the whole may only make sense in higher-level concepts. Neurons determine thoughts, but 'thought' is not a word that belongs to the vocabulary of neurons.
paras.uz: Bob bu g'oyalarni reduksionizm va xolizm o'rtasidagi katta bahs bilan bog'laydi. Reduksionizm aytadi: butunni tushunish uchun uning qismlarini tushun. Xolizm aytadi: butun uning qismlari yig'indisidan ko'proq. Hofstadter dialog orqali «qaysi biri to'g'ri?» degan savolga odatiy Zen javobini — «Mu» ni beradi. Ikkalasi ham kerak. Qismlar hamma narsani belgilaydi, lekin butunning tushuntirishi faqat yuqoriroq darajadagi tushunchalarda ma'noga ega bo'lishi mumkin. Neyronlar fikrlarni belgilaydi, lekin «fikr» neyronlar lug'atiga tegishli so'z emas.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I've been studying this painting through a magnifying glass for an hour. Dots. Yellow dots, blue dots, a few red ones. Tortoise: And the painting? Achilles: What painting? It's all dots! Tortoise: Step back three paces. Achilles: ...Oh. It's a boat. On a river. At sunset. Tortoise: Where was the sunset, among the dots? Achilles: Nowhere — and everywhere. Tortoise: Remember that answer. When people tell you the mind is 'just neurons', they are looking through your magnifying glass.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men bir soatdan beri bu rasmni lupa orqali o'rganyapman. Nuqtalar. Sariq nuqtalar, ko'k nuqtalar, bir nechta qizil. Toshbaqa: Rasm-chi? Axilles: Qanday rasm? Hammasi nuqtalar! Toshbaqa: Uch qadam orqaga chekin. Axilles: ...Oh. Bu qayiq. Daryoda. Quyosh botishida. Toshbaqa: Quyosh botishi nuqtalar orasida qayerda edi? Axilles: Hech qayerda — va hamma joyda. Toshbaqa: Bu javobni eslab qol. Odamlar senga aql «shunchaki neyronlar» deyishganda, ular sening lupang orqali qarayotgan bo'ladi.

o: They perceive meaningful chunks rather than separate pieces
quiz.why_uz: Ustalar donalarni ma'noli guruhlar — bo'laklar sifatida idrok etadi.

chapters.recap_uz: II qism («EGB») shu bob bilan boshlanadi. Bob bir xil narsani turli darajalarda tasvirlash mumkinligini ko'rsatadi: televizor ekranidagi nuqtalar va tasvir, gaz molekulalari va harorat, shaxmat ustasi ko'radigan «bo'laklar», kompyuterdagi mashina tili, assembler, kompilyatorlar va operatsion tizim. Asosiy g'oya: yuqori darajadagi xususiyatlar pastki darajada hech qayerda yozilmagan bo'lishi mumkin — ular paydo bo'luvchi (emergent) hodisalar.
chapters.note_uz: II qismning butun mantiqi shu bobga tayanadi: «men»ni tushunish uchun uni neyronlar darajasida emas, balki ancha yuqori darajada izlash kerak, xuddi tirbandlikni alohida mashinada emas, butun ko'chada ko'rish kerak bo'lgani kabi.

chapters.title: Ant Fugue and Chapter XI: Brains and thoughts
chapters.title_uz: Chumoli fugasi va XI bob: Miya va fikrlar

paras.en: The second half of the dialogue, '...Ant Fugue', is one of the most celebrated passages in the book. The Anteater tells the others that he regularly visits a friend called Aunt Hillary — who is not an ant, but an entire ant colony. Achilles is shocked: surely an anteater is the enemy of ants? The Anteater explains that he is more like a surgeon: by eating a few ants in the right places, he helps the colony think more clearly. And the colony, as a whole, enjoys his conversation. He 'talks' to it by tracing patterns in the nest, and it answers by the way its ants arrange themselves.
paras.uz: Dialogning ikkinchi yarmi — «...Chumoli fugasi» kitobdagi eng mashhur parchalardan biri. Chumolixo'r boshqalarga Xilari xola ismli do'stini muntazam ziyorat qilishini aytadi — u chumoli emas, balki butun bir chumoli koloniyasi. Axilles hayratda: chumolixo'r chumolilarning dushmani emasmi? Chumolixo'r o'zi ko'proq jarrohga o'xshashini tushuntiradi: to'g'ri joylardagi bir nechta chumolini yeb, u koloniyaga aniqroq fikrlashga yordam beradi. Koloniya esa butunligicha uning suhbatidan zavqlanadi. U uyada naqshlar chizib u bilan «gaplashadi», koloniya esa chumolilarining joylashuvi orqali javob beradi.

paras.en: The key idea of the Ant Fugue is levels. A single ant is very stupid: it follows simple chemical signals, wanders, carries things, reacts to neighbours. Nothing that one ant does could be called thinking. But ants form temporary groups that Hofstadter calls 'teams', and teams of teams, and these larger patterns move around the colony like messages. At the top level, the colony's state — the distribution of all these groups — encodes information about the world. Aunt Hillary 'knows' things that no ant knows, just as you know things that none of your neurons knows.
paras.uz: Chumoli fugasining asosiy g'oyasi — darajalar. Bitta chumoli juda ahmoq: u oddiy kimyoviy signallarga ergashadi, kezadi, narsalarni tashiydi, qo'shnilariga javob beradi. Bitta chumoli qiladigan hech narsani fikrlash deb atab bo'lmaydi. Lekin chumolilar Hofstadter «jamoalar» deb ataydigan vaqtinchalik guruhlarni, jamoalar jamoalarini hosil qiladi va bu kattaroq naqshlar koloniya bo'ylab xabarlar kabi harakatlanadi. Eng yuqori darajada koloniya holati — bu barcha guruhlarning taqsimlanishi — dunyo haqidagi ma'lumotni kodlaydi. Xilari xola hech bir chumoli bilmaydigan narsalarni «biladi», xuddi siz hech bir neyroningiz bilmaydigan narsalarni bilganingiz kabi.

paras.en: The dialogue makes several deep points in a playful way. The colony's 'thoughts' are not located in any particular ant; they exist in the pattern. Ants come and go, die and are replaced, but Aunt Hillary remains the same personality, just as your atoms are replaced over the years while you remain yourself. The dialogue also asks whether the colony is aware of its ants, and whether the ants are aware of the colony. The answer is no in both directions — the levels are almost sealed off from each other, except at certain points.
paras.uz: Dialog o'ynoqi tarzda bir nechta chuqur fikrlarni bildiradi. Koloniyaning «fikrlari» biror alohida chumolida joylashmagan; ular naqshda mavjud. Chumolilar kelib-ketadi, o'ladi va almashtiriladi, lekin Xilari xola bir xil shaxs bo'lib qoladi, xuddi yillar davomida atomlaringiz almashsa ham, siz o'zingiz bo'lib qolganingiz kabi. Dialog shuningdek koloniya o'z chumolilarini anglaydimi va chumolilar koloniyani anglaydimi, deb so'raydi. Javob ikkala yo'nalishda ham yo'q — darajalar ma'lum nuqtalardan tashqari bir-biridan deyarli muhrlangan.

paras.en: Chapter XI applies these ideas to the real brain. Hofstadter describes neurons: cells with many branches that receive signals from thousands of other neurons. If the total input is strong enough, a neuron 'fires', sending an electrical pulse along its axon to other neurons. The human brain has tens of billions of neurons and an enormous number of connections. Each neuron is a simple device, more complex than an ant but just as mindless. The question is how such simple units, all working together, produce memories, ideas and a sense of self.
paras.uz: XI bob bu g'oyalarni haqiqiy miyaga tatbiq etadi. Hofstadter neyronlarni tasvirlaydi: minglab boshqa neyronlardan signallar oladigan ko'p shoxli hujayralar. Agar umumiy kirish yetarlicha kuchli bo'lsa, neyron «otadi» — o'z aksoni bo'ylab boshqa neyronlarga elektr impulsini yuboradi. Inson miyasida o'nlab milliardlab neyronlar va ulkan miqdordagi bog'lanishlar bor. Har bir neyron — oddiy qurilma, chumolidan murakkabroq, lekin xuddi shunday aqlsiz. Savol — bunday oddiy birliklar birgalikda ishlab, qanday qilib xotiralar, g'oyalar va «men» tuyg'usini hosil qiladi.

paras.en: Where in the brain is a memory stored? Hofstadter discusses the American psychologist Karl Lashley, who trained rats to run mazes and then removed different parts of their brains, searching for the place where the memory of the maze was kept. He never found it: the rats lost skill gradually, depending on how much tissue was removed, not where. On the other hand, the Canadian surgeon Wilder Penfield found that stimulating certain points of a patient's brain during surgery could bring back vivid memories. Memory seems to be both spread out and, in some way, localised.
paras.uz: Xotira miyaning qayerida saqlanadi? Hofstadter kalamushlarni labirintdan yugurishga o'rgatib, keyin labirint xotirasi saqlanadigan joyni izlab, ularning miyasining turli qismlarini olib tashlagan amerikalik psixolog Karl Lashlini muhokama qiladi. U uni hech qachon topmagan: kalamushlar qaysi joydan emas, qancha to'qima olib tashlanganiga qarab, mahoratni asta-sekin yo'qotgan. Boshqa tomondan, kanadalik jarroh Uaylder Penfild operatsiya paytida bemor miyasining ma'lum nuqtalarini qo'zg'atish yorqin xotiralarni qaytarishi mumkinligini topgan. Xotira ham tarqalgan, ham qandaydir tarzda mahalliylashgandek ko'rinadi.

paras.en: To make sense of this, Hofstadter introduces his key concept: symbols. In his sense, a symbol is not a written sign but an active structure in the brain — a pattern of neural activity that corresponds to a concept, such as 'dog', 'running' or 'my grandmother'. When you think of a dog, the 'dog' symbol becomes active. Symbols are made of neurons, just as Aunt Hillary's signals are made of ants, but they live at a higher level. They can be partly overlapping, spread across many neurons, and still act as units.
paras.uz: Buni tushunish uchun Hofstadter o'zining asosiy tushunchasini kiritadi: belgilar (symbols). Uning ma'nosida belgi — yozma belgi emas, balki miyadagi faol tuzilma — «it», «yugurish» yoki «buvim» kabi tushunchaga mos keladigan neyron faoliyati naqshi. Siz it haqida o'ylaganingizda, «it» belgisi faollashadi. Belgilar neyronlardan tashkil topgan, xuddi Xilari xolaning signallari chumolilardan tashkil topgani kabi, lekin ular yuqoriroq darajada yashaydi. Ular qisman bir-birining ustiga tushishi, ko'plab neyronlarga tarqalishi va baribir birlik sifatida harakat qilishi mumkin.

paras.en: Symbols trigger one another. Thinking of 'rain' may activate 'umbrella', 'clouds', 'wet streets', 'a sad song'. Hofstadter suggests that thinking is the flow of activation among symbols, following the connections built up by experience. He distinguishes class symbols, such as 'dog' in general, from instance symbols, such as 'my neighbour's dog Rex'. Instances can be created on the fly by copying and modifying class symbols. This flexibility lets us imagine things we have never seen — a purple dog, a talking tortoise — by combining symbols in new ways.
paras.uz: Belgilar bir-birini qo'zg'atadi. «Yomg'ir» haqida o'ylash «soyabon», «bulutlar», «ho'l ko'chalar», «g'amgin qo'shiq»ni faollashtirishi mumkin. Hofstadter fikrlash tajriba qurgan bog'lanishlar bo'ylab belgilar orasidagi faollashuv oqimi ekanini taklif qiladi. U umuman «it» kabi sinf belgilarini «qo'shnimning iti Reks» kabi nusxa belgilaridan ajratadi. Nusxalarni sinf belgilarini nusxalash va o'zgartirish orqali shu zahoti yaratish mumkin. Bu moslashuvchanlik bizga belgilarni yangi usullarda birlashtirib, hech qachon ko'rmagan narsalarni — binafsha itni, gapiradigan toshbaqani — tasavvur qilishga imkon beradi.

paras.en: The chapter ends by connecting the brain to the main theme. If symbols are high-level patterns in a sea of neurons, then the brain is a system with many levels, like the colony. Among all the symbols there may be one very special symbol: a symbol for the self — a pattern that represents the whole system that contains it. That self-symbol would be a strange loop: a part of the brain that stands for the brain. Hofstadter does not develop this fully yet, but he plants the seed that will grow into the final chapter of the book.
paras.uz: Bob miyani asosiy mavzu bilan bog'lash bilan tugaydi. Agar belgilar neyronlar dengizidagi yuqori darajali naqshlar bo'lsa, unda miya koloniya kabi ko'p darajali tizim. Barcha belgilar orasida bitta juda alohida belgi bo'lishi mumkin: «men» uchun belgi — uni o'z ichiga olgan butun tizimni ifodalaydigan naqsh. Bu «men» belgisi g'alati halqa bo'lardi: miyani ifodalaydigan miya qismi. Hofstadter buni hali to'liq rivojlantirmaydi, lekin kitobning so'nggi bobiga aylanadigan urug'ni ekadi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Your friend Aunt Hillary sends her regards, says the Anteater. But Tortoise, which ant sent them? Tortoise: None of them. Ask an ant about Aunt Hillary and it will offer you a crumb. Achilles: Then where are her regards? Tortoise: In the shape of the crowd — the way the busy trails bend and gather. Achilles: Like a word made of people in a stadium? Tortoise: Better: a word that the stadium itself means, though no single person in it can read. Achilles: Then I am a stadium too? Tortoise: A very noisy one.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Do'sting Xilari xola salom yo'llayapti, deydi Chumolixo'r. Lekin, Toshbaqa, salomni qaysi chumoli yubordi? Toshbaqa: Hech biri. Chumolidan Xilari xola haqida so'rasang, u senga ushoq taklif qiladi. Axilles: Unda uning salomi qayerda? Toshbaqa: Olomonning shaklida — band yo'laklarning qanday egilib, to'planishida. Axilles: Stadiondagi odamlardan yasalgan so'z kabimi? Toshbaqa: Yaxshiroq: stadionning o'zi anglatadigan, lekin undagi hech bir odam o'qiy olmaydigan so'z. Axilles: Unda men ham stadionmanmi? Toshbaqa: Juda shovqinli stadion.

chapters.recap_uz: Kitobning eng mashhur dialoglaridan biri — «Chumoli fugasi»: Chumolixo'r butun bir chumoli koloniyasi — Xilari xola bilan suhbatlashadi. Alohida chumolilar ahmoq, lekin koloniya fikrlaydi. Bu tasvir XI bobga ko'prik: neyronlar, ularning o'zaro signallari, xotiraning miyada qayerda saqlanishi va Hofstadterning asosiy tushunchasi — «belgilar» (symbols): miyadagi tushunchalarni ifodalaydigan faol tuzilmalar.
chapters.note_uz: Xilari xola obrazini yodda tuting: chumoli → jamoa → signal → belgi → fikr. Hofstadter uchun miya xuddi shunday ko'p darajali: neyron fikrlamaydi, lekin neyronlar faoliyatining katta naqshlari fikrlaydi.

chapters.title: Chapter XII: Minds and thoughts
chapters.title_uz: XII bob: Aqllar va fikrlar

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XII is unusual: it is not a dialogue at all, but a poem presented in three languages. Lewis Carroll's 'Jabberwocky', from Through the Looking-Glass (1871), is full of invented words — 'brillig', 'slithy toves', 'frumious Bandersnatch' — that sound meaningful without having any dictionary meaning. Hofstadter places it side by side with a French and a German version made by later translators. How can you translate words that do not exist? The translators invented new words in their own languages that create the same feeling.
paras.uz: XII bobdan oldingi dialog g'ayrioddiy: u umuman dialog emas, balki uch tilda taqdim etilgan she'r. Lyuis Kerrolning «Ko'zgu ortida» (1871) kitobidagi «Jabberwocky» she'ri ma'noli eshitiladigan, lekin lug'atda hech qanday ma'nosi bo'lmagan to'qima so'zlarga — «brillig», «slithy toves», «frumious Bandersnatch» — to'la. Hofstadter uni keyingi tarjimonlar qilgan fransuzcha va nemischa versiyalari bilan yonma-yon qo'yadi. Mavjud bo'lmagan so'zlarni qanday tarjima qilish mumkin? Tarjimonlar o'z tillarida xuddi shu tuyg'uni yaratadigan yangi so'zlar o'ylab topishgan.

paras.en: This leads to the chapter's question: to what extent are two minds alike? When you and I both use the word 'dog', are the 'dog' symbols in our brains the same? Hofstadter's answer is: roughly, but not exactly. We share an enormous amount — the same words, the same physical world, much of the same culture. But each of us has built our network of concepts from different experiences. My 'dog' may be linked to a childhood pet, yours to a frightening bite. The overlap is large enough for communication, but it is not a perfect isomorphism.
paras.uz: Bu bob savoliga olib keladi: ikki aql qanchalik o'xshash? Siz va men «it» so'zini ishlatganimizda, miyalarimizdagi «it» belgilari bir xilmi? Hofstadterning javobi: taxminan, lekin aniq emas. Bizda ulkan umumiylik bor — bir xil so'zlar, bir xil fizik dunyo, madaniyatning ko'p qismi. Lekin har birimiz tushunchalar tarmog'imizni turli tajribalardan qurganmiz. Mening «it»im bolalikdagi uy hayvoni bilan, siznikingiz qo'rqinchli tishlash bilan bog'langan bo'lishi mumkin. Umumiylik muloqot uchun yetarlicha katta, lekin u mukammal izomorfizm emas.

paras.en: Hofstadter uses the image of maps. Imagine two people who each draw a map of their country from memory. One knows the motorways well; the other knows the small villages. Both maps will show the capital, the big rivers, the main cities, in roughly the right places. But they will differ in detail, in what is included, in what is connected to what. Two minds are like two such maps: their large-scale structure is similar because they describe the same world, but their fine structure is personal.
paras.uz: Hofstadter xaritalar obrazidan foydalanadi. Har biri o'z mamlakatining xaritasini xotiradan chizgan ikki odamni tasavvur qiling. Biri avtomagistrallarni yaxshi biladi; ikkinchisi kichik qishloqlarni biladi. Ikkala xarita ham poytaxtni, katta daryolarni, asosiy shaharlarni taxminan to'g'ri joylarda ko'rsatadi. Lekin ular tafsilotlarda, nima kiritilganida, nima nima bilan bog'langanida farq qiladi. Ikki aql shunday ikki xaritaga o'xshaydi: ularning katta miqyosdagi tuzilmasi o'xshash, chunki ular bir xil dunyoni tasvirlaydi, lekin nozik tuzilmasi shaxsiy.

paras.en: Translation is the clearest test of this. Hofstadter discusses a passage from Dostoevsky's Crime and Punishment that mentions a particular street in St Petersburg. A Russian reader immediately feels what kind of place it is; an English reader knows nothing. Should the translator keep the Russian name, replace it with a similar London street, or explain? Each choice keeps some meaning and loses some. Good translation is not word-for-word; it looks for an isomorphism at the right level — not between words, but between the experiences the words create.
paras.uz: Tarjima buning eng aniq sinovi. Hofstadter Dostoyevskiyning «Jinoyat va jazo» romanidan Peterburgdagi ma'lum bir ko'chani tilga oladigan parchani muhokama qiladi. Rus o'quvchisi bu qanday joy ekanini darhol his qiladi; ingliz o'quvchisi hech narsa bilmaydi. Tarjimon ruscha nomni saqlashi, uni o'xshash London ko'chasi bilan almashtirishi yoki tushuntirishi kerakmi? Har bir tanlov ma'noning bir qismini saqlaydi, bir qismini yo'qotadi. Yaxshi tarjima so'zma-so'z emas; u to'g'ri darajadagi izomorfizmni izlaydi — so'zlar o'rtasida emas, balki so'zlar yaratadigan tajribalar o'rtasida.

paras.en: Hofstadter then describes a 'semantic network': a web of concepts linked by relations of similarity, part-and-whole, cause and effect, and so on. 'Dog' is linked to 'animal', 'bark', 'tail', 'loyalty', 'cat'. In a mind, such a network is not fixed; links grow stronger or weaker with use, and new concepts are formed by blending old ones. Two people's networks share many of the same nodes and links, which is why they can understand each other, but the strengths and the hidden connections differ, which is why they sometimes misunderstand.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter «semantik tarmoq»ni tasvirlaydi: o'xshashlik, qism-butun, sabab-oqibat va hokazo munosabatlar bilan bog'langan tushunchalar to'ri. «It» «hayvon», «vovullash», «dum», «sadoqat», «mushuk» bilan bog'langan. Aqlda bunday tarmoq qat'iy emas; bog'lanishlar foydalanish bilan kuchliroq yoki zaifroq bo'ladi va yangi tushunchalar eskilarini aralashtirish orqali shakllanadi. Ikki odamning tarmoqlari ko'plab bir xil tugunlar va bog'lanishlarga ega, shuning uchun ular bir-birini tushuna oladi, lekin kuchlar va yashirin bog'lanishlar farq qiladi, shuning uchun ular ba'zan bir-birini noto'g'ri tushunadi.

paras.en: An important idea in this chapter is that the symbol level of the brain might be partly independent of the neural level. Two brains could have very different neural wiring and yet have similar symbol-level structures, just as two computers with different hardware can run the same program. This is why Hofstadter believes that intelligence could, in principle, be realised in a different medium — such as a computer. What matters for a mind is not the stuff it is made of, but the pattern of symbols and their interactions.
paras.uz: Bu bobdagi muhim g'oya — miyaning belgilar darajasi neyron darajasidan qisman mustaqil bo'lishi mumkin. Ikki miya juda boshqacha neyron simlanishiga ega bo'lishi va baribir belgilar darajasida o'xshash tuzilmalarga ega bo'lishi mumkin, xuddi turli apparat ta'minotiga ega ikki kompyuter bir xil dasturni ishga tushira olgani kabi. Shuning uchun Hofstadter aql printsipial jihatdan boshqa muhitda — masalan, kompyuterda amalga oshirilishi mumkin, deb ishonadi. Aql uchun muhimi — u nimadan yasalgani emas, balki belgilar va ularning o'zaro ta'siri naqshi.

paras.en: The chapter also discusses how the mind can imagine worlds that do not exist. We constantly think 'what if': what if I had taken another road, what if it rained tomorrow. Hofstadter suggests that this ability depends on 'slippability' — the capacity of concepts to slip into neighbouring concepts. 'Tomorrow' slips to 'next week', 'rain' slips to 'snow'. Some things slip easily, others are held fixed. Which things we allow to slip, and which we keep constant, reveals how our concepts are organised — a theme he will develop in the dialogue 'Contrafactus' later.
paras.uz: Bob shuningdek aql mavjud bo'lmagan dunyolarni qanday tasavvur qila olishini muhokama qiladi. Biz doimo «agar» deb o'ylaymiz: agar boshqa yo'lni tanlaganimda, agar ertaga yomg'ir yog'sa. Hofstadter bu qobiliyat «sirpanuvchanlik»ka — tushunchalarning qo'shni tushunchalarga sirpanib o'tish qobiliyatiga bog'liq ekanini taklif qiladi. «Ertaga» «keyingi hafta»ga, «yomg'ir» «qor»ga sirpanadi. Ba'zi narsalar oson sirpanadi, boshqalari qat'iy ushlab turiladi. Qaysi narsalarning sirpanishiga yo'l qo'yishimiz va qaysilarini o'zgarmas saqlashimiz tushunchalarimiz qanday tashkil etilganini ochib beradi — u bu mavzuni keyinroq «Contrafactus» dialogida rivojlantiradi.

paras.en: Finally, Hofstadter connects the theme back to Gödel. Brains, like formal systems, contain representations of the world, and some of those representations are of the brain itself. When you think about your own thoughts, your mind contains a model of your mind. This model is necessarily incomplete — a map cannot contain every detail of the territory, including itself. Yet the self-model is what lets us say 'I'. The imperfect isomorphism between minds, and between a mind and its model of itself, is the space in which personality lives.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, Hofstadter mavzuni yana Gödel bilan bog'laydi. Miyalar, formal tizimlar kabi, dunyoning tasvirlarini o'z ichiga oladi va bu tasvirlarning ba'zilari miyaning o'zi haqida. Siz o'z fikrlaringiz haqida o'ylaganingizda, aqlingiz aqlingizning modelini o'z ichiga oladi. Bu model albatta to'liq emas — xarita hududning har bir tafsilotini, jumladan o'zini ham o'z ichiga ola olmaydi. Shunga qaramay o'z-o'zi modeli bizga «men» deyishga imkon beradi. Aqllar o'rtasidagi va aql bilan uning o'z modeli o'rtasidagi nomukammal izomorfizm — shaxsiyat yashaydigan makon.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I translated a nonsense poem into Greek. Where the English said 'slithy', I wrote a word that doesn't exist in Greek either. Tortoise: And does it feel slimy and lithe? Achilles: To me it does! Tortoise: Then you have translated the feeling, not the word. Achilles: But how do I know your 'slimy' is like mine? Tortoise: You don't — not exactly. My maps of 'slimy' were drawn by snails in my garden; yours by fish at the harbour. Achilles: Then do we understand each other at all? Tortoise: Well enough to argue. That is already a miracle.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men ma'nosiz she'rni yunon tiliga tarjima qildim. Inglizcha «slithy» bo'lgan joyga yunon tilida ham mavjud bo'lmagan so'z yozdim. Toshbaqa: U shilimshiq va epchil tuyuladimi? Axilles: Menga shunday tuyuladi! Toshbaqa: Unda sen so'zni emas, tuyg'uni tarjima qilding. Axilles: Lekin sening «shilimshiq»ing meniki kabi ekanini qayerdan bilaman? Toshbaqa: Bilmaysan — aniq emas. Mening «shilimshiq» xaritalarimni bog'imdagi shilliqqurtlar chizgan; senikilarni — bandargohdagi baliqlar. Axilles: Unda biz umuman bir-birimizni tushunamizmi? Toshbaqa: Bahslashish uchun yetarlicha. Bu allaqachon mo''jiza.

quiz.q: What is presented before Chapter XII?
o: Carroll's 'Jabberwocky' in English, French and German
quiz.why_uz: «Jabberwocky» va uning ikki tarjimasi.

quiz.q: Are two minds perfectly isomorphic, according to Hofstadter?
o: Roughly similar in large structure, but different in fine detail
quiz.why_uz: Katta miqyosda o'xshash, nozik tuzilmada shaxsiy — ikki xarita kabi.

quiz.q: What does good translation look for, in Hofstadter's view?
o: An isomorphism at the right level — between experiences the words create
quiz.why_uz: So'zlar emas, ular yaratadigan tajribalar o'rtasidagi moslik.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldin Lyuis Kerrolning ma'nosiz so'zlarga to'la «Jabberwocky» she'ri va uning fransuzcha va nemischa tarjimalari keladi. Bob ikki odamning aqli qanchalik «izomorf» ekanini so'raydi: biz bir xil so'zlarni ishlatamiz, lekin ichimizdagi tushunchalar tarmog'i bir xilmi? Hofstadter turli xaritalar, tarjima va «tushunchalar tarmog'i» misollari orqali aqllar o'rtasidagi qisman, qo'pol o'xshashlikni tushuntiradi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob o'zbek o'quvchisi uchun ayniqsa qiziq: tarjima — ikki til, ikki madaniyat, ikki aql o'rtasidagi izomorfizm izlash. Hofstadter tarjimaning so'zma-so'z emas, balki tuzilma va tuyg'u darajasida bo'lishi kerakligini ko'rsatadi.

chapters.title: Chapter XIII: BlooP and FlooP and GlooP
chapters.title_uz: XIII bob: BlooP, FlooP va GlooP

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XIII is 'Aria with Diverse Variations', named after Bach's Goldberg Variations, which, according to legend, were written to entertain a count suffering from insomnia. Here Achilles cannot sleep, and the Tortoise entertains him with puzzles about numbers. One of them is the famous Goldbach conjecture: every even number greater than two is the sum of two primes (4 = 2+2, 6 = 3+3, 8 = 3+5...). Nobody has proved it, and nobody has found an exception. Achilles realises that a search for an exception might go on forever.
paras.uz: XIII bobdan oldingi dialog — «Turli variatsiyali ariya», afsonaga ko'ra uyqusizlikdan qiynalgan bir grafni ovuntirish uchun yozilgan Baxning «Goldberg variatsiyalari» sharafiga nomlangan. Bu yerda Axilles uxlay olmaydi va Toshbaqa uni sonlar haqidagi jumboqlar bilan ovuntiradi. Ulardan biri mashhur Goldbax gipotezasi: ikkidan katta har bir juft son ikkita tub sonning yig'indisi (4 = 2+2, 6 = 3+3, 8 = 3+5...). Hech kim uni isbotlamagan va hech kim istisno topmagan. Axilles istisno izlash abadiy davom etishi mumkinligini anglaydi.

paras.en: This difference — between a search that is guaranteed to finish and one that might never finish — is the subject of the chapter. Hofstadter invents a simple programming language called BlooP (from 'bounded loop'). In BlooP, every loop must state in advance the maximum number of times it will run: 'loop at most N times'. As a result, every BlooP program is guaranteed to stop and give an answer. BlooP can compute many useful things: factorials, whether a number is prime, the nth Fibonacci number, and so on.
paras.uz: Bu farq — tugashi kafolatlangan izlanish va hech qachon tugamasligi mumkin bo'lgan izlanish o'rtasidagi farq — bob mavzusi. Hofstadter BlooP ("bounded loop" — «chegaralangan sikl»dan) deb ataladigan oddiy dasturlash tilini ixtiro qiladi. BlooP da har bir sikl oldindan necha marta bajarilishining maksimal sonini aytishi kerak: «ko'pi bilan N marta takrorla». Natijada har bir BlooP dasturi albatta to'xtab, javob berishi kafolatlanadi. BlooP ko'p foydali narsalarni hisoblay oladi: faktoriallar, son tub ekanligi, n-Fibonachchi soni va hokazo.

paras.en: Functions that can be computed in BlooP correspond to what mathematicians call primitive recursive functions. For a long time it seemed that perhaps every reasonable computation could be done this way. Hofstadter shows that this is not so, using a beautiful argument borrowed from Georg Cantor, the founder of set theory: the diagonal method. Cantor had used it in the nineteenth century to prove that there are more real numbers than whole numbers. Hofstadter adapts it to programs.
paras.uz: BlooP da hisoblash mumkin bo'lgan funksiyalar matematiklar primitiv rekursiv funksiyalar deb ataydigan narsaga mos keladi. Uzoq vaqt davomida har qanday oqilona hisoblashni shu tarzda bajarish mumkindek tuyulgan. Hofstadter to'plamlar nazariyasi asoschisi Georg Kantordan olingan go'zal dalil — diagonal usul yordamida bunday emasligini ko'rsatadi. Kantor uni XIX asrda haqiqiy sonlar butun sonlardan ko'proq ekanini isbotlash uchun ishlatgan. Hofstadter uni dasturlarga moslashtiradi.

paras.en: The argument goes like this. Every BlooP program is a finite text, so we can list all BlooP programs that compute a function of one number: program 1, program 2, program 3, and so on. Hofstadter calls these 'Blue programs'. Now define a new function, Bluediag: for any N, Bluediag(N) is one plus the answer that Blue program number N gives when you feed it N. Bluediag can obviously be computed: find program N, run it on N (it will stop, because it is BlooP), and add one.
paras.uz: Dalil shunday. Har bir BlooP dasturi chekli matn, shuning uchun bitta sonning funksiyasini hisoblaydigan barcha BlooP dasturlarini ro'yxatga olishimiz mumkin: 1-dastur, 2-dastur, 3-dastur va hokazo. Hofstadter ularni «Ko'k dasturlar» deb ataydi. Endi yangi funksiyani — Bluediag ni ta'riflang: har qanday N uchun Bluediag(N) — N-raqamli Ko'k dasturga N berilganda beradigan javobga bir qo'shilgani. Bluediag ni aniq hisoblash mumkin: N-dasturni toping, uni N da ishga tushiring (u to'xtaydi, chunki u BlooP) va bir qo'shing.

paras.en: But Bluediag cannot itself be a BlooP program. Why? If it were, it would be on the list — say, as program number K. Then Bluediag(K) would have to equal the output of program K on input K, because program K is Bluediag. But by definition Bluediag(K) is that output plus one. A number cannot equal itself plus one. So Bluediag is a perfectly computable function that BlooP cannot compute. The diagonal construction 'escapes' every list that tries to contain it — exactly the kind of escape Gödel will use.
paras.uz: Lekin Bluediag ning o'zi BlooP dasturi bo'la olmaydi. Nega? Agar bo'lganida, u ro'yxatda bo'lardi — aytaylik, K-raqamli dastur sifatida. Unda Bluediag(K) K-dasturning K kirishdagi natijasiga teng bo'lishi kerak edi, chunki K-dastur — Bluediag. Lekin ta'rifga ko'ra Bluediag(K) — o'sha natijaga bir qo'shilgani. Son o'zi plyus birga teng bo'la olmaydi. Demak, Bluediag — BlooP hisoblay olmaydigan mutlaqo hisoblanadigan funksiya. Diagonal qurilma uni o'z ichiga olishga urinadigan har qanday ro'yxatdan «qochadi» — aynan Gödel foydalanadigan qochish turi.

paras.en: So Hofstadter introduces a more powerful language, FlooP ('free loop'). FlooP allows unbounded loops: 'keep searching until you find an answer'. With FlooP you can compute Bluediag and much more — in fact, FlooP is as powerful as any real computer language. But there is a price. A FlooP program might never stop. A program searching for an even number that is not the sum of two primes will run forever if the Goldbach conjecture is true. And you cannot always tell in advance whether a given FlooP program will stop.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun Hofstadter kuchliroq til — FlooP («erkin sikl»)ni kiritadi. FlooP chegaralanmagan sikllarga ruxsat beradi: «javob topguningcha izlashda davom et». FlooP bilan Bluediag ni va yana ko'p narsani hisoblash mumkin — aslida FlooP har qanday haqiqiy kompyuter tili qadar kuchli. Lekin buning bahosi bor. FlooP dasturi hech qachon to'xtamasligi mumkin. Ikki tub son yig'indisi bo'lmagan juft sonni izlayotgan dastur, agar Goldbax gipotezasi to'g'ri bo'lsa, abadiy ishlaydi. Va berilgan FlooP dasturi to'xtashini doim oldindan aytib bo'lmaydi.

paras.en: Hofstadter calls FlooP programs that always stop 'Green programs', and those that might not, 'Red programs'. Could we write a FlooP program that looks at any other FlooP program and decides whether it will stop — a perfect 'termination tester'? Using the diagonal method again, the answer is no. If such a tester existed, we could list all Green programs and build a Greendiag function that escapes the list, leading to a contradiction. This is a version of Alan Turing's famous 1936 result, known today as the halting problem: no program can decide, for all programs, whether they halt.
paras.uz: Hofstadter har doim to'xtaydigan FlooP dasturlarini «Yashil dasturlar», to'xtamasligi mumkin bo'lganlarini «Qizil dasturlar» deb ataydi. Har qanday boshqa FlooP dasturiga qarab, u to'xtaydimi yoki yo'qmi hal qiladigan FlooP dasturini — mukammal «to'xtash tekshiruvchisini» yoza olamizmi? Yana diagonal usuldan foydalanib, javob — yo'q. Agar bunday tekshiruvchi mavjud bo'lganida, barcha Yashil dasturlarni ro'yxatga olib, ro'yxatdan qochadigan Greendiag funksiyasini qura olardik, bu ziddiyatga olib keladi. Bu Alan Tyuringning bugun «to'xtash muammosi» nomi bilan mashhur 1936-yilgi natijasining bir varianti: hech bir dastur barcha dasturlar uchun ular to'xtashini hal qila olmaydi.

paras.en: Finally, GlooP. Is there a language even more powerful than FlooP, which could compute things FlooP cannot — for example, a termination tester? Hofstadter's answer, following the Church–Turing thesis, is that GlooP is a myth. As far as anyone knows, every mechanical procedure can be expressed in FlooP. There is no higher kind of mechanical computation. The limits of FlooP are the limits of mechanism itself. This sets the stage for the next chapter: TNT, too, is mechanical, and so it inherits these limits.
paras.uz: Nihoyat, GlooP. FlooP dan ham kuchliroq, FlooP hisoblay olmaydigan narsalarni — masalan, to'xtash tekshiruvchisini — hisoblay oladigan til bormi? Hofstadterning Cherch–Tyuring tezisiga ergashgan javobi — GlooP afsona. Hech kim bilganicha, har qanday mexanik protsedurani FlooP da ifodalash mumkin. Mexanik hisoblashning bundan yuqori turi yo'q. FlooP chegaralari — mexanizmning o'zining chegaralari. Bu keyingi bobga sahna tayyorlaydi: TNT ham mexanik, shuning uchun u bu chegaralarni meros qilib oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter also makes a connection back to TNT. Every BlooP-computable property of numbers can be expressed in TNT and, importantly, the true instances can be proved in TNT. TNT is said to 'represent' such properties. This is the technical bridge to Gödel: the property 'n is the Gödel number of a proof of the string with Gödel number m' is BlooP-computable — checking a proof is a bounded, mechanical task. So TNT can represent the relation 'is a proof of', and therefore it can talk about its own proofs.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek TNT ga qaytib bog'lanish qiladi. Sonlarning BlooP da hisoblanadigan har bir xususiyatini TNT da ifodalash mumkin va, eng muhimi, haqiqiy holatlarni TNT da isbotlash mumkin. TNT bunday xususiyatlarni «ifodalaydi» deyiladi. Bu Gödelga texnik ko'prik: «n — Gödel raqami m bo'lgan qatorning isboti Gödel raqami» degan xususiyat BlooP da hisoblanadi — isbotni tekshirish chegaralangan, mexanik vazifa. Demak, TNT «...ning isboti» munosabatini ifodalay oladi va shuning uchun o'z isbotlari haqida gapira oladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I wrote a program that checks every even number to see if it's the sum of two primes. It's been running since Tuesday. Tortoise: And when will it stop? Achilles: When it finds a counterexample. Tortoise: And if there isn't one? Achilles: Then... never. Can't I write another program to tell me whether the first one will stop? Tortoise: You can try. But for every such tester, I can write a program that does the opposite of whatever the tester predicts for it. Achilles: The diagonal again! Tortoise: The diagonal always wins.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men har bir juft sonni ikki tub son yig'indisi ekanini tekshiradigan dastur yozdim. U seshanbadan beri ishlayapti. Toshbaqa: Qachon to'xtaydi? Axilles: Qarshi misol topganda. Toshbaqa: Agar u yo'q bo'lsa-chi? Axilles: Unda... hech qachon. Birinchisi to'xtaydimi-yo'qmi aytadigan boshqa dastur yoza olmaymanmi? Toshbaqa: Urinib ko'rishing mumkin. Lekin har bir shunday tekshiruvchi uchun men tekshiruvchi u haqida nima bashorat qilsa, aksini qiladigan dastur yoza olaman. Axilles: Yana diagonal! Toshbaqa: Diagonal doim yutadi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Turli variatsiyali ariya» dialogida uyqusizlikdan qiynalgan Axillesga Toshbaqa Goldbax gipotezasi kabi «hech qachon tugamasligi mumkin bo'lgan izlanishlar» haqida gapiradi. Bob uchta xayoliy dasturlash tilini taqdim etadi: faqat chegaralangan sikllarga ega va doim tugaydigan BlooP, chegaralanmagan qidiruvga ruxsat beradigan FlooP va mavjud bo'lmagan GlooP. Kantor diagonal usuli yordamida BlooP hamma narsani hisoblay olmasligi, FlooP dasturlari esa to'xtashini oldindan bilib bo'lmasligi ko'rsatiladi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob zamonaviy informatikaning asosiy natijalaridan birini — «to'xtash muammosi»ni sodda tilda tushuntiradi. Diagonal usulni qog'ozda kichik jadval chizib tekshirib ko'ring.

chapters.title: Chapter XIV: On formally undecidable propositions of TNT
chapters.title_uz: XIV bob: TNT ning formal hal qilib bo'lmaydigan jumlalari haqida

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XIV, 'The Air on G's String', plays with a trick invented by the American philosopher W. V. O. Quine. You cannot easily make a sentence say 'this sentence is false' without the word 'this'. Quine found a way: take a phrase that describes what happens when a phrase is put after its own quotation, and then put that phrase after its own quotation. The result describes itself, without ever saying 'this'. Hofstadter calls the operation of putting a phrase after its own quotation 'quining', in Quine's honour.
paras.uz: XIV bobdan oldingi dialog — «G torida ariya» — amerikalik faylasuf U. V. O. Kuayn ixtiro qilgan hiyla bilan o'ynaydi. «Bu» so'zisiz jumlaga «bu jumla yolg'on» deb osongina aytdirib bo'lmaydi. Kuayn yo'lini topdi: ibora o'zining iqtibosidan keyin qo'yilganda nima bo'lishini tasvirlaydigan iborani oling, keyin o'sha iborani o'zining iqtibosidan keyin qo'ying. Natija hech qachon «bu» demasdan, o'zini tasvirlaydi. Hofstadter iborani o'zining iqtibosidan keyin qo'yish amalini Kuayn sharafiga «kuayn qilish» (quining) deb ataydi.

paras.en: A simple example in our own words: take the phrase 'when quined, gives a sentence that nobody can prove'. Quining it means writing it in quotation marks and then writing it again after: "'when quined, gives a sentence that nobody can prove' when quined, gives a sentence that nobody can prove". What sentence do you get when you quine that phrase? Exactly this one. So the sentence talks about itself indirectly, through a description of how it is built. Gödel's trick inside TNT is the arithmetical version of this.
paras.uz: O'z so'zlarimiz bilan oddiy misol: «kuayn qilinganda, hech kim isbotlay olmaydigan jumlani beradi» degan iborani oling. Uni kuayn qilish — uni qo'shtirnoqqa olib yozish va undan keyin yana yozish: "«kuayn qilinganda, hech kim isbotlay olmaydigan jumlani beradi» kuayn qilinganda, hech kim isbotlay olmaydigan jumlani beradi". Bu iborani kuayn qilganingizda qanday jumla hosil bo'ladi? Aynan shu jumla. Shunday qilib jumla o'zi haqida bilvosita, qanday qurilganining tavsifi orqali gapiradi. Gödelning TNT ichidagi hiylasi buning arifmetik versiyasi.

paras.en: The chapter builds Gödel's sentence from two ingredients. The first is the idea of a proof-pair. Every proof in TNT is a sequence of strings, and so it has a Gödel number. Say that two numbers, m and n, form a 'TNT-proof-pair' if m is the Gödel number of a proof whose last line is the string with Gödel number n. Checking whether two given numbers form a proof-pair is a bounded, mechanical task — so, as we saw in Chapter XIII, it can be represented in TNT by a formula. TNT can talk about which strings are proved.
paras.uz: Bob Gödel jumlasini ikki tarkibiy qismdan quradi. Birinchisi — isbot-juftlik g'oyasi. TNT dagi har bir isbot — qatorlar ketma-ketligi, shuning uchun uning Gödel raqami bor. Agar m — oxirgi satri Gödel raqami n bo'lgan qator bo'lgan isbotning Gödel raqami bo'lsa, m va n sonlari «TNT-isbot-juftlik» hosil qiladi, deylik. Berilgan ikki son isbot-juftlik hosil qilishini tekshirish — chegaralangan, mexanik vazifa, shuning uchun, XIII bobda ko'rganimizdek, uni TNT da formula bilan ifodalash mumkin. TNT qaysi qatorlar isbotlanganligi haqida gapira oladi.

paras.en: The second ingredient is arithmoquining, the TNT version of quining. Take a TNT formula with one free variable, say a″. Its arithmoquinification is what you get when you replace that variable by the numeral for the formula's own Gödel number. In other words, you feed the formula its own code. This, too, is a mechanical operation on numbers, so TNT can represent the relation 'n is the Gödel number of the arithmoquinification of the formula with Gödel number m'. A formula can now talk about what happens when a formula is fed its own description.
paras.uz: Ikkinchi tarkibiy qism — arifmo-kuayn qilish, kuayn qilishning TNT versiyasi. Bitta erkin o'zgaruvchili, aytaylik a″ li TNT formulasini oling. Uning arifmo-kuayn shakli — o'sha o'zgaruvchini formulaning o'z Gödel raqamining raqam-nomi bilan almashtirganingizda hosil bo'ladigan narsa. Boshqacha aytganda, siz formulaga o'zining kodini berasiz. Bu ham sonlar ustidagi mexanik amal, shuning uchun TNT «n — Gödel raqami m bo'lgan formulaning arifmo-kuayn shaklining Gödel raqami» munosabatini ifodalay oladi. Endi formula formulaga o'zining tavsifi berilganda nima bo'lishi haqida gapira oladi.

paras.en: Now combine them. Write a formula that says: 'There is no proof-pair whose second member is the arithmoquinification of a″.' Hofstadter calls this formula the 'uncle' of G. It has one free variable, a″. Let u be the Gödel number of the uncle. Now arithmoquine the uncle: replace a″ by the numeral for u. The resulting string is G. What does G say? It says: 'There is no proof of the arithmoquinification of the formula with Gödel number u.' But the arithmoquinification of the formula with Gödel number u is G itself. So G says: 'G is not a theorem of TNT.'
paras.uz: Endi ularni birlashtiring. «Ikkinchi a'zosi a″ ning arifmo-kuayn shakli bo'lgan isbot-juftlik yo'q» deydigan formula yozing. Hofstadter bu formulani G ning «amakisi» deb ataydi. Unda bitta erkin o'zgaruvchi bor — a″. u — amakining Gödel raqami bo'lsin. Endi amakini arifmo-kuayn qiling: a″ ni u ning raqam-nomi bilan almashtiring. Hosil bo'lgan qator — G. G nima deydi? U aytadi: «Gödel raqami u bo'lgan formulaning arifmo-kuayn shaklining isboti yo'q.» Lekin Gödel raqami u bo'lgan formulaning arifmo-kuayn shakli — G ning o'zi. Demak, G aytadi: «G TNT teoremasi emas.»

paras.en: Now the familiar reasoning applies. If G were a theorem, TNT would prove a statement saying that G is not a theorem — TNT would prove something false, and, as Hofstadter shows, it would then be inconsistent. So if TNT is consistent, G is not a theorem. But that is exactly what G says — so G is true. Could ~G be a theorem instead? Under a slightly stronger assumption about TNT (called ω-consistency), no. So neither G nor its negation can be proved: G is undecidable in TNT. TNT is incomplete. And the argument works for any extension of TNT as well.
paras.uz: Endi tanish mulohaza qo'llaniladi. Agar G teorema bo'lganida, TNT G teorema emasligini aytadigan gapni isbotlagan bo'lardi — TNT yolg'on narsani isbotlagan bo'lardi va, Hofstadter ko'rsatganidek, u holda ziddiyatli bo'lardi. Demak, agar TNT ziddiyatsiz bo'lsa, G teorema emas. Lekin aynan shuni G aytadi — demak G haqiqat. Buning o'rniga ~G teorema bo'la oladimi? TNT haqidagi biroz kuchliroq farazda (ω-ziddiyatsizlik deb ataladi), yo'q. Demak, na G ni, na uning inkorini isbotlab bo'lmaydi: G TNT da hal qilib bo'lmaydi. TNT to'liq emas. Va dalil TNT ning har qanday kengaytmasi uchun ham ishlaydi.

paras.en: Hofstadter also explains Gödel's second theorem. The reasoning above — 'if TNT is consistent, then G is not a theorem' — can itself be translated into TNT. If TNT could prove its own consistency, it could then prove G, which we know it cannot (if it is consistent). Therefore TNT cannot prove its own consistency. A system strong enough to talk about itself cannot certify its own reliability from the inside. Hilbert's dream of a self-certified mathematics is impossible.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek Gödelning ikkinchi teoremasini tushuntiradi. Yuqoridagi mulohaza — «agar TNT ziddiyatsiz bo'lsa, G teorema emas» — o'zi TNT ga tarjima qilinishi mumkin. Agar TNT o'z ziddiyatsizligini isbotlay olganida, u keyin G ni isbotlay olardi, biz esa (agar u ziddiyatsiz bo'lsa) buni qila olmasligini bilamiz. Demak, TNT o'z ziddiyatsizligini isbotlay olmaydi. O'zi haqida gapira oladigan darajada kuchli tizim o'z ishonchliligini ichkaridan tasdiqlay olmaydi. Hilbertning o'z-o'zini tasdiqlaydigan matematika orzusi imkonsiz.

paras.en: What can we do with G? We can add it to TNT as a new axiom, since we believe it is true. The new system, TNT+G, is stronger — but it has its own Gödel sentence, G′, built in the same way, which it cannot prove. Add G′, and there is G″. The incompleteness is not a hole that can be patched; it is 'essential'. This is the record-player story again: every new player has its own destructive record. Hofstadter shows a picture of this as an endless tower of systems, each one escaping the last but never escaping incompleteness.
paras.uz: G bilan nima qila olamiz? Uni haqiqat deb ishonganimiz uchun TNT ga yangi aksioma sifatida qo'shishimiz mumkin. Yangi tizim — TNT+G kuchliroq — lekin uning xuddi shunday qurilgan, o'zi isbotlay olmaydigan Gödel jumlasi G′ bor. G′ ni qo'shing, va G″ paydo bo'ladi. To'liqsizlik — yamab bo'ladigan teshik emas; u «mohiyatan». Bu yana grammofon hikoyasi: har bir yangi grammofonning o'z buzuvchi plastinkasi bor. Hofstadter buni cheksiz tizimlar minorasi sifatida tasvirlaydi, har biri oldingisidan qochadi, lekin hech qachon to'liqsizlikdan qochmaydi.

paras.en: Even stranger, we could add ~G as an axiom instead. Surprisingly, the system TNT+~G is also consistent — it never proves a plain contradiction. But it now 'believes' that G has a proof, and so that there exists a number which is the Gödel number of a proof of G — even though no ordinary number is. Such a number must be a 'nonstandard' number, which Hofstadter playfully calls a supernatural number. Just as denying Euclid's fifth postulate produced non-Euclidean geometry, denying G produces a non-standard arithmetic, with numbers beyond all the ordinary ones.
paras.uz: Bundan ham g'alatirog'i, biz buning o'rniga ~G ni aksioma sifatida qo'shishimiz mumkin. Hayratlanarlisi, TNT+~G tizimi ham ziddiyatsiz — u hech qachon ochiq ziddiyatni isbotlamaydi. Lekin endi u G ning isboti borligiga «ishonadi», demak, G isbotining Gödel raqami bo'lgan son mavjud — garchi hech bir oddiy son bunday bo'lmasa ham. Bunday son «nostandart» son bo'lishi kerak, Hofstadter uni o'ynoqi tarzda g'ayritabiiy son deb ataydi. Evklidning beshinchi postulatini inkor etish noevklid geometriyani hosil qilganidek, G ni inkor etish barcha oddiy sonlardan tashqaridagi sonlarga ega nostandart arifmetikani hosil qiladi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: So G says 'I am not a theorem' — but it never says 'I'! Tortoise: It describes a recipe: take this formula, feed it its own code number, and you get an unprovable statement. Achilles: And following the recipe gives... G itself. Tortoise: Exactly. G points at its own reflection without knowing it is a mirror. Achilles: And if TNT proved G? Tortoise: Then TNT would be lying, and a lying system can prove anything. Achilles: So G is true but unprovable. Tortoise: True, unprovable, and perfectly polite about it.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Demak, G «Men teorema emasman» deydi — lekin u hech qachon «men» demaydi! Toshbaqa: U retseptni tasvirlaydi: bu formulani ol, unga o'zining kod raqamini ber va isbotlab bo'lmaydigan gapni olasan. Axilles: Retseptga amal qilish esa... G ning o'zini beradi. Toshbaqa: Aynan. G ko'zgu ekanini bilmasdan o'z aksiga ishora qiladi. Axilles: Agar TNT G ni isbotlasa-chi? Toshbaqa: Unda TNT yolg'on gapirgan bo'lardi, yolg'onchi tizim esa hamma narsani isbotlay oladi. Axilles: Demak, G haqiqat, lekin isbotlab bo'lmaydi. Toshbaqa: Haqiqat, isbotlab bo'lmaydi va bu haqda mutlaqo xushmuomala.

quiz.q: What does G say, read on the higher level?
o: G is not a theorem of TNT
quiz.why_uz: G: «G TNT teoremasi emas».

quiz.q: What does Gödel's second theorem say?
o: TNT cannot prove its own consistency
quiz.why_uz: O'zi haqida gapira oladigan tizim o'z ziddiyatsizligini ichkaridan isbotlay olmaydi.

quiz.q: What happens if we add G as an axiom?
o: A new Gödel sentence G′ appears

chapters.recap_uz: Kitobning cho'qqisi: Gödel teoremasining isboti. Bobdan oldingi dialogda Toshbaqa faylasuf Kuayn ixtiro qilgan o'z-o'zini iqtibos qiladigan jumla bilan o'ynaydi. Bob ikki g'oyani — «isbot-juftlik» va «arifmo-kuayn qilish»ni — birlashtirib, TNT ichida «Men TNT teoremasi emasman» deydigan G jumlasini quradi. G hal qilib bo'lmaydi; TNT o'z ziddiyatsizligini isbotlay olmaydi; G yoki ~G ni aksioma sifatida qo'shish mumkin — ikkinchisi «g'ayritabiiy sonlar»ga olib keladi.
chapters.note_uz: Bobni sekin o'qing. Asosiy hiyla: jumla o'zini to'g'ridan-to'g'ri tilga ololmaydi, lekin u «shu-shu qilinganda hosil bo'ladigan jumla» haqida gapirishi mumkin — va o'sha jumla aynan o'zi bo'lib chiqadi.

chapters.title: Chapter XV: Jumping out of the system
chapters.title_uz: XV bob: Tizimdan sakrab chiqish

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XV is a comic piece: it is Achilles' birthday, and he wants the Tortoise to wish him happy birthday. The Tortoise is happy to, as soon as Achilles proves it really is his birthday. Achilles gives an answer; the Tortoise asks for confirmation of the answer; Achilles confirms; the Tortoise asks for confirmation of the confirmation — and so on, through an infinite sequence of questions. Even when Achilles cleverly answers the whole infinite sequence at once, the Tortoise invents a new question beyond it.
paras.uz: XV bobdan oldingi dialog — kulgili asar: Axillesning tug'ilgan kuni va u Toshbaqa uni tug'ilgan kuni bilan tabriklashini istaydi. Toshbaqa Axilles bu haqiqatan uning tug'ilgan kuni ekanini isbotlashi bilanoq tabriklashga tayyor. Axilles javob beradi; Toshbaqa javobning tasdig'ini so'raydi; Axilles tasdiqlaydi; Toshbaqa tasdiqning tasdig'ini so'raydi — va hokazo, cheksiz savollar ketma-ketligi bo'ylab. Hatto Axilles butun cheksiz ketma-ketlikka birdaniga aqlli javob berganda ham, Toshbaqa undan narida yangi savol o'ylab topadi.

paras.en: The dialogue illustrates the main idea of the chapter: no matter how you strengthen a formal system, you cannot escape Gödel's construction. We saw that adding G to TNT gives TNT+G, which has its own G′. One might try to be clever and build a system that adds all the Gödel sentences at once — G, G′, G″ and so on to infinity. But this new system is still mechanical, its axioms can still be listed by a program, and so Gödel's method still applies to it. There is a new sentence beyond the infinite list.
paras.uz: Dialog bobning asosiy g'oyasini tasvirlaydi: formal tizimni qanchalik kuchaytirmang, Gödel qurilmasidan qochib bo'lmaydi. Biz TNT ga G ni qo'shish o'z G′ siga ega TNT+G ni berishini ko'rdik. Aqllilik qilib, barcha Gödel jumlalarini — G, G′, G″ va hokazo cheksizgacha — birdaniga qo'shadigan tizim qurishga urinish mumkin. Lekin bu yangi tizim baribir mexanik, uning aksiomalarini baribir dastur bilan ro'yxatga olish mumkin, shuning uchun Gödel usuli unga ham tatbiq etiladi. Cheksiz ro'yxatdan narida yangi jumla bor.

paras.en: Mathematicians describe this using the transfinite ordinal numbers invented by Cantor: after G, G′, G″... comes a sentence at stage ω (omega), then ω+1, ω+2, and so on, through ever larger infinities. However far you go, there is always a next step. Hofstadter compares it to the Tortoise's endless questions. The process of 'Gödelizing' can itself be mechanised — you can write a program that takes any system and produces its Gödel sentence — but that program, together with the system, forms a new system with a new Gödel sentence.
paras.uz: Matematiklar buni Kantor ixtiro qilgan transfinit tartib sonlar yordamida tasvirlaydi: G, G′, G″... dan keyin ω (omega) bosqichidagi jumla keladi, keyin ω+1, ω+2 va hokazo, tobora kattaroq cheksizliklar bo'ylab. Qanchalik uzoqqa bormang, doim keyingi qadam bor. Hofstadter buni Toshbaqaning cheksiz savollariga qiyoslaydi. «Gödellashtirish» jarayonining o'zini mexanizatsiyalash mumkin — har qanday tizimni olib, uning Gödel jumlasini hosil qiladigan dastur yozish mumkin — lekin o'sha dastur tizim bilan birga yangi Gödel jumlasiga ega yangi tizimni hosil qiladi.

paras.en: Now the big philosophical question. In 1961 the Oxford philosopher J. R. Lucas argued that Gödel's theorem proves that the human mind is not a machine. His reasoning: any machine is equivalent to a formal system; for any formal system, a human mathematician can see that its Gödel sentence is true, while the system cannot prove it; therefore the human can always do something the machine cannot. Many people found this argument attractive. It seemed to put the human spirit safely beyond the reach of computers.
paras.uz: Endi katta falsafiy savol. 1961-yilda oksfordlik faylasuf J. R. Lukas Gödel teoremasi inson aqli mashina emasligini isbotlaydi, deb ta'kidlagan. Uning mulohazasi: har qanday mashina formal tizimga ekvivalent; har qanday formal tizim uchun inson matematik uning Gödel jumlasi haqiqat ekanini ko'ra oladi, tizim esa uni isbotlay olmaydi; demak, inson doim mashina qila olmaydigan narsani qila oladi. Ko'p odamlarga bu dalil yoqqan. U inson ruhini kompyuterlar yeta olmaydigan joyga xavfsiz joylashtirayotgandek tuyulgan.

paras.en: Hofstadter disagrees, and he explains why. To 'see' that a system's Gödel sentence is true, you must know that the system is consistent. For simple systems like TNT we believe this, but for a system as complicated as a human brain, could the human know it? A person cannot Gödelize himself. Hofstadter invents a playful sentence: 'Lucas cannot consistently assert this sentence.' Lucas himself cannot assert it without contradiction, yet anyone else can see that it is true. Humans, too, have their Gödel sentences.
paras.uz: Hofstadter rozi emas va nega ekanini tushuntiradi. Tizimning Gödel jumlasi haqiqat ekanini «ko'rish» uchun tizim ziddiyatsiz ekanini bilishingiz kerak. TNT kabi oddiy tizimlar uchun biz bunga ishonamiz, lekin inson miyasidek murakkab tizim uchun inson buni bila olarmidi? Inson o'zini gödellashtira olmaydi. Hofstadter o'ynoqi jumla o'ylab topadi: «Lukas bu jumlani ziddiyatsiz tasdiqlay olmaydi.» Lukasning o'zi uni ziddiyatsiz tasdiqlay olmaydi, shunga qaramay boshqa har kim uning haqiqat ekanini ko'ra oladi. Insonlarning ham o'z Gödel jumlalari bor.

paras.en: Hofstadter also points out that 'jumping out of the system' is something humans do, but only partly. We can step back from a task, notice patterns, change our rules — the I-mode of Chapter I. But we always jump into some larger system of habits, concepts and beliefs, which has its own limits. There is no final, system-free standpoint. Zen tried to find one, and even Zen became a system. Escher's print Dragon shows a dragon that tries to escape the flat paper by biting its own tail through slits in the page — but remains, of course, a drawing on flat paper.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek «tizimdan sakrab chiqish» insonlar qiladigan narsa ekanini, lekin faqat qisman ekanini ko'rsatadi. Biz vazifadan orqaga chekina olamiz, naqshlarni payqay olamiz, qoidalarimizni o'zgartira olamiz — I bobdagi I-rejim. Lekin biz doim o'z chegaralariga ega bo'lgan odatlar, tushunchalar va e'tiqodlarning qandaydir kattaroq tizimiga sakraymiz. Yakuniy, tizimsiz nuqtai nazar yo'q. Zen uni topishga urindi va hatto Zen ham tizimga aylandi. Escherning «Ajdaho» gravyurasi sahifadagi tirqishlar orqali o'z dumini tishlab, tekis qog'ozdan qochishga urinayotgan ajdahoni ko'rsatadi — lekin u, albatta, tekis qog'ozdagi rasm bo'lib qoladi.

paras.en: So does Gödel's theorem say anything about artificial intelligence? Hofstadter's view is that it does not forbid AI. A computer program that thinks like a human would be a formal system at its lowest level — the level of machine instructions — but its thinking would happen at a much higher level, the level of symbols and concepts, where it could be as flexible, intuitive and fallible as a human. Such a program would have its Gödel sentence, just as we do. Gödel shows the limits of all mechanisms, ourselves included, not a gap between us and machines.
paras.uz: Unda Gödel teoremasi sun'iy intellekt haqida biror narsa aytadimi? Hofstadterning qarashi shuki, u SI ni taqiqlamaydi. Inson kabi fikrlaydigan kompyuter dasturi eng past darajada — mashina ko'rsatmalari darajasida — formal tizim bo'lardi, lekin uning fikrlashi ancha yuqoriroq darajada, belgilar va tushunchalar darajasida sodir bo'lardi, u yerda u inson kabi moslashuvchan, intuitiv va xatoga moyil bo'la olardi. Bunday dasturning xuddi bizniki kabi o'z Gödel jumlasi bo'lardi. Gödel biz bilan mashinalar o'rtasidagi bo'shliqni emas, balki barcha mexanizmlarning, jumladan o'zimizning chegaralarimizni ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: This is an important shift in the book. Many people read Gödel's theorem as a victory of human intuition over machines. Hofstadter reads it as a deep fact about all self-referential systems: anything rich enough to represent itself will contain truths about itself that it cannot reach by its own rules. Instead of separating minds from machines, Gödel's theorem becomes, for Hofstadter, a clue to what minds are: systems so rich that they contain models of themselves, and therefore strange loops.
paras.uz: Bu kitobdagi muhim burilish. Ko'p odamlar Gödel teoremasini inson intuitsiyasining mashinalar ustidan g'alabasi sifatida o'qiydi. Hofstadter uni barcha o'z-o'ziga ishora qiluvchi tizimlar haqidagi chuqur fakt sifatida o'qiydi: o'zini ifodalash uchun yetarlicha boy har qanday narsa o'z qoidalari bilan yeta olmaydigan o'zi haqidagi haqiqatlarni o'z ichiga oladi. Hofstadter uchun Gödel teoremasi aqllarni mashinalardan ajratish o'rniga, aqllar nima ekaniga kalitga aylanadi: o'zlarining modellarini o'z ichiga oladigan va shuning uchun g'alati halqalar bo'lgan darajada boy tizimlar.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, it's my birthday! Say 'happy birthday'. Tortoise: Gladly — once you prove it's your birthday. Achilles: My mother says so. Tortoise: And who says your mother is right? Achilles: The calendar. Tortoise: And the calendar? Achilles: Ugh! Fine — I answer all your questions at once, the whole infinite list: yes, yes, yes, forever. Tortoise: Very impressive. Now, about that whole infinite list... Achilles: There's a question after infinity? Tortoise: There is always a question after your last answer. Happy birthday, by the way.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, bugun mening tug'ilgan kunim! «Tug'ilgan kuning bilan» de. Toshbaqa: Bajonidil — tug'ilgan kuning ekanini isbotlashing bilanoq. Axilles: Onam shunday deydi. Toshbaqa: Onang haq ekanini kim aytadi? Axilles: Kalendar. Toshbaqa: Kalendar-chi? Axilles: Uf! Mayli — men barcha savollaringga birdaniga javob beraman, butun cheksiz ro'yxatga: ha, ha, ha, abadiy. Toshbaqa: Juda ta'sirli. Endi o'sha butun cheksiz ro'yxat haqida... Axilles: Cheksizlikdan keyin savol bormi? Toshbaqa: Sening oxirgi javobingdan keyin doim savol bor. Aytgancha, tug'ilgan kuning bilan.

quiz.q: Why can't adding all Gödel sentences at once make the system complete?
o: The new system is still mechanical and has its own Gödel sentence
quiz.why_uz: Mexanik tizim — demak, Gödel usuli unga ham qo'llaniladi.

quiz.q: What did J. R. Lucas argue?
o: Gödel's theorem shows the human mind is not a machine
quiz.why_uz: Lukas: inson har doim mashina isbotlay olmaydigan Gödel jumlasini ko'radi.

quiz.q: What is Hofstadter's reply?
