quiz.why_uz: «Lukas bu jumlani ziddiyatsiz tasdiqlay olmaydi» — insonlarning ham Gödel jumlalari bor.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Tug'ilgan kun kantatatatasi» dialogida Toshbaqa Axillesning tug'ilgan kuni ekaniga ishonishdan cheksiz yangi bahonalar bilan bosh tortadi. Bob Gödel usulini avtomatlashtirish mumkinligini, lekin avtomatlashtirilgan tizimning ham o'z Gödel jumlasi bo'lishini ko'rsatadi. Hofstadter faylasuf J. R. Lukasning «Gödel teoremasi aql mashina emasligini isbotlaydi» degan dalilini tanqid qiladi: inson ham o'zidan butunlay sakrab chiqa olmaydi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bobning asosiy savoli — inson aqli formal tizimdan ustunmi? Hofstadter oddiy «ha» yoki «yo'q» o'rniga nozik javob beradi: biz tizimlardan sakrab chiqa olamiz, lekin faqat boshqa, kattaroq tizimga.

chapters.title: Chapter XVI: Self-ref and self-rep
chapters.title_uz: XVI bob: O'ziga ishora va o'zini ko'paytirish

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XVI, 'Edifying Thoughts of a Tobacco Smoker', takes place in the Crab's house, full of strange objects and paintings by the Belgian surrealist René Magritte, whose pictures often play with images inside images and with the relation between a picture and what it shows. The conversation drifts towards things that make copies of themselves, and towards the difference between talking about oneself and reproducing oneself. The chapter takes up both ideas.
paras.uz: XVI bobdan oldingi «Chekuvchining ibratli o'ylari» dialogi g'alati buyumlar va belgiyalik syurrealist Rene Magritt rasmlari bilan to'la Qisqichbaqaning uyida bo'lib o'tadi; Magrittning rasmlari ko'pincha tasvir ichidagi tasvirlar bilan va rasm bilan u ko'rsatadigan narsa o'rtasidagi munosabat bilan o'ynaydi. Suhbat o'z nusxalarini yaratadigan narsalarga va o'zi haqida gapirish bilan o'zini ko'paytirish o'rtasidagi farqqa qarab suzadi. Bob ikkala g'oyani ham ko'tarib oladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter begins with self-referential sentences in ordinary language. Some refer to themselves very directly: 'This sentence has five words.' Others are less direct and more interesting: sentences that describe how they are built, as in the quining trick. He shows that the word 'this' is a kind of shortcut — it points at the sentence without describing it — whereas Gödel's method gets self-reference without any shortcut, purely by description. The more indirect the self-reference, the more surprising and powerful it is.
paras.uz: Hofstadter oddiy tildagi o'ziga ishora qiluvchi jumlalardan boshlaydi. Ba'zilari o'ziga juda to'g'ridan-to'g'ri ishora qiladi: «Bu jumla beshta so'zdan iborat.» Boshqalari kamroq to'g'ridan-to'g'ri va qiziqroq: kuayn hiylasidagidek, qanday qurilganini tasvirlaydigan jumlalar. U «bu» so'zi o'ziga xos qisqa yo'l ekanini — u jumlani tasvirlamasdan unga ishora qilishini — ko'rsatadi, Gödel usuli esa hech qanday qisqa yo'lsiz, sof tavsif orqali o'ziga ishoraga erishadi. O'ziga ishora qanchalik bilvosita bo'lsa, shunchalik hayratlanarli va kuchli bo'ladi.

paras.en: Then he turns to self-reproduction. A program that prints out its own text — today called a 'quine' in Quine's honour — seems at first impossible: to print itself, the program must contain its own text, which must contain its own text, and so on forever. But the quining trick solves it. The program contains a template — a description of itself with a blank — and an instruction to print the template twice, once as data and once as code. The result is exactly the original program. Self-reproduction, like self-reference, works through a description plus a copying mechanism.
paras.uz: Keyin u o'zini ko'paytirishga o'tadi. O'z matnini chop etadigan dastur — bugun Kuayn sharafiga «kuayn» deb ataladi — avvaliga imkonsizdek tuyuladi: o'zini chop etish uchun dastur o'z matnini o'z ichiga olishi kerak, u esa o'z matnini o'z ichiga olishi kerak va hokazo abadiy. Lekin kuayn hiylasi buni hal qiladi. Dastur shablonni — bo'sh joyli o'z tavsifini — va shablonni ikki marta, bir marta ma'lumot sifatida va bir marta kod sifatida chop etish ko'rsatmasini o'z ichiga oladi. Natija aynan asl dastur. O'zini ko'paytirish, o'ziga ishora kabi, tavsif plyus nusxalash mexanizmi orqali ishlaydi.

paras.en: Hofstadter also asks: what counts as a 'copy'? A sentence in English and its translation into French — is one a copy of the other? A cell and its daughter cell are not identical atom for atom, but we call them copies. He suggests that self-reproduction, like meaning, depends on levels: something reproduces itself if, at the right level of description, the result has the same structure. This prepares the way for biology, where 'copying' is an incredibly complex chemical process that is nonetheless, at a high level, simple.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek so'raydi: «nusxa» deb nimani hisoblash mumkin? Ingliz tilidagi jumla va uning fransuz tiliga tarjimasi — biri ikkinchisining nusxasimi? Hujayra va uning qiz hujayrasi atomma-atom bir xil emas, lekin biz ularni nusxalar deb ataymiz. U o'zini ko'paytirish, ma'no kabi, darajalarga bog'liq ekanini taklif qiladi: agar to'g'ri tavsif darajasida natija bir xil tuzilmaga ega bo'lsa, narsa o'zini ko'paytiradi. Bu «nusxalash» nihoyatda murakkab kimyoviy jarayon bo'lgan, lekin yuqori darajada baribir oddiy biologiyaga yo'l tayyorlaydi.

paras.en: To make the biology understandable, Hofstadter invents a game called Typogenetics. It uses strings made of four letters, A, C, G and T, like DNA. Pairs of letters are read as instructions for 'enzymes' — little machines that act on strings: they can cut a string, copy a letter, move along, insert letters, and so on. The strings code for enzymes, and enzymes modify strings. Some strings, read as enzyme instructions, produce enzymes that copy those very strings. The game is a toy model of the deepest loop in biology.
paras.uz: Biologiyani tushunarli qilish uchun Hofstadter Tipogenetika deb ataladigan o'yin o'ylab topadi. U DNK kabi to'rtta harf — A, C, G va T dan tashkil topgan qatorlardan foydalanadi. Harf juftliklari «fermentlar» — qatorlar ustida harakat qiladigan kichik mashinalar uchun ko'rsatmalar sifatida o'qiladi: ular qatorni kesishi, harfni nusxalashi, siljishi, harf qo'yishi va hokazo mumkin. Qatorlar fermentlarni kodlaydi, fermentlar esa qatorlarni o'zgartiradi. Ba'zi qatorlar ferment ko'rsatmalari sifatida o'qilganda, aynan o'sha qatorlarni nusxalaydigan fermentlarni hosil qiladi. O'yin biologiyadagi eng chuqur halqaning o'yinchoq modeli.

paras.en: Then he explains the real thing. DNA is a long molecule made of four kinds of bases, A, C, G and T. A stretch of DNA is copied into a related molecule called messenger RNA. Ribosomes in the cell read the RNA three letters at a time; each triplet, or codon, stands for one of twenty amino acids. The ribosome links the amino acids into a chain, which folds into a protein. Proteins do almost all the work of the cell — including, as enzymes, copying DNA, making RNA and building ribosomes. This flow, DNA → RNA → protein, is called the Central Dogma of molecular biology.
paras.uz: Keyin u haqiqiy narsani tushuntiradi. DNK — to'rt turdagi asos — A, C, G va T dan tashkil topgan uzun molekula. DNK bo'lagi axborot RNKsi deb ataladigan qarindosh molekulaga ko'chiriladi. Hujayradagi ribosomalar RNKni bir vaqtda uch harfdan o'qiydi; har bir triplet yoki kodon yigirmata aminokislotadan birini anglatadi. Ribosoma aminokislotalarni zanjirga bog'laydi, u esa oqsilga buklanadi. Oqsillar hujayraning deyarli barcha ishini bajaradi — jumladan fermentlar sifatida DNKni nusxalash, RNK yasash va ribosomalar qurish. Bu oqim — DNK → RNK → oqsil — molekulyar biologiyaning Markaziy dogmasi deb ataladi.

paras.en: Here is the strange loop of life. DNA contains the instructions for building proteins; proteins are the machines that read and copy DNA. The genetic code — the rule that links codons to amino acids — is the 'decoding mechanism', like the record player for the record. And the code itself is carried out by molecules that are built according to the code. Hofstadter draws a careful parallel, which he calls the 'Central Dogmap': DNA corresponds to the strings of TNT, proteins to statements about strings, and the genetic code to Gödel numbering.
paras.uz: Mana hayotning g'alati halqasi. DNK oqsillarni qurish uchun ko'rsatmalarni o'z ichiga oladi; oqsillar esa DNKni o'qiydigan va nusxalaydigan mashinalar. Genetik kod — kodonlarni aminokislotalar bilan bog'laydigan qoida — xuddi plastinka uchun grammofon kabi «ochish mexanizmi». Kodning o'zi esa kodga muvofiq qurilgan molekulalar tomonidan bajariladi. Hofstadter ehtiyotkorlik bilan o'xshatish chizadi, uni «Markaziy dogmaxarita» deb ataydi: DNK TNT qatorlariga, oqsillar qatorlar haqidagi gaplarga, genetik kod esa Gödel raqamlashga mos keladi.

paras.en: In both cases, a system contains a code that allows it to represent itself, and therefore to act on itself. Gödel's sentence refers to itself through arithmoquining; a cell reproduces itself through DNA being read by machines made from DNA. Hofstadter also discusses viruses, such as bacteriophages, which inject their DNA into a bacterium and hijack its machinery to make copies of themselves — a little like a sentence that tricks a reader into repeating it. Self-reference and self-reproduction turn out to be two sides of the same idea.
paras.uz: Ikkala holatda ham tizim o'zini ifodalashga va shuning uchun o'ziga ta'sir qilishga imkon beradigan kodni o'z ichiga oladi. Gödel jumlasi o'ziga arifmo-kuayn qilish orqali ishora qiladi; hujayra DNKdan yasalgan mashinalar DNKni o'qishi orqali o'zini ko'paytiradi. Hofstadter shuningdek bakteriofaglar kabi viruslarni muhokama qiladi, ular o'z DNKsini bakteriyaga kiritib, uning mexanizmini o'z nusxalarini yasash uchun egallab oladi — bu o'quvchini aldab, o'zini takrorlattiradigan jumlaga biroz o'xshaydi. O'ziga ishora va o'zini ko'paytirish bir g'oyaning ikki tomoni bo'lib chiqadi.

paras.en: Why does this matter for the book's central question? Because it shows that self-reference is not a rare trick of logicians. It is everywhere in nature, at the heart of life itself. If life arose when molecules began to represent and copy themselves, perhaps mind arises when patterns in the brain begin to represent themselves. Hofstadter is building a chain: Gödel's loop in arithmetic, the genetic loop in cells, and — in the final chapter — the loop of the self in the brain.
paras.uz: Bu kitobning markaziy savoli uchun nega muhim? Chunki u o'ziga ishora mantiqchilarning noyob hiylasi emasligini ko'rsatadi. U tabiatda hamma joyda, hayotning o'zining qoq markazida. Agar hayot molekulalar o'zlarini ifodalay va nusxalay boshlaganda paydo bo'lgan bo'lsa, balki aql miyadagi naqshlar o'zlarini ifodalay boshlaganda paydo bo'lar. Hofstadter zanjir qurmoqda: arifmetikadagi Gödel halqasi, hujayralardagi genetik halqa va — so'nggi bobda — miyadagi «men» halqasi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I wrote a program that prints its own text! It took me all night. Tortoise: Congratulations — you have built a tiny creature. Achilles: A creature? It's ten lines of code. Tortoise: It contains a description of itself and a way to copy that description. So does every living cell. Achilles: But my program doesn't eat or grow. Tortoise: Give it a few billion years and a hungry environment. Achilles: And the cell's description is DNA, and its copier is made of proteins built from that same DNA? Tortoise: Yes. A record that builds its own record player. Mind the strange loop on your way out.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men o'z matnini chop etadigan dastur yozdim! Butun tun ketdi. Toshbaqa: Tabriklayman — sen kichkina mavjudot yaratding. Axilles: Mavjudot? Bu o'n satrlik kod. Toshbaqa: U o'zining tavsifini va o'sha tavsifni nusxalash usulini o'z ichiga oladi. Har bir tirik hujayra ham shunday. Axilles: Lekin mening dasturim ovqatlanmaydi va o'smaydi. Toshbaqa: Unga bir necha milliard yil va och muhit ber. Axilles: Hujayraning tavsifi DNK, uning nusxalovchisi esa o'sha DNKdan qurilgan oqsillardan yasalganmi? Toshbaqa: Ha. O'z grammofonini quradigan plastinka. Chiqib ketayotganda g'alati halqaga qoqilib ketma.

quiz.q: What is a 'quine' in computing?
o: A program that prints its own text
quiz.why_uz: O'z matnini chop etadigan dastur — Kuayn sharafiga.

quiz.q: What is the Central Dogma of molecular biology?
quiz.why_uz: DNK RNKga ko'chiriladi, RNK oqsilga tarjima qilinadi.

quiz.q: In Hofstadter's 'Central Dogmap', what does the genetic code correspond to?
quiz.why_uz: Genetik kod — hayotning Gödel raqamlashi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bob o'ziga ishora qiluvchi jumlalar va o'zini ko'paytiradigan narsalar — o'zini chop etadigan dasturlar (kuaynlar), Hofstadterning «Tipogenetika» o'yini va haqiqiy hujayradagi DNK, RNK va oqsillar — o'rtasidagi o'xshashlikni ko'rsatadi. Genetik kod hayotning «Gödel kodi» ekani va molekulyar biologiyaning «markaziy dogmasi» Gödel teoremasining tuzilishiga qanday mos kelishi tushuntiriladi.
chapters.note_uz: Biologiyadan qo'rqmang: asosiy fikr oddiy — DNK ham ko'rsatma (qator), ham o'sha ko'rsatmalarni bajaradigan mashinalarni (oqsillarni) qurish uchun reja. Tizim o'zini o'zi tasvirlaydi va ko'paytiradi — xuddi Gödel jumlasi kabi.

chapters.title: Chapter XVII: Church, Turing, Tarski, and others
chapters.title_uz: XVII bob: Cherch, Tyuring, Tarski va boshqalar

paras.en: In the dialogue before Chapter XVII, 'The Magnificrab, Indeed', the Crab appears to have a remarkable gift: when someone plays him a piece of music that encodes a mathematical statement, he can tell at once whether the statement is true or false. Achilles is amazed. The Tortoise is suspicious. Could anyone — human or machine — really have a perfect sense of mathematical truth? The chapter answers: no, not if that sense is mechanical in any way, because of a theorem by the Polish logician Alfred Tarski.
paras.uz: XVII bobdan oldingi «Ajoyib Qisqichbaqa» dialogida Qisqichbaqa ajoyib iste'dodga ega bo'lib ko'rinadi: kimdir unga matematik gapni kodlaydigan musiqa asarini chalganda, u gap haqiqat yoki yolg'on ekanini darhol ayta oladi. Axilles hayratda. Toshbaqa shubhada. Haqiqatan kimdir — inson yoki mashina — matematik haqiqatni mukammal sezishi mumkinmi? Bob javob beradi: yo'q, agar o'sha sezgi qandaydir tarzda mexanik bo'lsa, polshalik mantiqchi Alfred Tarskining teoremasi tufayli.

paras.en: The chapter centres on the Church–Turing thesis. In the 1930s, Alonzo Church and Alan Turing independently proposed precise definitions of 'computable' — Church through a system of functions, Turing through his imaginary machines — and the definitions turned out to be equivalent. They also equal Hofstadter's FlooP. The thesis says that anything which can be computed by any reasonable step-by-step method can be computed by a Turing machine. It cannot be proved, because 'reasonable method' is an informal idea, but no counterexample has ever been found.
paras.uz: Bob Cherch–Tyuring tezisi atrofida aylanadi. 1930-yillarda Alonzo Cherch va Alan Tyuring bir-biridan mustaqil ravishda «hisoblanadigan»ning aniq ta'riflarini taklif qilishgan — Cherch funksiyalar tizimi orqali, Tyuring o'zining xayoliy mashinalari orqali — va ta'riflar ekvivalent bo'lib chiqqan. Ular Hofstadterning FlooP iga ham teng. Tezis aytadiki, har qanday oqilona qadamba-qadam usul bilan hisoblanishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday narsani Tyuring mashinasi hisoblay oladi. Uni isbotlab bo'lmaydi, chunki «oqilona usul» — norasmiy g'oya, lekin hech qachon qarshi misol topilmagan.

paras.en: Hofstadter then lists several versions of the thesis, from cautious to bold. A modest version says that whatever a human can calculate by following clear rules, a FlooP program can calculate. A bolder version says that any mental process that can be divided into steps can be programmed. The boldest, which he calls the 'AI version', says that every mental process at all — perception, intuition, creativity — is ultimately the result of brain activity that a computer could, in principle, simulate. He explains each version and the reasons people accept or reject it.
paras.uz: Keyin Hofstadter tezisning ehtiyotkordan dadilgacha bo'lgan bir nechta versiyasini sanab o'tadi. Kamtar versiya aytadiki, inson aniq qoidalarga amal qilib nimani hisoblay olsa, FlooP dasturi ham hisoblay oladi. Dadilroq versiya qadamlarga bo'linishi mumkin bo'lgan har qanday aqliy jarayonni dasturlash mumkin, deydi. U «SI versiyasi» deb ataydigan eng dadil versiya esa har qanday aqliy jarayon — idrok, intuitsiya, ijodkorlik — oxir-oqibat kompyuter, printsipial jihatdan, simulyatsiya qila oladigan miya faoliyatining natijasi, deydi. U har bir versiyani va odamlar uni qabul qilish yoki rad etish sabablarini tushuntiradi.

paras.en: He also considers the opposite view: that there might be something in human thinking that no mechanism can capture — a soul, or some special quality of biology. He calls this the 'soulist' position and treats it with respect but disagrees. In his view the brain is made of neurons that obey physical laws, and physical laws can be simulated. The question is not whether thought is mechanical at the bottom level — it must be — but whether the high-level patterns can be reproduced in another medium. He believes they can.
paras.uz: U qarama-qarshi qarashni ham ko'rib chiqadi: inson fikrlashida hech qanday mexanizm qamrab ololmaydigan narsa — ruh yoki biologiyaning qandaydir alohida sifati — bo'lishi mumkin. U buni «ruhparastlik» pozitsiyasi deb ataydi va unga hurmat bilan munosabatda bo'ladi, lekin rozi emas. Uning fikricha, miya fizik qonunlarga bo'ysunadigan neyronlardan iborat, fizik qonunlarni esa simulyatsiya qilish mumkin. Savol fikrlash eng quyi darajada mexanikmi degani emas — u shunday bo'lishi kerak — balki yuqori darajadagi naqshlarni boshqa muhitda qayta yaratish mumkinmi degani. U mumkin deb hisoblaydi.

paras.en: To test the idea that some people have mysterious powers, Hofstadter discusses Srinivasa Ramanujan, the self-taught Indian mathematician who astonished the English mathematician G. H. Hardy with formulas that seemed to come from nowhere. Ramanujan said that a goddess showed them to him in dreams. Hofstadter also describes 'lightning calculators' — people who can multiply huge numbers in their heads, or tell you the day of the week for any date. Are these powers beyond mechanism? He argues not: they show how far unconscious, highly practised processes can go.
paras.uz: Ba'zi odamlarda sirli qobiliyatlar bor degan g'oyani sinash uchun Hofstadter ingliz matematigi G. H. Hardini go'yo hech qayerdan kelgan formulalar bilan hayratga solgan o'zini o'zi o'qitgan hind matematigi Srinivasa Ramanujan haqida gapiradi. Ramanujan ularni unga tushida ma'buda ko'rsatgan, degan. Hofstadter shuningdek «chaqmoq hisobchilar»ni tasvirlaydi — boshida ulkan sonlarni ko'paytira oladigan yoki istalgan sana uchun haftaning qaysi kuni ekanini ayta oladigan odamlarni. Bu qobiliyatlar mexanizmdan tashqaridami? U yo'q, deydi: ular ongsiz, juda ko'p mashq qilingan jarayonlar qanchalik uzoqqa borishini ko'rsatadi.

paras.en: An important point is that even a calculating genius does not 'feel' her own steps. The work happens below the level of consciousness, just as when you recognise a friend's face without knowing how. This is the gap between the low level of neurons and the high level of thoughts that Hofstadter has been describing since the Ant Fugue. Mysterious-seeming abilities need not be supernatural; they may be the result of complex processes we cannot observe in ourselves.
paras.uz: Muhim nuqta shundaki, hatto hisoblash dahosi ham o'z qadamlarini «his qilmaydi». Ish ong darajasidan pastda sodir bo'ladi, xuddi do'stingizning yuzini qanday tanishingizni bilmasdan tanigandek. Bu Hofstadter Chumoli fugasidan beri tasvirlab kelayotgan neyronlarning quyi darajasi bilan fikrlarning yuqori darajasi o'rtasidagi bo'shliq. Sirli tuyulgan qobiliyatlar g'ayritabiiy bo'lishi shart emas; ular o'zimizda kuzata olmaydigan murakkab jarayonlarning natijasi bo'lishi mumkin.

paras.en: Now Tarski's theorem. Suppose there were a formula in TNT, call it TRUE(a), which held exactly when a is the Gödel number of a true statement of number theory. Then, using the same trick as Gödel's, we could build a sentence that says 'I am not true' — the Epimenides paradox itself, inside arithmetic. It would be true if and only if it were false, which is impossible. So no such formula can exist. Truth about numbers cannot be defined inside number theory. Provability can be represented; truth cannot.
paras.uz: Endi Tarski teoremasi. Faraz qiling, TNT da TRUE(a) deb ataylik formula bor va u a sonlar nazariyasining haqiqiy gapining Gödel raqami bo'lganda aynan bajariladi. Unda, Gödelnikiga o'xshash hiyladan foydalanib, «Men haqiqat emasman» deydigan jumlani qura olardik — arifmetika ichidagi Epimenid paradoksining o'zi. U faqat va faqat yolg'on bo'lganda haqiqat bo'lardi, bu esa imkonsiz. Demak, bunday formula mavjud bo'la olmaydi. Sonlar haqidagi haqiqatni sonlar nazariyasi ichida aniqlab bo'lmaydi. Isbotlanuvchanlikni ifodalash mumkin; haqiqatni — yo'q.

paras.en: This is why the Crab's gift is suspicious. If his judgement of truth were a mechanical process — even one happening in a brain — it would be representable, and Tarski shows that no representable process can capture all arithmetical truth. Hofstadter draws a lesson about human beings: our sense of truth is powerful but imperfect, heuristic, open to error. We are not perfect truth-detectors, and no machine will be. The dream of a final oracle for mathematics, like Hilbert's dream of completeness, is gone.
paras.uz: Shuning uchun Qisqichbaqaning iste'dodi shubhali. Agar uning haqiqat haqidagi hukmi mexanik jarayon bo'lsa — hatto miyada sodir bo'ladigan jarayon bo'lsa ham — u ifodalanuvchi bo'lardi, Tarski esa hech qanday ifodalanuvchi jarayon barcha arifmetik haqiqatni qamrab ololmasligini ko'rsatadi. Hofstadter insonlar haqida saboq chiqaradi: haqiqatni sezishimiz kuchli, lekin nomukammal, evristik, xatolarga ochiq. Biz mukammal haqiqat aniqlagichlar emasmiz va hech bir mashina bunday bo'lmaydi. Hilbertning to'liqlik orzusi kabi, matematika uchun yakuniy orakul orzusi ham yo'qoldi.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Mr Crab, play me a tune, and tell me if the theorem in it is true! Crab: With pleasure. True. And that one — false. Tortoise: Then let me compose a special tune for you: it encodes the statement 'The Crab will judge this tune to be false.' Crab: Hmm... if I say false, it becomes true; if I say true, it becomes false. Achilles: Your gift has broken! Tortoise: Every gift breaks on the right tune. Crab: I prefer to call it a natural limit of the ear. Tortoise: Tarski would agree with you.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Janob Qisqichbaqa, menga kuy chaling va undagi teorema haqiqatmi, ayting! Qisqichbaqa: Bajonidil. Haqiqat. Anavi esa — yolg'on. Toshbaqa: Unda men siz uchun maxsus kuy bastalay: u «Qisqichbaqa bu kuyni yolg'on deb hukm qiladi» degan gapni kodlaydi. Qisqichbaqa: Hmm... yolg'on desam, u haqiqatga aylanadi; haqiqat desam, yolg'onga aylanadi. Axilles: Iste'dodingiz buzildi! Toshbaqa: Har qanday iste'dod to'g'ri kuyda buziladi. Qisqichbaqa: Men buni quloqning tabiiy chegarasi deb atashni afzal ko'raman. Toshbaqa: Tarski siz bilan rozi bo'lardi.

Bob Cherch–Tyuring tezisining turli versiyalarini — «fikrlash mexanik hisoblashga keltirilishi mumkinmi?» — ko'rib chiqadi, hind matematigi Ramanujan va hisoblovchi vunderkindlar haqida gapiradi va Tarskining haqiqatni formal tizim ichida aniqlab bo'lmasligi haqidagi teoremasini tushuntiradi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob texnik matematikadan falsafaga ko'prik. Asosiy savol: miya qiladigan har qanday narsani kompyuter dasturi ham qila oladimi? Hofstadter bir nechta javobni yonma-yon qo'yadi va o'zinikini aniq aytadi.

chapters.title: Chapter XVIII: Artificial Intelligence: Retrospects
chapters.title_uz: XVIII bob: Sun'iy intellekt — o'tmishga nazar

paras.en: The dialogue before Chapter XVIII, 'SHRDLU, Toy of Man's Designing', is unusual: it is based on a real conversation between a person and a computer program written by Terry Winograd at MIT around 1970. SHRDLU lived in an imaginary world of coloured blocks and pyramids on a table. You could type commands in English — pick up a red block, put it in the box — and ask questions about what it had done and why. For its time, it seemed astonishingly intelligent. The title is a pun on a Bach chorale known in English as 'Jesu, Joy of Man's Desiring'.
paras.uz: XVIII bobdan oldingi «SHRDLU, inson yaratgan o'yinchoq» dialogi g'ayrioddiy: u inson va 1970-yillar atrofida MIT da Terri Vinograd yozgan kompyuter dasturi o'rtasidagi haqiqiy suhbatga asoslangan. SHRDLU stol ustidagi rangli kubiklar va piramidalarning xayoliy dunyosida yashagan. Ingliz tilida buyruqlar yozishingiz mumkin edi — qizil kubikni ol, uni qutiga qo'y — va u nima qilgani va nega qilgani haqida savollar berish mumkin edi. O'z davri uchun u hayratlanarli darajada aqlli tuyulgan. Sarlavha ingliz tilida «Iso, inson orzusining quvonchi» nomi bilan tanilgan Bax xoraliga so'z o'yini.

paras.en: The chapter begins with Alan Turing's famous 1950 paper, 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'. Instead of asking the vague question 'Can machines think?', Turing proposed a test he called the imitation game, now known as the Turing test. A judge talks by typed messages with two hidden partners, one human and one machine. If the judge cannot reliably tell which is which, we should say that the machine thinks. Hofstadter admires the paper and discusses the objections Turing himself anticipated.
paras.uz: Bob Alan Tyuringning mashhur 1950-yilgi «Hisoblash mashinalari va aql» maqolasidan boshlanadi. Noaniq «Mashinalar fikrlay oladimi?» savolini berish o'rniga Tyuring o'zi taqlid o'yini deb atagan, hozir Tyuring testi deb tanilgan testni taklif qilgan. Hakam yozma xabarlar orqali ikki yashirin sherik — bir inson va bir mashina bilan gaplashadi. Agar hakam qaysi biri qaysi ekanini ishonchli ajrata olmasa, mashina fikrlaydi deb aytishimiz kerak. Hofstadter maqolaga qoyil qoladi va Tyuringning o'zi oldindan ko'rgan e'tirozlarni muhokama qiladi.

paras.en: One of those objections comes from Ada Lovelace, the nineteenth-century mathematician who worked with Charles Babbage on his Analytical Engine. She wrote that the machine can do only what we order it to do; it has no power to originate anything. Turing replied that machines often surprise their makers. Hofstadter adds a deeper reply: a program follows its rules at the lowest level, but at a high level its behaviour may be completely unpredictable, just as neurons follow chemistry while people make up poems.
paras.uz: O'sha e'tirozlardan biri XIX asr matematigi, Charlz Bebbij bilan uning Analitik mashinasi ustida ishlagan Ada Lavleysdan keladi. U mashina faqat biz buyurgan narsani qila olishini, hech narsani yaratish qudratiga ega emasligini yozgan. Tyuring mashinalar ko'pincha o'z yaratuvchilarini hayratga solishini aytib javob bergan. Hofstadter chuqurroq javob qo'shadi: dastur eng quyi darajada o'z qoidalariga amal qiladi, lekin yuqori darajada uning xatti-harakati butunlay oldindan aytib bo'lmaydigan bo'lishi mumkin, xuddi neyronlar kimyoga amal qilgani holda odamlar she'r to'qiganidek.

paras.en: Then comes a brief history of AI. Early programs played games: Arthur Samuel's checkers program, in the 1950s, learned from experience and eventually beat its creator. Chess programs used 'look-ahead' — exploring trees of possible moves — but even the best of them in the 1970s played without anything like a human player's sense of the position. Hofstadter explains why: a master does not calculate more moves than a beginner; she sees the board in large meaningful chunks, just as a reader sees words rather than letters.
paras.uz: Keyin SI ning qisqacha tarixi keladi. Ilk dasturlar o'yinlar o'ynagan: Artur Semyuelning 1950-yillardagi shashka dasturi tajribadan o'rgangan va oxir-oqibat o'z yaratuvchisini yutgan. Shaxmat dasturlari «oldinga qarash»dan — mumkin bo'lgan yurishlar daraxtlarini o'rganishdan — foydalangan, lekin 1970-yillardagi eng yaxshilari ham inson o'yinchining pozitsiyani his qilishiga o'xshash hech narsasiz o'ynagan. Hofstadter nega ekanini tushuntiradi: usta yangi boshlovchidan ko'proq yurishlarni hisoblamaydi; u taxtani katta ma'noli bo'laklarda ko'radi, xuddi o'quvchi harflarni emas, so'zlarni ko'rganidek.

paras.en: Hofstadter describes programs that proved theorems in logic and geometry. One famous story concerns a geometry program that found a proof that a triangle with two equal sides has two equal angles. Instead of the usual construction, it compared the triangle with its own mirror image — a proof that seemed elegant and creative. Hofstadter asks: was the program creative, or did it just stumble on a trick that looks creative to us? The question of where creativity lives — in the program, in the programmer, or in the observer — runs through the chapter.
paras.uz: Hofstadter mantiq va geometriyada teoremalarni isbotlagan dasturlarni tasvirlaydi. Mashhur hikoyalardan biri ikki tomoni teng uchburchakning ikki burchagi teng ekanining isbotini topgan geometriya dasturi haqida. Odatiy qurilma o'rniga u uchburchakni o'zining ko'zgudagi aksi bilan solishtirgan — nafis va ijodiy tuyulgan isbot. Hofstadter so'raydi: dastur ijodkor bo'lganmi yoki shunchaki bizga ijodiy ko'rinadigan hiylaga tasodifan duch kelganmi? Ijodkorlik qayerda yashaydi — dasturdami, dasturchidami yoki kuzatuvchidami — degan savol butun bob bo'ylab o'tadi.

paras.en: Then he turns to language. Early machine translation projects in the 1950s were very optimistic, but they failed, because translation requires understanding, not just dictionaries and grammar rules. A sentence like 'The pen is in the box' and 'The box is in the pen' uses 'pen' in two senses — a writing tool and an enclosure for animals — and only world knowledge tells you which. Hofstadter also describes ELIZA, Joseph Weizenbaum's program that imitated a psychotherapist by reflecting the user's words back. People confided in it, though it understood nothing.
paras.uz: Keyin u tilga o'tadi. 1950-yillardagi ilk mashina tarjimasi loyihalari juda optimistik bo'lgan, lekin ular muvaffaqiyatsizlikka uchragan, chunki tarjima shunchaki lug'atlar va grammatika qoidalarini emas, tushunishni talab qiladi. «The pen is in the box» va «The box is in the pen» kabi jumla «pen» so'zini ikki ma'noda — yozuv quroli va hayvonlar uchun qo'ra ma'nosida — ishlatadi va qaysi biri ekanini faqat dunyo haqidagi bilim aytadi. Hofstadter shuningdek Jozef Vaysenbaumning foydalanuvchi so'zlarini unga qaytarib aks ettirib psixoterapevtga taqlid qilgan ELIZA dasturini tasvirlaydi. Odamlar unga sirlarini aytishgan, garchi u hech narsani tushunmagan bo'lsa ham.

paras.en: SHRDLU was much more serious. It had a model of its little world, a grammar of English, and a way to plan actions. It could understand pronouns ('put it on the green one'), ask for clarification when a command was ambiguous, and explain its reasons ('because you asked me to'). Hofstadter shows its strengths and its limits: outside the block world, it knew nothing. The trick of making a tiny world rich enough for real understanding did not easily scale up to the big, messy world of human life.
paras.uz: SHRDLU ancha jiddiyroq edi. Unda o'zining kichik dunyosining modeli, ingliz tili grammatikasi va harakatlarni rejalashtirish usuli bor edi. U olmoshlarni tushuna olardi («uni yashilining ustiga qo'y»), buyruq noaniq bo'lganda aniqlashtirish so'ray olardi va o'z sabablarini tushuntira olardi («chunki siz meni so'radingiz»). Hofstadter uning kuchli tomonlari va chegaralarini ko'rsatadi: kubiklar dunyosidan tashqarida u hech narsani bilmagan. Kichkina dunyoni haqiqiy tushunish uchun yetarlicha boy qilish hiylasi inson hayotining katta, chalkash dunyosiga oson kengaymagan.

paras.en: Hofstadter mentions what he calls Tesler's Theorem, after the computer scientist Larry Tesler: AI is whatever hasn't been done yet. Each time a program does something that once seemed to need intelligence — play chess, prove a theorem, understand a sentence — people decide that this task did not really require intelligence after all. The goalposts keep moving. Hofstadter finds this both funny and revealing: we do not really know what intelligence is, so we define it by what machines cannot yet do.
paras.uz: Hofstadter kompyutershunos Larri Tesler nomi bilan Tesler teoremasi deb ataydigan narsani eslatadi: SI — hali qilinmagan narsa. Har safar dastur bir vaqtlar aql talab qiladigandek tuyulgan narsani — shaxmat o'ynash, teoremani isbotlash, jumlani tushunish — qilganda, odamlar bu vazifa aslida aql talab qilmagan ekan, degan qarorga keladi. Darvoza ustunlari siljib turadi. Hofstadter buni ham kulgili, ham ochib beruvchi deb biladi: biz aql nima ekanini aslida bilmaymiz, shuning uchun uni mashinalar hali qila olmaydigan narsa orqali ta'riflaymiz.

paras.en: Note for today's reader: this chapter was written in 1979, before personal computers became common, long before the internet and decades before modern language models. Many of the difficulties Hofstadter describes — ambiguity, world knowledge, the gap between symbols and meaning — are still debated. Hofstadter himself, in later interviews, has expressed both admiration and deep unease about recent AI systems. Reading this chapter now is like reading an early map: some coasts are wrong, but the questions it asks are still the right ones.
paras.uz: Bugungi o'quvchi uchun izoh: bu bob 1979-yilda, shaxsiy kompyuterlar keng tarqalishidan oldin, internetdan ancha oldin va zamonaviy til modellaridan o'nlab yillar oldin yozilgan. Hofstadter tasvirlagan ko'p qiyinchiliklar — ko'p ma'nolilik, dunyo haqidagi bilim, belgilar va ma'no o'rtasidagi bo'shliq — hali ham bahs-munozara mavzusi. Hofstadterning o'zi keyingi intervyularda so'nggi SI tizimlari haqida ham hayrat, ham chuqur xavotir bildirgan. Bu bobni hozir o'qish ilk xaritani o'qishga o'xshaydi: ba'zi qirg'oqlar noto'g'ri, lekin u bergan savollar hamon to'g'ri savollar.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Program, please put the small pyramid in the box. Program: OK. Achilles: Why did you do that? Program: Because you asked me to. Achilles: Remarkable! Now, what do you think of Bach? Program: I don't understand which block you mean by 'Bach'. Tortoise: There you have it, Achilles — a brilliant mind the size of a tabletop. Achilles: And if we made the table as big as the world? Tortoise: Then, my friend, you would need to teach it everything a child learns by falling off chairs.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Dastur, iltimos, kichik piramidani qutiga qo'y. Dastur: Xo'p. Axilles: Nega buni qilding? Dastur: Chunki siz meni so'radingiz. Axilles: Ajoyib! Endi, Bax haqida nima deb o'ylaysan? Dastur: «Bax» deganda qaysi kubikni nazarda tutayotganingizni tushunmayapman. Toshbaqa: Mana, Axilles — stol yuzasidek kattalikdagi ajoyib aql. Axilles: Agar stolni dunyodek katta qilsak-chi? Toshbaqa: Unda, do'stim, unga bola stullardan yiqilib o'rganadigan hamma narsani o'rgatishing kerak bo'lardi.

quiz.q: What is the Turing test?
o: A judge tries to tell a human from a machine by typed conversation
quiz.why_uz: Taqlid o'yini: hakam yozma suhbat orqali inson va mashinani ajratishga urinadi.

quiz.q: What is 'Tesler's Theorem'?
o: AI is whatever hasn't been done yet
quiz.why_uz: Mashina biror narsani qilganda, odamlar uni «aslida aql emas» deb qaror qiladi.

quiz.q: What was SHRDLU's main limitation?
o: It knew nothing outside its block world
quiz.why_uz: Kubiklar dunyosidan tashqarida u hech narsani bilmagan.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi dialog Terri Vinogradning SHRDLU dasturi — kubiklar dunyosida ingliz tilida buyruqlarni tushunadigan dastur — bilan suhbatni ko'rsatadi. Bob SI tarixini ko'rib chiqadi: Tyuringning 1950-yilgi «taqlid o'yini», Ledi Lavleysning e'tirozi, shaxmat va shashka dasturlari, teorema isbotlovchi dasturlar, ELIZA, mashina tarjimasi va SHRDLU. Hofstadter «Tesler teoremasi»ni eslatadi: SI — hali qilinmagan narsa.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob 1979-yildagi holatni tasvirlaydi. Bugungi til modellari zamonida o'qiganda, ko'p bashoratlar va muammolar qanchalik o'zgarganini (yoki o'zgarmaganini) solishtirish qiziq.

chapters.title: Chapter XIX: Artificial Intelligence: Prospects
chapters.title_uz: XIX bob: Sun'iy intellekt — kelajakka nazar

paras.en: In the dialogue before Chapter XIX, 'Contrafactus', Achilles and the Sloth watch a football game on a strange television that can show 'subjunctive instant replays' — not what happened, but what would have happened if something had been different. What if the ball had been a little to the left? What if the game had been played in three dimensions instead of four? Some changes seem natural, others absurd. The dialogue raises the question: which features of a situation do we feel free to 'slip', and which do we hold fixed?
paras.uz: XIX bobdan oldingi «Kontrafaktus» dialogida Axilles va Yalqov (hayvon) «shart mayli bo'yicha zudlik bilan qayta ko'rsatish»larni — nima bo'lganini emas, agar nimadir boshqacha bo'lganida nima bo'lishini — ko'rsata oladigan g'alati televizorda futbol o'yinini tomosha qilishadi. Agar to'p biroz chaproqda bo'lganida-chi? Agar o'yin to'rt o'lchov o'rniga uch o'lchovda o'ynalganida-chi? Ba'zi o'zgarishlar tabiiy, boshqalari bema'ni tuyuladi. Dialog savol qo'yadi: vaziyatning qaysi xususiyatlarini «siljitishga» o'zimizni erkin his qilamiz va qaysilarini qattiq ushlab turamiz?

paras.en: Hofstadter argues that this ability is at the heart of intelligence. Every day we think of 'near misses' — I almost caught the train; if I had left a minute earlier... — and such thoughts help us learn. The interesting question is why some counterfactuals come to mind easily and others never do. Nobody thinks 'if only there had been fewer prime numbers, I would have caught the train'. Our minds have a sense of which concepts are 'slippable' and how far they can slip. A thinking machine would need the same sense.
paras.uz: Hofstadter bu qobiliyat aqlning yuragida ekanini ta'kidlaydi. Har kuni biz «sal qoldi»lar haqida o'ylaymiz — poyezdga sal qoldi ulgurishimga; agar bir daqiqa oldin chiqqanimda... — va bunday fikrlar bizga o'rganishga yordam beradi. Qiziq savol — nega ba'zi kontrafaktuallar xayolga oson keladi, boshqalari esa hech qachon. Hech kim «qaniydi tub sonlar kamroq bo'lganida, poyezdga ulgurardim» deb o'ylamaydi. Aqlimizda qaysi tushunchalar «sirpanuvchan» ekanini va ular qanchalik uzoqqa sirpanishi mumkinligini his qilish bor. Fikrlovchi mashinaga xuddi shunday his kerak bo'lardi.

paras.en: He connects slippability to analogy. When we see that two situations are 'the same' in some deep way — the Ant Fugue and a brain, Gödel's sentence and DNA — we are letting some features slip while keeping the essential structure. Analogy-making, for Hofstadter, is not a special skill used occasionally; it is the core of all thinking. (His later work, in books such as Fluid Concepts and Creative Analogies and Surfaces and Essences, developed this idea for decades.)
paras.uz: U sirpanuvchanlikni o'xshatish bilan bog'laydi. Ikki vaziyat qandaydir chuqur tarzda «bir xil» ekanini — Chumoli fugasi va miya, Gödel jumlasi va DNK — ko'rganimizda, biz muhim tuzilmani saqlab qolgan holda ba'zi xususiyatlarning sirpanishiga yo'l qo'yamiz. Hofstadter uchun o'xshatish yasash vaqti-vaqti bilan ishlatiladigan alohida ko'nikma emas; u barcha fikrlashning o'zagi. (Uning keyingi ishlari, «Suyuq tushunchalar va ijodiy o'xshatishlar» va «Sirtlar va mohiyatlar» kabi kitoblarda, bu g'oyani o'nlab yillar davomida rivojlantirgan.)

paras.en: To show how understanding might work in a machine, Hofstadter discusses 'frames', an idea of the AI researcher Marvin Minsky. A frame is a structure for a typical situation — a birthday party, a restaurant, a room — with slots for the expected parts: a host, a cake, guests. When we enter a situation, we bring a frame and fill its slots, using default values for what we cannot see. Frames can be nested inside other frames and can be swapped when a situation turns out to be different from what we expected.
paras.uz: Mashinada tushunish qanday ishlashi mumkinligini ko'rsatish uchun Hofstadter SI tadqiqotchisi Marvin Minskiyning g'oyasi bo'lgan «freymlar»ni muhokama qiladi. Freym — odatiy vaziyat uchun tuzilma — tug'ilgan kun ziyofati, restoran, xona — kutilgan qismlar uchun uyalar bilan: mezbon, tort, mehmonlar. Vaziyatga kirganimizda freym olib kelamiz va uning uyalarini to'ldiramiz, ko'ra olmaydigan narsalar uchun standart qiymatlardan foydalanamiz. Freymlar boshqa freymlar ichiga joylashtirilishi va vaziyat kutganimizdan boshqacha bo'lib chiqqanda almashtirilishi mumkin.

paras.en: The heart of the chapter is a long discussion of Bongard problems, invented by the Russian scientist Mikhail Bongard. Each problem shows twelve boxes: six on the left share some property, six on the right share a different one. The task is to find the rule. Sometimes it is simple — circles versus triangles — and sometimes subtle — figures with a line inside versus figures with a line outside, or 'the small shape is closer to the big one' versus 'further away'. Solving them requires seeing the boxes at the right level of description.
paras.uz: Bobning yuragi — rus olimi Mixail Bongard ixtiro qilgan Bongard masalalarining uzun muhokamasi. Har bir masala o'n ikkita qutichani ko'rsatadi: chapdagi oltitasi qandaydir xususiyatga ega, o'ngdagi oltitasi boshqasiga. Vazifa — qoidani topish. Ba'zan u oddiy — doiralarga qarshi uchburchaklar — ba'zan nozik — ichida chiziq bor shakllar va tashqarisida chiziq bor shakllar yoki «kichik shakl kattasiga yaqinroq» va «uzoqroq». Ularni yechish qutichalarni to'g'ri tavsif darajasida ko'rishni talab qiladi.

paras.en: Hofstadter sketches how a program might solve Bongard problems. It would start by describing each box with simple features, then build higher-level descriptions, compare the two sides, notice partial patterns, try a hypothesis, and back off when the hypothesis fails. Crucially, it would need to be able to restructure its descriptions — to see a figure as 'a triangle' at one moment and as 'three lines' at another. Perception, in this view, is not passive reception; it is active, flexible description at many levels.
paras.uz: Hofstadter dastur Bongard masalalarini qanday yechishi mumkinligini chizib beradi. U har bir qutichani oddiy xususiyatlar bilan tasvirlashdan boshlaydi, keyin yuqoriroq darajadagi tavsiflarni quradi, ikki tomonni solishtiradi, qisman naqshlarni payqaydi, gipotezani sinaydi va gipoteza muvaffaqiyatsiz bo'lganda orqaga chekinadi. Eng muhimi, u o'z tavsiflarini qayta tuzish qobiliyatiga ega bo'lishi kerak — shaklni bir lahzada «uchburchak», boshqa lahzada «uchta chiziq» sifatida ko'rish. Bu qarashda idrok passiv qabul qilish emas; u ko'p darajalardagi faol, moslashuvchan tavsif.

paras.en: Hofstadter also discusses music and AI. Could a program compose music as moving as Chopin's or Bach's? He is doubtful that this will happen soon. Music, in his view, expresses the deepest patterns of human emotion, which come from a lifetime of living in the world. A program that composed truly great music would have to understand — in some sense feel — what it is to be human. Ironically, he suggests that such a program would be nearly as hard to build as a whole artificial person.
paras.uz: Hofstadter shuningdek musiqa va SI ni muhokama qiladi. Dastur Shopen yoki Baxnikidek ta'sirli musiqa basta qila oladimi? U bu tez orada sodir bo'lishiga shubha qiladi. Uning fikricha, musiqa dunyoda butun umr yashashdan kelib chiqadigan inson his-tuyg'ularining eng chuqur naqshlarini ifodalaydi. Haqiqatan buyuk musiqa bastalaydigan dastur inson bo'lish nima ekanini tushunishi — qandaydir ma'noda his qilishi — kerak bo'lardi. Kinoyali tarzda, u bunday dasturni qurish butun bir sun'iy insonni qurishdek qiyin bo'lishini taklif qiladi.

paras.en: The chapter ends with 'Ten Questions and Speculations', in which Hofstadter gives his own predictions. Will a computer ever write beautiful music? Yes, but not soon. Will emotions be programmable? Not directly — they would emerge from a complex system. Will an intelligent program be able to add fast? Perhaps not — its intelligence would live at a level far above its arithmetic circuits, just as ours does. And will there be chess programs that can beat anyone? His answer was: no — such programs would be general intelligences who might not even want to play.
paras.uz: Bob «O'nta savol va taxmin» bilan tugaydi, unda Hofstadter o'z bashoratlarini beradi. Kompyuter qachondir go'zal musiqa yoza oladimi? Ha, lekin tez orada emas. His-tuyg'ularni dasturlash mumkin bo'ladimi? To'g'ridan-to'g'ri emas — ular murakkab tizimdan paydo bo'lardi. Aqlli dastur tez qo'sha oladimi? Balki yo'q — uning aqli, bizniki kabi, arifmetik sxemalaridan ancha yuqori darajada yashardi. Va kimni bo'lsa ham yuta oladigan shaxmat dasturlari bo'ladimi? Uning javobi: yo'q — bunday dasturlar o'ynashni xohlamasligi ham mumkin bo'lgan umumiy aqllar bo'lardi.

paras.en: Note for today's reader: the chess prediction was wrong. In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue defeated the world champion Garry Kasparov, and it did so mostly through enormous search, not through human-like understanding. Hofstadter later admitted the mistake and found it instructive: tasks we think require general intelligence sometimes yield to narrow, powerful methods. Some of his other predictions — about music, translation and emotion — are being tested today in ways he could not have imagined in 1979.
paras.uz: Bugungi o'quvchi uchun izoh: shaxmat haqidagi bashorat noto'g'ri chiqdi. 1997-yilda IBM ning Deep Blue dasturi jahon chempioni Garri Kasparovni yutdi va buni asosan inson kabi tushunish orqali emas, ulkan qidiruv orqali qildi. Keyinchalik Hofstadter xatoni tan oldi va uni ibratli deb topdi: biz umumiy aql talab qiladi deb o'ylaydigan vazifalar ba'zan tor, kuchli usullarga bo'ysunadi. Uning musiqa, tarjima va his-tuyg'ular haqidagi boshqa ba'zi bashoratlari bugun u 1979-yilda tasavvur ham qila olmagan tarzlarda sinovdan o'tmoqda.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Look, a replay! The goalkeeper missed — but here's what would have happened if he'd caught it. Sloth: Charming. Now show me what would happen if the ball were a cube. Achilles: A cube? That's silly — it wouldn't roll! Sloth: And if the field were a Möbius strip? Achilles: Now you're just being difficult. Tortoise: No, Achilles — he is asking the real question: why do some 'what ifs' feel natural and others ridiculous? Achilles: Because... some things can slip and some can't? Tortoise: Exactly. And knowing which is which is half of being intelligent.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Qara, qayta ko'rsatish! Darvozabon o'tkazib yubordi — lekin mana, agar u ushlab qolganida nima bo'lardi. Yalqov: Yoqimli. Endi to'p kub bo'lganida nima bo'lishini ko'rsat. Axilles: Kub? Bu bema'nilik — u dumalamasdi! Yalqov: Maydon Myobius tasmasi bo'lganida-chi? Axilles: Endi shunchaki qiyinchilik tug'diryapsan. Toshbaqa: Yo'q, Axilles — u haqiqiy savolni beryapti: nega ba'zi «agar»lar tabiiy, boshqalari kulgili tuyuladi? Axilles: Chunki... ba'zi narsalar sirpana oladi, ba'zilari esa yo'qmi? Toshbaqa: Aynan. Qaysi biri qaysi ekanini bilish esa aqlli bo'lishning yarmi.

quiz.q: What is a Bongard problem?
o: Twelve boxes; find the rule that separates the left six from the right six
quiz.why_uz: Chapdagi oltita va o'ngdagi oltita qutichani ajratadigan qoidani topish.

quiz.q: Why does Hofstadter think counterfactuals matter for AI?
o: Knowing which features can 'slip' is at the heart of intelligence
quiz.why_uz: Sirpanuvchanlik va o'xshatish — fikrlashning o'zagi.

quiz.q: Which of Hofstadter's 1979 predictions turned out wrong?
o: That no chess program would beat everyone
quiz.why_uz: 1997-yilda Deep Blue Kasparovni yutdi.

chapters.recap_uz: Bobdan oldingi «Kontrafaktus» dialogida qahramonlar «agar shunday bo'lganida» dunyolariga sayohat qiladi. Bob SI kelajagi haqida: aql «sirpanuvchan» tushunchalar, o'xshatishlar va «nima bo'lardi?» degan tasavvurga asoslanadi. Hofstadter freymlar, Bongard masalalari, musiqa va SI, va SI haqidagi o'nta savolga o'z javoblarini beradi. Uning shaxmat haqidagi bashorati keyinchalik noto'g'ri chiqqan.
chapters.note_uz: «Kontrafaktual» — haqiqatga zid «agar» gapi: «Agar kecha yomg'ir yog'maganda edi...». Hofstadter bunday gaplarni yasash qobiliyati aqlning yuragida ekanini ta'kidlaydi.

chapters.title: Chapter XX: Strange Loops, or Tangled Hierarchies
chapters.title_uz: XX bob: G'alati halqalar yoki chigal ierarxiyalar

paras.en: The dialogue before the last chapter, 'Sloth Canon', is itself built like one of Bach's canons, with one speaker's lines answered by another's in inverted form. It is a reminder that form and content have been intertwined throughout the book. Chapter XX then gathers all the threads. Its subject is the 'tangled hierarchy': a system with levels, in which the levels do not simply stack one above the other but loop back, so that a lower level reaches up and affects the level that is supposed to control it.
paras.uz: So'nggi bobdan oldingi «Yalqov kanoni» dialogi o'zi Baxning kanonlaridan biri kabi qurilgan, bir so'zlovchining satrlariga boshqasining satrlari teskari shaklda javob beradi. Bu shakl va mazmun butun kitob davomida bir-biriga chirmashib kelganini eslatadi. Keyin XX bob barcha iplarni yig'adi. Uning mavzusi — «chigal ierarxiya»: darajalari bor, lekin darajalar shunchaki bir-birining ustiga taxlanmaydigan, balki qaytib aylanadigan tizim, shuning uchun quyi daraja yuqoriga cho'zilib, uni boshqarishi kerak bo'lgan darajaga ta'sir qiladi.

paras.en: A simple example is a game whose moves can change its own rules. Hofstadter imagines a version of chess in which each move also alters the rules for later moves — and then a game in which the rules for changing the rules can themselves be changed, and so on upward. Legal systems are similar: a constitution sets the rules for making laws, but courts interpret the constitution, and sometimes the constitution itself is amended by procedures it defines. There is always an 'inviolate level' — the most basic rules, or the physical world — that does not change, but above it the levels can tangle.
paras.uz: Oddiy misol — yurishlari o'z qoidalarini o'zgartira oladigan o'yin. Hofstadter har bir yurish keyingi yurishlar qoidalarini ham o'zgartiradigan shaxmat versiyasini tasavvur qiladi — keyin esa qoidalarni o'zgartirish qoidalarining o'zi ham o'zgarishi mumkin bo'lgan o'yinni va hokazo yuqoriga qarab. Huquqiy tizimlar ham shunga o'xshash: konstitutsiya qonunlar chiqarish qoidalarini belgilaydi, lekin sudlar konstitutsiyani talqin qiladi va ba'zan konstitutsiyaning o'zi u belgilagan tartiblar bilan o'zgartiriladi. Doim o'zgarmaydigan «daxlsiz daraja» — eng asosiy qoidalar yoki fizik dunyo — bor, lekin uning ustida darajalar chigallashishi mumkin.

paras.en: Escher's art provides the clearest pictures. In 'Drawing Hands' (1948), a left hand draws a right hand, which draws the left hand. Each hand is both creator and created. Hofstadter points out that the tangle is only apparent: outside the picture, there is an invisible third hand — Escher's — which drew both. The strange loop exists at one level, but there is an inviolate level beyond it. He suggests that the same is true of the mind: the self seems to create itself, but underneath, neurons obey physics.
paras.uz: Escher san'ati eng aniq rasmlarni beradi. «Chizayotgan qo'llar» (1948) asarida chap qo'l o'ng qo'lni chizadi, o'ng qo'l esa chap qo'lni chizadi. Har bir qo'l ham yaratuvchi, ham yaratilgan. Hofstadter chigallik faqat ko'rinishda ekanini ta'kidlaydi: rasmdan tashqarida ikkalasini chizgan ko'rinmas uchinchi qo'l — Escherniki — bor. G'alati halqa bir darajada mavjud, lekin undan narida daxlsiz daraja bor. U aql uchun ham shunday ekanini taklif qiladi: «men» o'zini o'zi yaratayotgandek tuyuladi, lekin ostida neyronlar fizikaga bo'ysunadi.

paras.en: Even more striking is Escher's 'Print Gallery' (1956). A young man in a gallery looks at a print of a town by the sea; in the town there is a building, and in the building is a gallery — the very gallery in which the young man stands. The picture contains itself. Escher could not complete the loop at the centre, and left a white patch there. (Decades after Hofstadter's book, in 2003, mathematicians showed how the missing centre could be filled in, using the mathematics of the picture's distortion.) The young man is inside the picture he is looking at.
paras.uz: Escherning «Rasm galereyasi» (1956) asari bundan ham hayratlanarliroq. Galereyadagi yigit dengiz bo'yidagi shahar tasvirlangan gravyuraga qarayapti; shaharda bino bor, binoda galereya bor — aynan yigit turgan galereya. Rasm o'zini o'z ichiga oladi. Escher halqani markazda yakunlay olmagan va u yerda oq dog' qoldirgan. (Hofstadter kitobidan o'nlab yillar o'tib, 2003-yilda matematiklar rasmning buzilish matematikasidan foydalanib, yetishmayotgan markazni qanday to'ldirish mumkinligini ko'rsatishdi.) Yigit o'zi qarayotgan rasmning ichida.

paras.en: René Magritte's paintings play with the relation between picture and reality. His famous painting of a pipe, with words beneath it saying that this is not a pipe, reminds us that a picture of a pipe is not a pipe — a symbol is not the thing it stands for. Other paintings show a painted canvas on an easel in front of a window, exactly covering the view it depicts, so that we cannot tell where the painting ends and the 'real' landscape begins. Hofstadter uses these images to show how symbols and the world can become tangled in a mind.
paras.uz: Rene Magrittning rasmlari tasvir va voqelik o'rtasidagi munosabat bilan o'ynaydi. Uning ostida bu chilim emasligini aytuvchi so'zlar yozilgan mashhur chilim rasmi chilim rasmi chilim emasligini — belgi o'zi ifodalaydigan narsa emasligini eslatadi. Boshqa rasmlar deraza oldidagi molbertda o'zi tasvirlagan manzarani aniq to'sib turgan bo'yalgan polotnoni ko'rsatadi, shuning uchun rasm qayerda tugashini va «haqiqiy» manzara qayerdan boshlanishini ajrata olmaymiz. Hofstadter bu tasvirlardan belgilar va dunyo aqlda qanday chigallashishi mumkinligini ko'rsatish uchun foydalanadi.

paras.en: Then the idea spreads to other fields. In science, the observer is part of the world being observed. In music, Bach's endlessly rising canon from the Musical Offering returns to its starting key after climbing through all the others. And Gödel's sentence is a tangled hierarchy too: a statement of arithmetic (the low level) that is also a statement about arithmetic (the high level). In all these cases, a system that represents itself folds back on its own levels.
paras.uz: Keyin g'oya boshqa sohalarga yoyiladi. Fanda kuzatuvchi kuzatilayotgan dunyoning bir qismi. Musiqada Baxning «Musiqiy tortiq»dagi cheksiz ko'tariluvchi kanoni boshqa barcha tonalliklardan o'tib, boshlang'ich tonalligiga qaytadi. Gödel jumlasi ham chigal ierarxiya: arifmetikaning gapi (quyi daraja), ayni paytda arifmetika haqidagi gap (yuqori daraja). Bu holatlarning barchasida o'zini ifodalaydigan tizim o'z darajalariga qaytib buklanadi.

paras.en: Now the central claim of the whole book. The brain contains symbols — active patterns of neurons that stand for concepts. Among these symbols is one that represents the brain's owner: the self-symbol. The self-symbol is connected to all the others, and it represents the brain's own activity, at a very high level. When the self-symbol becomes rich enough, the brain begins to perceive itself, think about itself, and act on the basis of its picture of itself. This loop — a pattern that represents the system that contains it — is what we call 'I'.
paras.uz: Endi butun kitobning markaziy da'vosi. Miya belgilarni — tushunchalarni ifodalaydigan neyronlarning faol naqshlarini — o'z ichiga oladi. Bu belgilar orasida miya egasini ifodalaydigan biri bor: «men»-belgi. «Men»-belgi qolganlarning barchasi bilan bog'langan va u miyaning o'z faoliyatini juda yuqori darajada ifodalaydi. «Men»-belgi yetarlicha boy bo'lganda, miya o'zini idrok qila, o'zi haqida o'ylay va o'zi haqidagi tasviriga asoslanib harakat qila boshlaydi. Bu halqa — o'zini o'z ichiga olgan tizimni ifodalaydigan naqsh — biz «men» deb ataydigan narsa.

paras.en: This gives Hofstadter a view of free will. The neurons obey physical laws; at that level, there are no choices. But at the level of symbols, the self-symbol takes part in decisions: it considers options, imagines outcomes and weighs them. We feel free because we do not see the low level; we see only our high-level reasons. A helpful comparison (ours, in the spirit of the book) is a chess program that, if it could describe itself, would say 'I decided to move my knight', even though, underneath, it is running fixed rules. Freedom lives at the level of the loop.
paras.uz: Bu Hofstadterga iroda erkinligi haqida qarash beradi. Neyronlar fizik qonunlarga bo'ysunadi; o'sha darajada tanlovlar yo'q. Lekin belgilar darajasida «men»-belgi qarorlarda ishtirok etadi: u variantlarni ko'rib chiqadi, natijalarni tasavvur qiladi va ularni tortib ko'radi. Biz o'zimizni erkin his qilamiz, chunki quyi darajani ko'rmaymiz; biz faqat yuqori darajadagi sabablarimizni ko'ramiz. Foydali qiyos (bizniki, kitob ruhida) — agar o'zini tasvirlay olganida, ostida qat'iy qoidalarni bajarayotgan bo'lsa ham, «Men otimni yurishga qaror qildim» deydigan shaxmat dasturi. Erkinlik halqa darajasida yashaydi.

paras.en: Gödel's theorem, in this picture, becomes a metaphor for the self. Just as TNT cannot fully prove all truths about itself, a self cannot fully understand itself: the self-symbol is always a simplified model of a far more complex brain. There will always be things about ourselves that we cannot see from the inside. Hofstadter finds this not depressing but beautiful. The mystery of consciousness, he suggests, is the feeling of being a strange loop — a system that sees itself, but never completely.
paras.uz: Bu manzarada Gödel teoremasi «men» uchun metaforaga aylanadi. TNT o'zi haqidagi barcha haqiqatlarni to'liq isbotlay olmaganidek, «men» ham o'zini to'liq tushuna olmaydi: «men»-belgi doim ancha murakkabroq miyaning soddalashtirilgan modeli. Doim o'zimiz haqida ichkaridan ko'ra olmaydigan narsalar bo'ladi. Hofstadter buni tushkunlikka soluvchi emas, go'zal deb biladi. Ong siri, deb taklif qiladi u, g'alati halqa bo'lish hissi — o'zini ko'radigan, lekin hech qachon to'liq ko'rmaydigan tizim.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, I've been thinking about thinking, and now I'm thinking about thinking about thinking. Tortoise: Careful — you're becoming a strange loop. Achilles: Is that dangerous? Tortoise: Not at all. You've been one since you were a baby. You just noticed. Achilles: But who is doing the noticing? Tortoise: The same loop, looking at itself. Achilles: Like Escher's hands drawing each other? Tortoise: Yes — though, somewhere outside the picture, there is still a hand of neurons and chemistry holding the pen. Achilles: Then I am both the drawing and the drawer. Tortoise: And never quite either. Welcome to being yourself.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, men fikrlash haqida o'ylayapman, endi esa fikrlash haqida o'ylash haqida o'ylayapman. Toshbaqa: Ehtiyot bo'l — sen g'alati halqaga aylanyapsan. Axilles: Bu xavflimi? Toshbaqa: Umuman yo'q. Sen go'dakligingdan beri shundaysan. Shunchaki payqading. Axilles: Lekin payqayotgan kim? Toshbaqa: O'sha halqa, o'ziga qarab. Axilles: Escherning bir-birini chizayotgan qo'llari kabimi? Toshbaqa: Ha — garchi rasmdan tashqarida qayerdadir qalamni ushlab turgan neyronlar va kimyo qo'li hamon bo'lsa ham. Axilles: Unda men ham rasm, ham chizuvchiman. Toshbaqa: Va hech qachon to'liq biri ham emas. O'zing bo'lishga xush kelibsan.

quiz.q: What is a 'tangled hierarchy'?
o: A system of levels that loop back, so a lower level affects the higher
quiz.why_uz: Darajalar qaytib aylanadi — quyi daraja yuqorisiga ta'sir qiladi.

quiz.q: In 'Drawing Hands', what is the 'inviolate level'?
o: Escher's own hand outside the picture
quiz.why_uz: Ikkala qo'lni chizgan ko'rinmas uchinchi qo'l — Escherniki.

quiz.q: According to Hofstadter, what is the 'I'?
o: A soul separate from the brain
A strange loop: the self-symbol representing the brain that contains it
quiz.why_uz: «Men» — o'zini o'z ichiga olgan tizimni ifodalaydigan naqsh.

chapters.recap_uz: Kitobning yakuniy bobi barcha iplarni bog'laydi. Hofstadter «chigal ierarxiya»ni — darajalar bir-biriga qaytib aylanadigan tizimni — ta'riflaydi va uni huquqda, san'atda (Escherning «Chizayotgan qo'llar», «Rasm galereyasi», Magritt), fan va musiqada ko'rsatadi. Asosiy da'vo: «men» — miyaning o'z-o'ziga ishora qiluvchi belgilari yaratgan g'alati halqa; iroda erkinligi va ong shu halqadan kelib chiqadi.
chapters.note_uz: Bu bob butun kitobning javobi. Agar avvalgi boblar «qanday?» degan savolga javob bergan bo'lsa, bu bob «nega bu muhim?» degan savolga javob beradi: chunki biz o'zimiz g'alati halqalarmiz.

chapters.title: Six-Part Ricercar and Afterword
chapters.title_uz: Olti ovozli rikerkar va yakuniy so'z

paras.en: The last dialogue, 'Six-Part Ricercar', brings together Achilles, the Tortoise, the Crab and other characters at a musical evening. Its form imitates the six-voice ricercar from Bach's Musical Offering — the hardest piece in that collection, which Bach composed on the theme given to him by King Frederick. In the course of the conversation the characters return to the story of Bach's visit to Potsdam, so that the book ends where it began, in the Introduction. The final words, in effect, lead the reader back to the start.
paras.uz: So'nggi dialog — «Olti ovozli rikerkar» — Axilles, Toshbaqa, Qisqichbaqa va boshqa qahramonlarni musiqiy kechada yig'adi. Uning shakli Baxning «Musiqiy tortiq»idagi olti ovozli rikerkarga taqlid qiladi — bu to'plamdagi eng qiyin asar, Bax uni qirol Fridrix bergan mavzu asosida bastalagan. Suhbat davomida qahramonlar Baxning Potsdamga tashrifi hikoyasiga qaytadi, shuning uchun kitob boshlangan joyda — Kirishda tugaydi. Yakuniy so'zlar, mohiyatan, o'quvchini boshiga qaytaradi.

paras.en: This circular ending is deliberate. The whole book has been about systems that loop back on themselves — canons that return to their starting key, sentences that talk about themselves, cells that build their own builders, selves that perceive themselves. A book that simply ended would have contradicted its own message. By returning to its opening, GEB becomes the thing it describes: a strange loop. This is one more example of the book's favourite trick, the unity of form and content.
paras.uz: Bu doiraviy yakun ataylab qilingan. Butun kitob o'ziga qaytib aylanadigan tizimlar haqida bo'lgan — boshlang'ich tonalligiga qaytadigan kanonlar, o'zi haqida gapiradigan jumlalar, o'z quruvchilarini quradigan hujayralar, o'zini idrok qiladigan «men»lar. Shunchaki tugaydigan kitob o'z xabariga zid kelgan bo'lardi. O'z boshiga qaytib, GEB o'zi tasvirlaydigan narsaga aylanadi: g'alati halqaga. Bu kitobning sevimli hiylasining yana bir misoli — shakl va mazmun birligi.

paras.en: What is the book's legacy? Gödel, Escher, Bach won the Pulitzer Prize for general non-fiction in 1980 and became an unexpected bestseller. Many people who later became computer scientists, cognitive scientists and philosophers have said that it changed their lives, by showing them that logic, art and the mind could be studied together. Its style — mixing playful dialogues with serious explanation — inspired a whole genre of popular science books. And its central question, how meaning and selves can arise from meaningless parts, is more urgent now than ever.
paras.uz: Kitobning merosi nima? «Gödel, Escher, Bax» 1980-yilda badiiy bo'lmagan umumiy adabiyot bo'yicha Pulitser mukofotini qo'lga kiritgan va kutilmagan bestsellerga aylangan. Keyinchalik kompyutershunos, kognitiv olim va faylasuf bo'lgan ko'p odamlar u ularning hayotini o'zgartirganini — mantiq, san'at va aqlni birga o'rganish mumkinligini ko'rsatganini aytishgan. Uning uslubi — o'ynoqi dialoglarni jiddiy tushuntirish bilan aralashtirish — ilmiy-ommabop kitoblarning butun bir janrini ilhomlantirgan. Va uning markaziy savoli — ma'no va «men»lar ma'nosiz qismlardan qanday paydo bo'lishi mumkin — hozir har qachongidan ham dolzarbroq.

paras.en: Hofstadter himself felt that many readers missed the main point. In the preface to the twentieth-anniversary edition (1999), he explained that the book is not mainly about mathematics, music or art, but about the question of what an 'I' is. In 2007 he published I Am a Strange Loop, a more direct and personal book on the same theme, partly written after the death of his wife Carol. In it he argues that a person's 'I' can partly live on in the brains of those who knew and loved them, because their patterns are copied there at a lower resolution.
paras.uz: Hofstadterning o'zi ko'p o'quvchilar asosiy fikrni o'tkazib yuborganini his qilgan. Yigirma yillik yubiley nashrining (1999) so'zboshisida u kitob asosan matematika, musiqa yoki san'at haqida emas, balki «men» nima degan savol haqida ekanini tushuntirgan. 2007-yilda u xuddi shu mavzudagi to'g'ridanroq va shaxsiyroq kitob — «Men — g'alati halqa»ni nashr etgan, u qisman rafiqasi Kerolning vafotidan keyin yozilgan. Unda u inson «men»i uni bilgan va sevgan odamlarning miyalarida qisman yashashda davom etishi mumkin, chunki uning naqshlari u yerda pastroq aniqlikda nusxalanadi, deb ta'kidlaydi.

paras.en: The book has its critics. Some mathematicians feel that its use of Gödel's theorem as a metaphor for the self goes beyond what the theorem actually says: Gödel's result is about formal systems of arithmetic, and the brain is not obviously one. Some philosophers, such as John Searle, argue that symbol manipulation, however complex, can never produce real understanding. Others find the book too long, or the puns too many. These criticisms are worth knowing — reading GEB well means arguing with it, as Achilles argues with the Tortoise.
paras.uz: Kitobning tanqidchilari bor. Ba'zi matematiklar Gödel teoremasidan «men» uchun metafora sifatida foydalanish teorema aslida aytadigan narsadan oshib ketadi, deb hisoblaydi: Gödel natijasi arifmetikaning formal tizimlari haqida, miya esa aniq shunday tizim emas. Ba'zi faylasuflar, masalan Jon Syorl, belgilarni boshqarish qanchalik murakkab bo'lmasin, hech qachon haqiqiy tushunishni hosil qila olmaydi, deb ta'kidlaydi. Boshqalar kitobni juda uzun yoki so'z o'yinlarini juda ko'p deb topadi. Bu tanqidlarni bilish foydali — GEB ni yaxshi o'qish, Axilles Toshbaqa bilan bahslashgani kabi, u bilan bahslashishni anglatadi.

paras.en: How should you read the book after this study edition? Do not try to read it in one go. Read a dialogue, then its chapter, then stop and think. Do the MU-puzzle with a pencil. Listen to Bach's Musical Offering and the Goldberg Variations while you read. Look at Escher's prints in a good book or online collection. When a chapter is too technical, skim it and come back later — the dialogues will often explain the idea in a lighter way. Many readers return to GEB several times over the years and find a different book each time.
paras.uz: Bu o'quv nashridan keyin kitobni qanday o'qish kerak? Uni bir o'tirishda o'qishga urinmang. Dialogni o'qing, keyin uning bobini, keyin to'xtab o'ylang. MU-boshqotirmani qalam bilan bajaring. O'qish davomida Baxning «Musiqiy tortiq»i va «Goldberg variatsiyalari»ni tinglang. Escherning gravyuralariga yaxshi kitobda yoki onlayn to'plamda qarang. Bob juda texnik bo'lsa, ko'z yugurtirib chiqing va keyinroq qayting — dialoglar ko'pincha g'oyani yengilroq tarzda tushuntiradi. Ko'p o'quvchilar yillar davomida GEB ga bir necha marta qaytadi va har safar boshqa kitob topadi.

paras.en: A note about this WordDrop edition. Gödel, Escher, Bach is protected by copyright, so we cannot reproduce Hofstadter's text or his dialogues. Everything you have read here — the explanations, the translations and the short 'Scenes' between Achilles, the Tortoise, the Crab and others — was written for WordDrop to help you understand the ideas and practise English. The Scenes are our own small dialogues, written in the spirit of the book; they are not quotations. To experience the real dialogues — their wordplay, their musical structure, their acrostics — read the original book.
paras.uz: Bu WordDrop nashri haqida izoh. «Gödel, Escher, Bax» mualliflik huquqi bilan himoyalangan, shuning uchun biz Hofstadter matnini yoki uning dialoglarini ko'chira olmaymiz. Bu yerda o'qiganlaringizning hammasi — tushuntirishlar, tarjimalar va Axilles, Toshbaqa, Qisqichbaqa va boshqalar o'rtasidagi qisqa «Sahnalar» — g'oyalarni tushunishingizga va ingliz tilini mashq qilishingizga yordam berish uchun WordDrop uchun yozilgan. Sahnalar — kitob ruhida yozilgan o'zimizning kichik dialoglarimiz; ular iqtibos emas. Haqiqiy dialoglarni — ularning so'z o'yinlarini, musiqiy tuzilishini, akrostixlarini — his qilish uchun asl kitobni o'qing.

paras.en: Finally, a thought to take with you. Throughout this book you have been doing what Hofstadter describes: reading symbols — English words, Uzbek words, formulas — and building meaning from them at a higher level. Learning a new language is itself a lesson in levels of description: at first you see letters and grammar rules; later, whole sentences carry meaning without effort; finally, you begin to think in the language. Each new level is a small jump out of the system. That, perhaps, is the best tribute to GEB a language learner can pay.
paras.uz: Va nihoyat, o'zingiz bilan olib ketadigan fikr. Bu kitob davomida siz Hofstadter tasvirlagan narsani qildingiz: belgilarni — inglizcha so'zlarni, o'zbekcha so'zlarni, formulalarni — o'qidingiz va ulardan yuqoriroq darajada ma'no qurdingiz. Yangi til o'rganishning o'zi tavsif darajalari haqidagi saboq: avvaliga harflar va grammatika qoidalarini ko'rasiz; keyinroq butun jumlalar zo'riqishsiz ma'no tashiydi; nihoyat, o'sha tilda fikrlay boshlaysiz. Har bir yangi daraja — tizimdan kichik sakrab chiqish. Bu, ehtimol, til o'rganuvchi GEB ga bildira oladigan eng yaxshi hurmat.

paras.en: Scene — Achilles: Tortoise, we've reached the end of the book. Tortoise: Have we? Listen — the musicians are playing the King's theme again. Achilles: That's the theme from the very beginning! Tortoise: Of course. Every good canon returns to its home key. Achilles: So the end is the beginning? Tortoise: The end is the beginning, one level higher. You are not the same Achilles who opened the book. Achilles: Then shall we start again? Tortoise: Shall we? Crab: Somebody please pass the cake before the next modulation.
paras.uz: Sahna — Axilles: Toshbaqa, biz kitobning oxiriga yetdik. Toshbaqa: Yetdikmi? Quloq sol — musiqachilar yana Qirol mavzusini chalishyapti. Axilles: Bu eng boshidagi mavzu-ku! Toshbaqa: Albatta. Har bir yaxshi kanon o'z uy tonalligiga qaytadi. Axilles: Demak, oxir — boshlanishmi? Toshbaqa: Oxir — boshlanish, bir daraja yuqoriroqda. Sen kitobni ochgan Axilles emassan. Axilles: Unda yana boshlaymizmi? Toshbaqa: Boshlaymizmi? Qisqichbaqa: Kimdir iltimos, keyingi modulyatsiyadan oldin tortni uzatib yuborsin.

chapters.recap_uz: Kitob «Olti ovozli rikerkar» dialogi bilan tugaydi: unda barcha qahramonlar yig'iladi va suhbat Baxning «Musiqiy tortiq»iga — kitob boshlangan joyga — qaytadi. Bu WordDrop yakuniy so'zida kitobning merosi, keyingi «Men — g'alati halqa» (2007) kitobi, tanqidlar va kitobni qanday qayta o'qish haqida gap boradi.
chapters.note_uz: Kitob o'z boshiga qaytadi — xuddi Baxning cheksiz ko'tariluvchi kanoni kabi. Bu ham g'alati halqa: tugash — yangi boshlanish.
